pr:311.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes GitHub issue [#310](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/310).

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

pr:315.body:
# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

ScienceDiscovery's issue, review and CI queues need explicit handoffs: the next actor, the missing evidence and the condition that permits progress. This proposal adds an operator-invoked development-loop skill and guide, linked from CONTRIBUTING.

## What changes

- Three queues: issue implementation, PR review, and CI/acceptance.
- Seven decision points: requirement claim, design/dependencies, implementation, source review, CI repair, real acceptance and release sign-off.
- Role-separated contributor/reviewer/maintainer TODOs, verified versus suggested ownership, release impact and recheck triggers.
- Exact-head review history, current readiness refreshes, pagination/error coverage and duplicate-request prevention.
- ScienceDiscovery's PR L1/L2, merge-group L3, daily L4 and release L5 stay distinct. Fix commits first reuse the automatic synchronize run; pending runs do not invite duplicate reruns.

Related: release tracker #249 and source-review skill proposal #231. This complements source review and does not adopt an unmerged proposal as trusted policy. Magpie is credited for unified agent/model routing and instruction-library inspiration; this is not represented as an imported upstream PR-loop skill.

## Scope and rollout

Documentation and agent instructions only. No scheduler, workflow, paid research, credentials or repository settings are installed or changed. Maintainers must separately approve deployment cadence, quotas, notifications and write actions. Keep this PR draft until the proposed handoffs and rollout choices are reviewed.

## Validation

- Independent read-only review: four manual scenarios checked (new head/new CI attempt, changed state before publication, incomplete screenshot evidence, PR versus merge-group gates); no blocking findings. These are reasoning checks, not an executed scheduler or production effectiveness measurement.
- Base inspected: `cc974a14468cbdfd66c76f2720ebd751aefb1cdd`.
- Full application UT/ST/E2E and live-model journeys have not been executed. No product/runtime files changed. CI policy tests establish routing invariants, not product or scientific correctness.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable to the product: this change adds contributor/agent workflow documentation with no user-observable runtime path. The eight dry-run acceptance scenarios describe checks required before future automation deployment; they do not claim that a loop has been deployed or tested end to end.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: developer-facing review and queue coordination guidance.

pr:372.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

![Connector picker after the biomed server is turned off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dbf29ea-549c-49c7-b1b2-4aab3e220d86)

![Connector picker when enabled servers fail to connect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a977f904-fd31-4182-8cef-5656492cd825)

![The same failure text at a narrow width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/388977e4-55bc-42b8-9d6d-961c87f31353)

![A disabled MCP server remains on the settings page with its switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbe9e5a5-f828-4b17-a4e7-0198f386283e)

pr:390.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

Compatibility and migration: none for application users. SDK dependencies are isolated in the skill's optional host package. Existing private pipeline state is neither imported nor modified.

## Follow-up: Issue-as-Interface + OSS ops skills

Added on top of `repo-issue-pipeline` (commit `01f1df6`):

- **IAI delivery:** `issue-as-interface-contract`, `issue-review-agent-ready`, `iai-developer-patrol`, `iai-worker-implement`, `iai-reviewer-patrol`, `iai-reviewer-execute`, `magpie-pr-review-pipeline`
- **OSS ops (parallel):** `oss-ops-newcomer-gfi`, `oss-ops-stale-sweep`, `oss-ops-maintainer-stats`, `oss-ops-repo-health`
- **Docs:** [zh](docs/zh/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) / [en](docs/en/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) (+ links from CONTRIBUTING and issue-pipeline pages)

Still opt-in documentation/skills only — installing does not start bots. Reviewer execute authority is skill text for hosts that enable it; this PR does not merge or change CI policy.

pr:408.body:
Closes #309.

The artifact viewer was a small card — 1080×758 inside a 1920×1080 window — with a 560px preview inside it, so a report, a table or a plot was read through three nested scrollbars. It is now a large-screen content window whose content actually fills it.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css` | `.artifact-modal-panel` → `width: min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`, `height: min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`. `.artifact-modal-body` gets `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` (it owns the leftover height and the scroll), header and mode tabs are pinned with `flex: 0 0 auto`. Markdown prose keeps a readable measure: `.markdown-body > :is(p, ul, ol, dl, blockquote) { max-width: 76ch }`. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/artifacts.css` | Inside `.artifact-modal-panel .artifact-modal-body` only: `max-height: none` for `.manuscript-preview`, `.artifact-source-preview`, `.dataset-table-wrapper`, `.notebook-cells`, and `.annotatable-figure img { max-height: min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px)) }`. Inline and timeline previews share those classes and keep their 560/460/420px caps. `.manuscript-preview pre` (fenced code blocks inside a report) deliberately keeps its 460px cap so a huge source file cannot stretch the panel into one endless column. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/memory-graph.css` | Stale comment on `.evidence-title` that still described the old fixed viewer size. |
| `apps/web/tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx` | The #309 test now asserts the panel size, the 76ch measure, the body flex rule, the pinned header/tabs and the whole in-modal override block — plus counter-assertions that the base 560px / 460px caps survive. |

Review follow-up (HongyeZhou, `38a46e01`) is included: the taller window alone added blank space, so the rest of this PR is about making the content use it.

## Verification (specific to this change)

Measured on the **real `ArtifactModal` component** built from this branch with the repo's Vite config, served at a 1920×1063 viewport (the 1600×960 window), in headless Chromium:

| | Panel | `.artifact-modal-body` | Preview | Scrollbars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 614px tall, flex `0 1 auto`, ends 206px above the panel bottom | `.manuscript-preview` 560px, capped at 560px, scrolls inside itself | 2 (preview + body) |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), source file | 1600×960 | 534px tall, ends 286px above the bottom | `.artifact-source-preview` 460px, self-scrolling | 2 |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 818px tall, flex `1 1 auto`, bottom edge at 1011 vs panel bottom 1012 | 8865px tall, `max-height: none`, does not self-scroll | 1 (body) |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), source file | 1600×960 | 818px tall, same 1px gap | 15697px tall, `max-height: none` | 1 (body) |

Also measured after the change: `.annotatable-figure img` → `min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px))` = 753px at this viewport; fenced `pre` inside a report still 460px; and in a non-modal container the computed caps are still 560px (`.manuscript-preview`), 460px (source / table / notebook) and 420px (figure image), so inline and timeline previews are unchanged. Smaller windows behave as before: 1280×800 → panel 1200×633 with the same fill (body 491px, bottom 1px above the panel edge); `<=900px` still goes full screen.

### Screenshots (real component, 1600×960 window)

Long markdown report — top of the document:

![markdown preview, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-md-top.png)

The same report scrolled to the bottom: the document runs to the panel's bottom edge, no empty band:

## Tests

- `apps/web`: `pnpm test` — 972/972 pass; `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
- CI: see the checks on `38a46e01` (L1 static checks, L2 mocked E2E slices, code check).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **What is not verified here:** the full app with a real backend, runner and artifact store — this environment cannot start the sandboxed E2E stack (no bubblewrap, no root). The screenshots and numbers above are the real component and the real stylesheets, but a human should still open one real long artifact, a wide table and a notebook at 1920 and confirm it looks right. Flagging this explicitly rather than calling the PR visually verified.
- `.manuscript-preview pre` keeps its 460px cap on purpose (see the table above). Say if you would rather have it lifted too.

pr:441.body:
Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. The final commit only relocates the unchanged connector-persistence test to avoid an append-at-end conflict with current main; production code and other tests are identical to the product-validation candidate.
The requester explicitly waived baseline reproduction for this feature. The baseline capability/gap assessment was source inspection, not a baseline live-service result. The candidate journeys below used built production API/Runner entry points, the bundled stdio MCP server, isolated Session/data state and official live providers. Agent validation used the native executor and a deterministic local model stub; it does not certify JiuwenSwarm or real-model behavior.

| Acceptance area | Candidate evidence | Status / remaining limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five sources discoverable, enabled and callable | Production sources API, saved Session selections, five live Inspector calls; browser Inspector journey | PASS for representative paths; Agent tool execution exercised with AlphaFold, not every source |
| GEO metadata/files/verified matrix | GSE1000, sample annotations and actual directory listing; completed matrix download, SHA-256 and parsed 22,283 probe rows × 10 samples | PASS; identify expression profiling by array and avoid assuming raw counts |
| ChEMBL constrained measurements/pagination | CHEMBL203 activity query, two distinct provider pages, units/relations/assay metadata/confidence retained | PASS for representative query |

pr:470.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head
`4bf3ff891beb4ff0c8e9bf2776dc5882e28a551f` is a merge of `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928` and `origin/main` `f4ceca57b74b7f5a10b4f8f77313513a09886c02`. The merge tree matches a clean merge. No conflict was resolved by hand. `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`, and the CLA steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are unchanged from `3bde9d39`. The CLA paragraph in `.ci/README.md` is unchanged; other README edits came in from `main`.

GitHub Actions run [40210190231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40210190231) completed with conclusion `success` on this head:
- UT: planned 4853, executed 4853, passed 4853, failed 0, skipped 0.
- ST: planned 24, executed 24, passed 24, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Mocked E2E, four shards combined: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118.
- Coverage and merge-gate succeeded. L3, L4/L5, Docker, and the binary release were skipped by policy.
- `Require CLA policy` ran. This pull request's own `license/cla` status was `success`, so the bot exemption was not the path that made the gate pass.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`, before the merge:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They are not the result for the current head.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5, skipped 0. All five failures were in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` and matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked): planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. The spec matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.

The GitHub run above is the result for `4bf3ff89`. The earlier local UT failure in `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` did not fail this run.

## E2E user journeys
PASS on the current head for the mocked shards in run 40210190231: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118. Real-model journeys were not run. This change does not alter product UI.

The earlier local mocked run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d` failed one pre-existing layout assertion: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. Counts for that older run: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

## Release

User impact: none in the product. Only `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` can merge when `license/cla` is present and not success. Other bots and human authors stay blocked in that case. A CLA check that never appears does not block anyone.

Compatibility and migration: none. `license/cla` stays off the required status checks on purpose. This workflow change needs a human review; merge-when-ready is not enabled.

pr:498.body:
Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and the scientific memory graph.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy with the imported conversation and evidence. New research preserves the original snapshot. The compact continuation action appears beside the composer notice; the copy-origin notice disappears after 10 seconds.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies; complete exports include broader history and trajectory details. File selections, export profiles, counts, and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- User messages have a copy action; the existing assistant copy action is retained. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply, including after restart and for branches of branches.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence and discloses unavailable history; it never replaces a missing historical file with a later version. Busy sessions are rejected, request retries are idempotent, and imported snapshots remain protected.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the local graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration.

## Validation

Tested commit: `4e198ebe9ea9161d826827af816df59a09d02fb1`, based on official `main` at `9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`. Exactly one feature commit; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Targeted feature regressions: 50 Node tests passed (21 package/API/import/branch cases and 29 UI-control/trajectory cases), plus 2 scientific-memory Python tests passed. These are targeted results, not a passing full UT layer.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: failed during Node collection with `NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED` after the collector's 120,000 ms timeout; no plan was produced and no tests executed. The same full-layer command on pristine official `main` failed at the same collection timeout.
- `pnpm ci:st`: 24 planned, 24 executed, 17 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped. Pristine official `main` has the same counts and the same seven failed planned identities: five specialist-runtime/ACP cases, the Evolve Python-runtime download reaching the worker timeout, and the Swarm SDK contract command. Nested SDK results differ: the candidate reports 26 failed / 53 passed / 1 teardown error, while main reports 25 failed / 54 passed; both also report 20 passed subtests. The candidate has an additional timeout in `test_http_disconnect_propagates_cancellation_to_adapter`; this runtime validation difference remains unresolved. The SDK check completed normally before the local wait limit; it was not reported as a pass or skipped.
- No test assertions were weakened or cases skipped to obtain a passing result. Runtime failures and browser coverage gaps remain open; this PR stays Draft.

## E2E user journeys

**FAIL / incomplete coverage**, on the tested commit above, using the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend and local mocked models. `pnpm ci:e2e` reports 103 planned, 9 reported/executed, 7 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped; 94 identities were not run. One of the two reported failures is an interrupted case, not a completed assertion failure.

Command: `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/runtime pnpm ci:e2e`, after dependencies, full build, bubblewrap, and the pinned Chromium were prepared in an isolated detached worktree.

| Batch | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research, 20 planned | Healthy isolated stack, then research journeys | BLOCKED before browser execution: scientific memory did not become healthy within the startup script's 10-second wait. |
| Standard, 77 planned | Healthy gateway, valid serialized ordering, then UI journeys | Reporter raised `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST`; the gateway also timed out during WebSocket opening handshake. Network guard passed, the first inline-card case failed, and the unhealthy run was manually interrupted: 1 passed / 1 failed / 1 interrupted / 74 not run. The tagged summary counts the interruption as FAIL. Supplemental Swarm `history` recorded FAIL; remaining supplemental checks were stopped. |
| Literature, 6 planned | Offline literature-source contracts complete through the local product stack | 6 executed, 6 passed. |

The changed user goals are importing and inspecting evidence, continuing a snapshot in a writable session, previewing/downloading workspace files, inspecting trajectory/export scopes, copying a user message, and branching from a reply with navigation back to its source. Expected outcomes are persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable branches, and return to the source reply. pr:524.body:
设置 was a modal with two tabs and a back/forward history, and most of the
service's own configuration had no surface at all: custom MCP servers, experts,
timeouts and the proxy policy could only be changed in the configuration file.
This layer replaces the dialog with the handoff's full-height settings surface
and fills the panes it needs.

**Stack:** part 3 of 5, built on #523. The next layer is #525.
Compare this layer against the layer below: https://github.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/compare/pr/08-workspace-panel...pr/09-settings

## The surface

`SystemSettingsDialog` is a grouped directory — 系统, 智能, 连接, 工作区 — with
eight panes: 通用, 模型, 技能, MCP 服务器, 专家, 网络, 远程, 超时. It opens over
the task surface, remembers the pane it last showed, and has a footer of 取消并
关闭, 保存 and 保存并关闭. Pages that save immediately say so (这一页的改动即时
保存) instead of showing a save button that would do nothing.

The rail and the composer both open it, and both name the pane they mean —
the model pill's 添加模型 leads to 模型, and 专家 leads to 专家 — instead of
dropping the reader on 通用.

## 模型

One row per profile with its connection test (可用 / the failure message and
latency), 设为主模型, and a delete button drawn but disabled with the reason:
there is no delete route. There is no per-profile edit either — the row does
not offer one, because changing a provider's key is the 添加模型 form with the
same endpoint, which is a different job from editing one row. The add form
lives in a modal and reuses the provider whose base URL it already knows, so a
second visit updates that provider rather than leaving two rows with the key on
one of them.

## MCP 服务器, 专家, 超时

`McpServers` edits custom servers over both transports: command, arguments,
working directory and environment pairs for stdio; URL, headers and an auth
mode (headers or OAuth with client metadata) for HTTP. Secrets are write-only —
a saved value shows 已保存，留空沿用 and is never read back. Test, enable/disable
and delete each report what the server said.

`Specialists` edits the reusable instruction-and-tool sets: name, description,
instructions, runtime (原生 or the external command-line agent), model,
connectors and skills, with delete behind a confirmation that says what stops
working.

`Timeouts` sets the five wall-clock limits, each with an 不限 switch, so a run
that legitimately takes hours is a setting rather than a workaround.

The API surface for these — connectors, global settings, proxy, MCP, web,
memory, IdeaTree and specialists — joins `api/settings.ts` and `api/types.ts`.

pr:528.body:
The single-PR skill covers one change end to end, but this project proposes
larger changes as a stack of layers, and the rules that make a stack work were
spread across the session that built one. This adds them as a skill so the next
stack starts from the same procedure.

**Independent of the other pull requests in this batch.**

## What the skill covers

- The shape: one branch per layer cut from the layer below, one capability per
  layer, and no layer referencing a symbol that only exists above it.
- The body's stack section, so a reviewer knows which diff to read and in what
  order the pull requests merge.
- Rebase-merge rather than squash, because a squash collapses two layers into
  one commit and the next branch loses the parent it was built on.
- The push-through-the-Git-Data-API path for when `github.com` is unreachable
  for git transport, including the check that every server-side blob, tree and
  commit SHA matches the local one.
- What to do after a lower layer merges: reconstruct the rewritten commit,
  rebase the next layer onto it, verify the diff is still the layer's own, and
  push again.
- Review threads on lower layers: out of scope for the upper pull request, and
  answered rather than quietly resolved.

The single-PR skill gains a link to it.

pr:544.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

pr:548.body:
Nightly real-model E2E treated a single transient model-gateway HTTP 500/503 the same as a product run that finished and failed to deliver, so one provider outage failed the whole Daily gate while other cases in the same job still passed. This change keeps the provider error visible, soft-classifies those faults, optionally repeats an early fault once, and leaves product failures hard-failing.

**The required real-E2E check now has a floor: a planned case that only faulted is an unverified case, and the check does not pass on it.** A soft classification is not a soft green.

After the optional early repeat, a case that passes on the repeat is a genuine `PASS` and the check may go green; a case that still faults keeps the `PROVIDER_FAULT` status and makes the check non-pass.

Closes #232

## The gate floor

| Outcome | Status | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every planned case passed | `PASS` | 0 |
| A provider fault remains, no product failure | `PROVIDER_FAULT` | non-zero |
| A product failure | `FAIL` | non-zero |

The two failure kinds stay apart: a provider fault is still reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT: <case>` and never as `FAIL: <case>`, and a product failure is never softened into an outage. Neither one is a pass. The floor is the same in every place that decides, for the daily, merge L3 and release L5 profiles alike — no profile can turn an outage into a green required check:

- **`verifyResults`** (`test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`): the exit code is 1 whenever a provider fault or a product problem remains; the status is `PROVIDER_FAULT` for a fault, `FAIL` for a product failure, `PASS` only for a run without either.
- **the worker** (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`): a repeat that did not work is audited in the accounting (`PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_FAILED`, `PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_REPORT_MISSING`) instead of only in the log; a batch that faulted as a whole is probed with a couple of repeats instead of re-running every case; a worker whose only failures were provider faults is not double-counted as an opaque worker failure, and the summary's exit code is 1 while a fault remains.
- **the suite reconcile** (`.ci/real-report.mjs`): a provider-fault shard is valid evidence — the identity checks still apply — whose results are folded into the suite accounting; the suite's exit code comes from that accounting, so a remaining fault makes it non-zero. The provider-fault problems stay visible instead of being flattened into an opaque `SHARD_FAILED`, and a shard cannot hide a fault behind a `PASS` it did not earn.
- **the shared-plan summary** (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`): a provider fault is a problem of its own, `planned == executed == passed` is still required, and `passed + provider faults == planned` is no longer enough for green.

## The detector

The provider context has to name the gateway itself: its `181001` model-call code, the wording of a failed model call, the API it answers on, or its own routing failure. Bare words — "provider", "llm", "gateway", "upstream" — are not context: a product delivery failure that mentions one beside a `500` is the product's own failure and stays a `FAIL`. A delivery miss or an assertion diff is the product's own report in the first place and is never soft-classified.

The gateway's own report is unchanged: the `181001` model-call code, the openAI API stream error and the routing failures recorded in the Nightly of 2026-10-06 are still detected as provider faults, and the provider's text is still kept verbatim.

## What changed
- `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`: the tightened provider context, the product-report reject, and the audit codes a failed repeat leaves behind.
- `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`: the exit-code floor in `verifyResults`; the status of a provider fault stays `PROVIDER_FAULT`.
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`: the audited repeat, the capped outage probe, and the worker-failure pairing with the attempt whose exit code it explains.
- `.ci/real-report.mjs`: the reconcile keeps a provider-fault shard's evidence and the suite's exit code follows the accounting.
- `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`: a provider fault is a problem of its own.
- Docs in `.ci/README.md` and `test/support/tagged/README.md`.
- Tests in `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.

Product agent loop, model client, and run orchestration are untouched: only the CI harness and its accounting changed.

pr:550.body:
A delegated child used to surface as the raw `task` tool card: an argument blob with no account of what the child actually did. This folds the child's own events into the transcript and gives the right panel a mode for reading them.

This branch was stacked on #549 (`feat/desktop-welcome-page`), which has since merged. It is now rebased onto `main`; the two commits under review are `fb412694` and `d9c15425`.

## One line inside the run fold

Each child is one line where the delegation tool would have been, reading `Subagent <task>`. It sits inside the folded run, beside the tool calls it replaces, and is a button rather than a card. The line is named by what the child was asked to do: no persona, no avatar, no team tab and no "currently active" box.

The delegation tools (`task`, `subagent_*`) are hidden while their child snapshot exists, because the line already says what they said. A `task` call with no snapshot is still drawn — pruned or older event logs would otherwise leave the turn with no account of the delegation at all.

## The panel shows the child, not the roster

Pressing the line swaps the panel's 产物/工作区 groups for that child. 任务 and 执行详情 are cards that start closed, so the panel opens on the child's answer rather than on a screen of steps; 输出 stays open. Pressing the same line again leaves the mode — the panel has no back arrow of its own, so the transcript line is the way back.

Inside that mode, system bookkeeping steps (turn markers, brief revisions) are dropped, a reply is prose in the timeline rather than a fold of its own, and a tool's result sits in a named output box beside its input.

输出 is only for a completed child: there is a deliverable to name. What a running or timed-out child last said is a progress note it was interrupted in the middle of, so it stays in the timeline instead of being presented as a result. A failed child's reason sits under the execution card, where it explains how the child ran. There is no status row in the panel — the transcript's line already carries the status, the turn count and the error.

## Steps that a replayed run does not carry

The run's event log persists `subagent.updated` snapshots without their steps: the steps live on the child's own substream, which a run replay does not read. A reopened finished run would therefore have shown an empty panel. The panel reads the session's subagent catalog (`GET /api/sessions/:id/subagents`) when the snapshot carries no steps, and reads it again when the open child reaches a terminal status, so the last steps are not lost.

When a parent agent first called `task` with parseable JSON that omitted the required `prompt` (specialist delegation), the call reached `createSubagent`, threw, and showed a raw failed tool card for a call that was never executable. The model then self-repaired. This partial fix handles that miss before a failed card is the durable outcome, while keeping `prompt` required in the schema (`description` never substitutes for it).

Related to #335
Refs #335

**Partial fix; keep #335 open.** Do not close the issue: lmfit/`conf_interval`, Scenario 1 soft failures, and the general 失败卡→正在重试 narrative remain deferred.

- JiuwenSwarm model gateway withholds calls missing `lifecycle.requiredArguments[name]` the same way it withholds unparseable JSON; the agent wires `requiredArgumentsOf(registry.values())` into `startModelGateway`.

pr:552.body:
Issue #305 asks for a workspace where a conversation does not need a Project before it can start. The desktop app used to invent a Project on launch (我的工作区) and stack every Session under it, so a first-run workspace could not tell a Project from a conversation. This change gives standalone conversations a real home on the server, and gives the column two lists that say what a Session belongs to.

## A hidden inbox Project on the server

`Project` gains an optional `kind: "inbox"`. `ensureInboxProject()` creates the single inbox idempotently inside the settings mutation queue, with the full default settings a Project needs (runner allowlist, overrides), and writes it in one `saveCatalog` so a concurrent reader never sees it without its mark. `POST /api/inbox` hands out its id; `GET /api/projects` lists the user's Projects only. The inbox cannot be renamed or deleted (`409`), but its runner allowlist stays editable, so 设置 › 远程 works for a standalone conversation like for any other.

Internal sweeps keep using `listProjects()`: run recovery, runner bindings, usage summaries, the workbench search guard and skills' deletion impact still see the inbox. Hiding it from navigation must not hide it from accounting. The workbench search skips it explicitly, so `GET /api/workbench/search` does not offer an inbox conversation to the web app, which has no navigation for it.

## The column: 项目, then 最近会话

`Sidebar` now draws every Project the user made as a fold with its own `+` (a Session inside that Project), and 最近会话 below them for the inbox's Sessions. States are per fold (`folded`/`expanded` sets), so one long list no longer unfolds another. 新建项目 asks for a name alone, and opens the Session the server creates with the Project so a new Project is not left holding an untitled row nobody asked for.

`activeProject` is derived from the open Session's own record, not from state written once at launch: switching, renaming and a language change all reach it without a second copy to keep in step. The inbox is never printed under its stored name (`Recent sessions`); the interface uses its own word.

## The welcome page's project picker

The strip under the landing composer was a label; it is now a button. It opens a menu of the user's Projects with a check on the current one, 新建项目, and 不在任何项目中 — the last one means the next conversation appears under 最近会话. With no Project chosen the chip shows 选择项目 in the placeholder grey and stays flat until it is hovered or open. Choosing a Project here creates nothing: the picker corrects where the next message goes, and the first send writes the Session there.

`selectProject` and `newSession` write `projectRef` before setting state, because the next send and `createOpenSession` read the ref, not the state that lands a render later.

## 新建会话 reuses the untouched page

A Session keeps the service's `Untitled session` sentinel until its first run renames it, so the sentinel is a durable "never written in" mark that survives a restart. `reusableDraft` finds the newest such Session in the target Project and 新建会话 opens it instead of writing another row the user cannot tell apart. `sessionCreation` is keyed by Project and token-gated, so a `+` in one Project and a `+` in another are two Sessions, and a late creation for a Project the user left does not clear a newer one.

## One name for an unnamed Session

`sessionTitle` moved from `views` to `app` so `use-workspace` can use it too. The sidebar row, the session bar, the rename field and the delete confirmation all print 未命名会话 / Untitled session for the sentinel. Confirming a rename field unchanged is a no-op in both places; otherwise the phrase would be stored as the title and silently disable the reuse above. The session bar drops the 最近会话 crumb for a standalone Session: that is the column's word for the list, not a place.

## Overlays that were painted under the page

`PromptDialog` and `RowMenu` now portal to `document.body`. The sidebar is a sticky column, which makes it a stacking context, and the landing hero's entrance animation leaves `transform: translateY(0)` behind, which makes it a containing block for `position: fixed`. A dialog opened from a Project row was painted under the composer and the hero; the row menu measured from the wrong origin. Both render in a portal, with an SSR fallback for the component tests.

## Stack

#549 and #550 have both merged, so this pull request is now a single commit on `main` and nothing has to land before it.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — 298 passed, 0 failed
- `pnpm ci:ut` — planned 4865, executed 4836, passed 4832, failed 4:

pr:562.body:
The right panel listed the open Session's output and nothing else, one row per version rather than per artifact, in a fixed 240px list beside a fixed document column. Work from an earlier Session disappeared as soon as the next one started, a rewritten file appeared twice, clicking the same row twice opened a second tab, and neither column could be closed.

The branch it was stacked on — #552, which carried #550 and #549 — has merged, so the branch now sits directly on `main` and this pull request is only its own work: `8df530ff`, plus `b4e0a315` for the two review findings (the version race in `openPreview`, and the list width the panel renders) and `9e2abcbe` for two more (the version picker's name, and where focus goes after a pick). 20 files, all in `apps/desktop`.

## Every Session's artifacts, the open one first

The list is built from every Session the app knows about, read once per Session and cached; the open Session is still re-read after each run and upload, and a Session that leaves the list takes its cached rows with it. `artifact-groups` puts each artifact under the Session that created it — a later Session can rewrite the file, but the heading stays where it came from — with the open Session pinned first and the rest in sidebar order.

A group whose Session has been deleted keeps its rows under the title recorded at creation: hiding a readable file because its heading lost its page would be the wrong trade, and the artifact outlives the Session in the project-scoped store.

## One row per artifact, its versions behind it

`artifact-labels` folds the versions of an artifact into its newest row. The picker beside the document reaches the other versions, and each version is read through the Session that wrote it, which is why a document request now carries a Session as well as an artifact. Clicking a row that is already open focuses its tab instead of reading it again, and a failed read is refilled rather than duplicated. Two artifacts that share a name get their folder as a second fact on the row.

The open Session's group starts open; the others start folded and are one click away, and a search opens every group it reaches. Group headings are the same weight whether or not they are pinned, so the list can be scanned by Session name rather than by emphasis.

## The list and the document

The divider between the columns belongs to the reader: drag it and the list takes the width, past its own end it snaps closed and the document gets the panel. A closed column leaves no hairline but keeps a 26px band along its edge, and a click there restores the default split. `panel-split` holds the arithmetic, `use-panel-split` the pointer handling, and both are covered as pure functions.

## Reading

A `.txt` is set as a page — the document's own type, no box, no second scrollbar — while logs and source keep the monospaced listing where columns line up. The document column's empty state says 还没有打开产物 — 还没有打开文件 in 工作区 — rather than claiming the Session has none, which is a different question from the one the list answers. Both lists get a search; the file tree keeps the folders above a match and drops folders that lead nowhere.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: pass.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: 380 passed, 0 failed (run on `9e2abcbe`, two new tests for the version gate).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`: pass.
- `pnpm ci:ut` (run at `09d9090b`, before the branch was rebased onto #552): 4926 planned, 4926 executed, 4921 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped. The branch's diff against its merge base with `main` (`65eddde1`) touches only `apps/desktop`, so every failing file below is byte-identical to `main`:
  - `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` — clones `deep_research_bench` from `github.com`; the TLS connection is refused before any test body runs.
  - `check:research-python-ut` — same clone, same `GnuTLS recv error (-110)`.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — `bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`; this host has bubblewrap 0.6.1, which predates that flag.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — the title call records no `context.captured` event; fails identically when run alone, outside the layer.
  - `services/api/src/server.test.ts` — a queued run does not start within the timeout under the layer's parallel load.
- `pnpm ci:st` (same commit): 24 planned, 24 executed, 22 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped.
  - `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` — downloads a pinned Python runtime from `github.com`, which this host cannot reach.
  - `check:swarm-sdk-contract` — `test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once` times out (78 other tests in that suite pass); the same case failed the same way on the parent branch.
- GitHub Actions, run `40512622373` on `9e2abcbe` (ready for review, whole matrix): Select CI policy, L1, ST, Coverage and all five L2 mocked E2E shards pass — standard-journeys, standard-config, governed, research, literature. `UT` failed with 4972 of 4973 cases passing; the one failure is `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts` "Shell background mode…", which asserts `wait:job:5` against an implementation that computes `deadline - Date.now()` (`workspace.ts:1506,1511`) and yields 4 whenever a clock tick falls between the two reads — a pre-existing timing race in a file this branch does not touch. `merge-gate` failed only because UT did. The earlier run `40508972752` on `b4e0a315` was green in every job but `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)`, whose red case is the web `journey-compact-process` Skill entry, and run `40320408506` on the pre-rebase head `09d9090b` was green in every job that ran. The host-only failures listed above do not reproduce in CI.

## E2E user journeys

Status: PASS for the changed app; the mocked browser suite failed 3 of 119, all outside `apps/desktop`.

- Tested commit: `09d9090b` for the mocked suite and the hand-driven run; the desktop package's tests were re-run at the current head `9e2abcbe` (380 passed).
- Browser (mocked, Playwright), `CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/ci-results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/ci-runtime pnpm ci:e2e`: 119 planned, 119 executed, 116 passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped. The suite serves `apps/web`; this branch touches no `apps/web` or `services` file.
  - `journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen.spec.ts` J309 — "a paragraph keeps a readable measure instead of spanning the window": a web viewer geometry assertion, not reachable from this diff.
  - `journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts` — the web settings pane's submit box overlaps its footer; `apps/web` selectors only.
  - `journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` — BLOCKED: `managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`, this host has no download access.
- Desktop app (local Vite dev server, API mocked in the browser), hand-driven Playwright script:
  - Two Sessions, one artifact created and written now, one created last week and rewritten now, one written only last week → the open Session's group is pinned first and expanded, the other is folded: PASS (`▸ 正在写的会话 当前会话` above `▸ 上周的会话`, one row visible).
  - Fold the open group, search for a name behind the fold, clear the search → the search opens both groups and the fold returns afterwards: PASS.
  - Open the row from the other Session → the document reads `sOld:v3` through `/api/sessions/sOld/artifact-versions/v3/content`: PASS.
  - Open the rewritten artifact and pick its earlier version → the picker offers `v2, v1` and choosing `v1` reads `/api/sessions/sOld/artifact-versions/v1/content`: PASS.
- API / CLI: no API or CLI behaviour changed.
- Coverage gap: the repository's mocked E2E suite has no desktop journeys, so this panel has no automated browser coverage in CI yet; the hand-driven run above is the evidence.


## Release

Release category: release:feature (the `release:feature` label could not be applied by the contributor account; a maintainer needs to add it)
User impact: artifacts from every Session are listed with the open one's group first and foldable; one row per artifact with a version picker; the list and document columns resize and collapse; `.txt` previews read as prose; both lists search.
Compatibility and migration: none. No stored data, API or configuration change.
