closed_recent.body:
## Problem

The local ScienceMemory backend can exhaust memory while building the folded session subgraph. A variable-length `next*0..` traversal enumerates paths across historical sessions before the requested session is filtered, and the interpreter materializes the intermediate rows before deduplication. A small stored graph can consequently require enormous query memory.

This remains reproducible on `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `7a1f0e37`. The relevant `query.py`, `_cypher.py`, and `local_backend.py` files have no diff from the historical incident checkout `d54cfc2d`.

## Historical incident and confidence boundary

During TC-E2E-01 on September 24, 2026:

- The startup log identifies PID 104627 as the memory-graph Python service, listening on port 17876.
- The contemporaneous incident record reports an OOM kill at 04:02:31 Asia/Shanghai, with anonymous RSS of 113,370,408 KiB (approximately 108.1 GiB) for that PID.
- The test stack was interrupted; TC-E2E-01 did not complete, and the next queued DRB-75 case was not started.

The original kernel entry is no longer available in the current journal/dmesg; the RSS figure comes from the retained incident record. There is no Python stack or heap profile from the instant of that OOM. The reproduction below establishes a current, concrete failure mechanism on retained data, but does not prove which exact request was executing at the historical OOM instant.

This is separate from the Node API trajectory/versioning memory problems observed with ScienceMemory disabled.

## Read-only reproduction on retained real graph data

The retained local store contains 4,520 nodes and 5,854 edges. The requested incident session has only **one node**.

Using current code, replay the JSONL records into a standalone in-memory `Graph`, then execute the SQL-like Cypher strings from `get_subgraph` with the incident session ID. Avoid constructing `Graph(Store(...))` directly against original evidence: loading may compact the store. Use a copy or read-only replay.

The diagnostic process was constrained to **512 MiB address space** and a **25-second alarm**. No model calls or service mutations were performed.

| Query | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Session nodes | 1 row, approximately 8 ms |
| Direct edges | 0 rows, approximately 18 ms |
| Folded surrogate-edge UNION | `MemoryError` after approximately 3.95 seconds, peak RSS approximately 502 MiB |
| Same folded query, with an early `WITH scope, first WHERE scope.session_id = $sid` before each variable-length match | 0 rows, approximately 1 ms |

The failure stack is inside `_match` / `_match_parts`. Early filtering is a diagnostic control, **not a complete fix**: querying an affected, branched session can still enumerate a huge number of paths.

## Mechanism

1. [`get_subgraph`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py#L164) builds folded surrogate edges using:

   ```cypher
   MATCH (scope:Task)-[:contains]->(first:ToolCall)
   OPTIONAL MATCH (first)-[:next*0..]->(child:ToolCall)
   MATCH (child)-[:produces]->(c:Code)-[:produces]->(art:Artifact)
   WHERE scope.session_id = $sid
   ...
   RETURN DISTINCT ...
   ```

   The same traversal shape occurs in other UNION branches. The local interpreter does not push the later session predicate before the preceding variable-length match.

2. [`_walk`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/_cypher.py#L1290) tracks used relationships per path. It enumerates relationship-simple paths rather than unique reachable endpoints. A DAG can therefore cause combinatorial growth without any cycle.

3. [`_match`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/_cypher.py#L1171) appends all matching rows to a list. Projection, DISTINCT, and output LIMIT happen later, so small final output does not bound intermediate memory.

4. The retained `next` graph has 1,677 vertices and is acyclic, but contains **41 branching nodes**: 33 mix `scope_chain` and `temporal_chain` edges, four have multiple `scope_chain` edges, and four have multiple `temporal_chain` edges. This traversal does not filter by `method`. Dynamic programming on this DAG counts **237,316,988 paths, including zero-length paths, from one scope entry**.

5. [`LocalSession`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/local_backend.py#L48) uses a shared graph store across sessions and holds a graph-wide lock for the transaction. Historical data can affect a new nearly-empty session, and an expensive query can block other graph operations.

The origin of the extra chain branches is **not yet established**. Inspect chain rebuilding and scope/temporal edge membership rather than assuming a particular write race.

## Suggested fix scope

- Filter session/scope before traversal and prevent crossing unrelated scopes or chain types.
- For folded reachability views, compute the required reachable products/`via_child` identities without enumerating every path. Do not globally replace Cypher path semantics where callers actually require distinct paths.
- Investigate and validate chain construction/rebuild invariants; cover mixed chain types and historical stores.
- Add bounded intermediate-work/memory handling and cancellation so a graph query cannot take down the scientific task stack. Output limits alone are insufficient.
- Preserve low-volume query diagnostics: query identity, duration, graph size, traversal/intermediate counts, termination reason. Do not log sensitive graph contents by default.

## Acceptance / regression coverage

- A new nearly-empty session remains cheap to query when unrelated historical sessions contain branching chains.
- A deterministic small synthetic DAG with repeated branch/rejoin structure completes a folded reachability query with bounded work, correct deduplication, and preserved `via_child` information.
- Querying an affected session itself is safe; early session filtering alone is not considered sufficient.
- Cycles, mixed scope/temporal chains, rollback, and existing subgraph behavior retain their intended semantics.
- Validation runs under a strict process memory/time cap, avoiding another host OOM.

## Retained evidence

Local experiment-host paths (not publicly accessible):

- `/root/sciencediscovery-pr171-e2e-run/status.json` and `stack.log`
- `/root/.science-agent/memory-graph/{nodes,edges}.jsonl`
- `/root/sciencediscovery-memory-graph-diagnosis/{findings.md,probe.py,original-query.log,early-filter.log}`

The counts, query shape, guarded reproduction results, and uncertainty boundaries are included above so this issue is understandable without access to those private experiment files.
closed_recent.title: Memory graph local backend: folded subgraph path explosion can exhaust host memory

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #103](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/103) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

### 🚀 Background Description

Session-level **data connectors** (PubMed, arXiv, UniProt, …) already have a consistent checkbox: the composer “Data connectors” popover, plus the connector field in session / project / global runtime settings. Unchecked connectors are hidden from the Agent.

Custom MCP and Web access do not have an equally obvious counterpart:

1. **Custom MCP**: System settings → MCP servers has a whole-server “Enable this MCP server” switch. Once a server is in the registry it also appears in the connector checkbox list (ids like `custom-…`). The list is titled “Data connectors” and mixed with built-in literature/database sources, so it is easy to miss that a custom MCP must be ticked for the **current session**. Global enable ≠ session enable; the docs say so, the UI does not make it as obvious as data sources.
2. **Web access**: `web_search` / `web_fetch` are a global base capability with **no session switch**. System settings → Web only toggles engines / fetch vendors and keys. That cannot mean “this session must not use the public web.” The model always sees both tools.

Request: like today’s data connectors, give **custom MCP** and **Web access** checkboxes that can be turned on and off. When unchecked, the Agent in that session must not use the corresponding capability.

This is not [GitCode #67](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/67) (per-tool allow/deny on a custom MCP). This issue is server-level / Web-capability enablement.

### Design Ideas

Treat “which external capabilities this session may use” with the same interaction as data connectors: checkboxes, optional project/global inheritance, tools omitted when unchecked.

Suggested behavior:

- **Custom MCP**: one checkbox per saved custom server, labeled with the user-given server name (not only `custom-` + hex). Tools are exposed only when the box is checked **and** the server is globally enabled. Unchecked or globally disabled → no tools. Reusing `enabledConnectorIds` is fine, but the UI should group “Data sources” vs “Custom MCP” so users do not think the list is literature-only.
- **Web access**: one checkbox at the same level (e.g. “Web access”) that gates `web_search` and `web_fetch`. Unchecked: those tools are absent from the schema; permission cards for them must not appear. Engine/key/proxy settings still decide **how** search/fetch work once Web is on; they do not replace this switch.
- **Surfaces**: at least the composer capability picker (same entry as connectors, or immediately beside it) and session / project / global runtime settings. Inheritance matches connectors (inherit / override).
- **Defaults** (undecided, confirm before implementation): Web stays on by default and can be turned off, vs off until explicitly checked. Custom MCP should stay off the session by default (`enabledByDefault: false` today).

Out of scope:

- per-tool MCP allowlists (#67);
- changing Web engine order or vendor list;
- re-registering Web as an MCP Source.

### Involved Public APIs

- Session / project / global runtime settings must persist Web-access enablement (new field or a stable id such as `web` beside connectors). Custom MCP may keep using `custom-…` in `enabledConnectorIds`, but APIs and docs must describe that checkbox clearly.
- Tool assembly: disabled capabilities must not enter the model-visible schema; permission and audit paths must not invoke them.
- No new public network API. CLI overrides such as `--connectors` should be able to turn Web and custom MCP on/off if they already override connectors.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Composer connector picker and `ScopedSettingsEditor` connector field: same checkbox surface;
- Custom MCP system-settings enable vs session checkbox: both gates required;
- Workspace `web_search` / `web_fetch`: gated by the session switch, not unconditional base tools;
- Permissions: `connector:web:search` and `web_fetch` host permission only when Web is enabled;
- i18n: do not use “Data connectors” as the only label for MCP and Web;
- Does not replace MCP response-size protection or the Web providers settings page.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- [ ] After adding a custom MCP, the capability list shows the **server name**; checking it lets the session Agent call its tools; unchecking removes the tools from the schema.
- [ ] A globally disabled custom MCP cannot be used from the session (session check alone is not enough).
- [ ] Unchecking Web access removes `web_search` / `web_fetch` from the tool list; checking restores them.
- [ ] Project/global inherit vs session override matches data connectors.
- [ ] Built-in data-connector checkboxes keep current behavior.

Regression:

- [ ] Existing PubMed-style connector tests / E2E;
- [ ] Existing custom MCP journeys (system enable, Inspector, session check then call);
- [ ] Web provider settings, cache, and permission cards still hold when Web is enabled.

User-journey E2E:

- Open the session capability checkboxes: data sources, custom MCP, and Web access can be toggled separately;
- With Web off, a search-like prompt cannot call `web_search` (or fails without a permission card);
- With a custom MCP checked, one tool call succeeds. Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: like the current data-source connectors, add enable/disable checkboxes for custom MCP and Web access.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Enable/disable custom MCP and Web access with the same checkboxes as data connectors

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Reasoning/thinking effort selection **already exists** for interactive conversations, and it is well built. This issue is about the two places it is still missing: **the command line**, and **per-role agents**.

## What already works (so this is not a request to build it)

- **Composer control.** `apps/web/src/composer/ModelPicker.tsx` renders a combined thinking control whose options are `off` / `auto` / `on` / `effort:<level>`, driven by `thinkingChoiceOptions()` in `modelThinking.ts`, labelled "Thinking effort for this conversation".
- **First-class scoped settings.** `thinkingEffort` and `thinkingMode` are `RuntimeSettingsField`s alongside `modelId`, resolved across `global` → `project` → `session` (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
- **Provider-declared stops.** A manually configured endpoint can state the effort levels it actually accepts (`providers.manual.efforts`, "low,high,max"), and those values are sent raw, never translated.
- **Per-variant mapping,** with honest per-variant hints: DeepSeek's thinking switch plus effort, Kimi K3's `low|high|max` `reasoning_effort`, Gemini's OpenAI-compatibility field, OpenAI Responses reasoning items, Anthropic adaptive effort versus the legacy fixed budget, and Qwen/MiniMax which have no effort field at all.
- **Graceful degradation.** When a variant has no thinking control field, the setting is not saved and the UI says why, instead of pretending it applied.

That is a good design. The gaps below are about reach, not about the mechanism.

## Gap 1 — the CLI cannot set it

`ScienceDiscovery run` overrides plenty per invocation: `--model`, `--skills`, `--connectors`, `--approval`, `--review`, `--session`, `--project`. There is **no `--effort` and no `--thinking`**, even though `thinkingEffort` / `thinkingMode` sit beside `modelId` in `RuntimeSettingsOverrides`.

Consequences:

- A scripted or batch run gets whatever effort the session or global default happened to be — invisible from the script that produced the result.
- Reproducibility suffers for exactly the workload where it matters most: a script that pins the model but not the reasoning effort has not pinned the run.
- Sweeping effort levels to compare cost and quality — a natural experiment for this audience — is impossible without clicking through the UI between runs.

**Proposal:** add `--effort <level>` and `--thinking <off|auto|on>` to `run`, validated against the selected model's declared stops, with a clear error when the variant has no control field (the CLI counterpart of `settings.thinking.unsupportedHint`) rather than silently ignoring the flag.

## Gap 2 — every sub-agent inherits one effort level

`reviewModelId` exists as a peer of `modelId`, so the design already accepts that a distinct role deserves its own model. But there is no `reviewThinkingEffort`, and `packages/specialist`, `packages/orchestration`, `packages/idea-tree`, and `packages/plan` contain **zero** references to effort. Every delegated agent therefore runs at the conversation's level.

That is the wrong shape for a multi-agent system:

- a literature-search or file-reading sub-agent running at `max` burns reasoning tokens on work that does not need them;
- an assessor, reviewer, or aggregator running at whatever the user last picked in the composer may be under-powered for the one judgement call that actually matters;
- the Idea Tree's designer / assessor / aggregator roles already have separate prompts (`ideaTree.designPrompt`, `.assessorPrompt`, `.aggregatorPrompt`) — separate effort is the natural companion, and the place where cost is most visible.

**Proposal:** make thinking effort part of the per-role profile (specialists, reviewer, Idea Tree roles), defaulting to *inherit* so nothing changes for anyone who does not set it. Cost control and quality both improve when the expensive setting can be spent where it matters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run --effort <level>` and `run --thinking <mode>` work and are documented in `help` and the CLI reference.
- [ ] An effort the model does not accept produces an explicit CLI error, not a silent no-op.
- [ ] A per-role effort can be set for at least the reviewer and the Idea Tree roles, defaulting to inherit.
- [ ] Unset behaviour is unchanged for every existing user.

## Open questions

- Is the *effective* effort of a completed run recorded anywhere a user can see it — usage, provenance, or the run record? If not, that is worth adding alongside the CLI flag: a batch of results is not comparable unless each one says what it was run at.
- Should `--effort` also accept a per-role form (e.g. `--review-effort`), or is that settings-only?
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Extend reasoning effort selection to the CLI and to per-role agents

## Problem

`services/api/src/http/static.ts` rejects paths with `candidate.startsWith(\`${staticDir}/\`)`. On Windows `resolve()` yields backslash separators, so the prefix check is always false and every SPA asset/route returns **400 Invalid path**.

This was discovered while reviewing PR #478 (`feat(F3.1): CAS platform abstraction`), which embeds a fix + tests. It is **out of scope for #477 (F3.1 CAS)** and should land as its own change with its own verification.

## Expected

Path containment uses a platform-neutral check (e.g. `path.relative` + `isAbsolute` / `..` segments) so Linux/macOS behaviour is unchanged and Windows serves SPA assets correctly.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows SPA asset served
- **Preconditions:** API built with `apps/web` static output; process running on Windows (or a path with `\` separators for `staticDir`).
- **Steps:** `GET /` and `GET /assets/<existing-bundle>.js` against the static handler.
- **Expected / pass:** Both return **200** with the expected body (not 400).

### Case 2 — Escape still rejected
- **Preconditions:** Same as Case 1; a file exists just above the static root.
- **Steps:** Request `/../escape.txt` and a percent-encoded variant `/%2e%2e/escape.txt`.
- **Expected / pass:** Both return **400 Invalid path**.

### Case 3 — No Linux/macOS regression
- **Preconditions:** Same suite on Linux (or macOS).
- **Steps:** Run the static containment unit tests (`services/api/src/http/static.test.ts` or equivalent).
- **Expected / pass:** All cases green; nested `..data` directory name is still served (not treated as escape).

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478
- Parent Windows desktop track: #400 / #31

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Long agent runs spend an increasing amount of time synchronously publishing trajectory records before the next model request. The main source is repeated full transitive-closure validation in the ScienceDiscovery CAS ref publication path.

This is visible with the JiuwenSwarm executor because it records every model request and completed turn through `AgentVersionRecorder`, but the expensive closure walk is implemented by ScienceDiscovery, not JiuwenSwarm.

The behavior was reproduced at commit `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`.

## Scope

This does not appear to be enabled only by CI:

- `createAgentRun()` supplies `versioning` for every normal agent run.
- `JiuwenSwarmTrajectory` creates an `AgentVersionRecorder` whenever `versioning` is present.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_TRACE_GATEWAY_PROGRESS=1` only adds progress logging around the same operations. It does not enable trajectory persistence, and the Nightly workflow does not set it.

Therefore ordinary local/UI runs use the same trajectory recording path. Short runs usually hide the cost; long histories amplify it.

## Evidence from two BiomniBench runs

Both runs disabled subagents, so child-agent execution is not required to reproduce the slowdown.

| Case | Session span | Completed model outputs | Model request time | Tool time | Time outside measured model/tool intervals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 76m 32.7s | 74 | 27m 39.7s | 7m 31.3s | 42m 59.3s |
| DA-14-1 | 81m 36.8s | 73 | 30m 47.8s | 10m 24.6s | 41m 55.6s |

The interval around a turn was split at `state.committed`:

| Case | Last tool to state committed | State committed to next model input | Combined |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 17m 57.0s | 19m 50.7s | 37m 47.7s |
| DA-14-1 | 15m 43.8s | 20m 56.4s | 36m 40.2s |

Per-turn combined medians grew with turn count:

| Case | Turns 0-19 | Turns 20-49 | Turns 50+ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 9.2s | 22.9s | 55.2s |
| DA-14-1 | 6.8s | 25.5s | 59.3s |

This time is shown under the broad UI `thinking` phase, but much of it occurs before the next model request has been sent.

## Direct CAS measurements

On the preserved DA-13-3 CAS:

- Step 5: 100 reachable objects, 4.1 MiB, 449-518ms to validate.
- Step 20: 346 objects, 22.9 MiB, about 1.7-2.1s.
- Step 50: 755 objects, 81.7 MiB, about 4.4-6.0s.
- Step 73: 989 objects, 141.6 MiB, about 7-11s.
- The model-input context closure at turn 74 contained 992 objects and took 9.27s to validate.

At least two such commits are on each turn's critical path: the exact model-input/context ref and the completed trajectory step.

A separate 70-turn synthetic `AgentVersionRecorder` benchmark used no model, network, web search, Jina, or subagent calls. It still showed:

- `after_assembly` median: 193ms for turns 0-19, 1,488ms for turns 50-69.
- `after_turn` median: 275ms for turns 0-19, 1,601ms for turns 50-69.
- Total runtime was about two minutes.

## Root cause

`RefStore.commit()` calls `VersionStore.validateClosure(target)` before every ref transaction. `validateClosure()` reads and hashes every reachable object. Trajectory steps strongly reference prior steps, snapshots, contexts, actions, and event segments, so the reachable closure grows with every turn.

Revalidating all immutable ancestors on every publication makes a long trajectory approximately quadratic in total validation work.

Relevant paths:

- `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`: `VersionStore.validateClosure()` and `RefStore.commit()`.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts`: context and step ref commits.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`: synchronous recording around model requests and completed turns.

## Isolated prototype

An offline prototype kept the public `validateClosure()` as a full byte/hash audit. For commit-time validation it:

1. Still traverses every reachable object.
2. Caches each successfully verified object's dependencies and filesystem identity (`dev`, `ino`, `size`, `mtimeNs`, `ctimeNs`).
3. Skips rereading and rehashing an object only when that identity is unchanged.
4. Falls back to full verification if the object is new or its metadata changed.
5. Publishes cache entries only after the entire closure succeeds.

Results:

| Measurement | Current implementation | Prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 70-turn late `after_assembly` median | 1,488ms | 168ms |
| 70-turn late `after_turn` median | 1,601ms | 252ms |
| 70-turn total runtime | about 120s | 29.7s |
| Real DA-13-3 steps 50-73 validation | final scans about 7-11s each | 409ms median, 535ms max |
| Replay all 74 DA-13-3 history roots | not measured as one batch | 20.7s total |

The two late-turn critical recording stages fell from about 3.09s to 0.42s, an 86% reduction in the synthetic run.

The prototype passed all 26 CAS tests. Tests also confirmed that a previously verified dependency is still rejected after deletion and after same-size content corruption.

## Expected behavior

Trajectory recording should remain available for exports, provenance, recovery, and debugging, but its synchronous per-turn cost should depend mainly on newly published objects rather than the size of the full historical trajectory.

## Possible direction

- Add an incremental commit-validation path while retaining an explicit full audit API.
- Consider a persistent verified-object index or storage generation if reuse across API restarts is needed.
- Keep full hash audits available on read/export, startup, background verification, or an explicit integrity operation.
- Add stage duration metrics for workspace snapshot, context publication, step publication, history serialization, SQLite commit, and model request so future stalls are attributable without multi-gigabyte artifact analysis.

The metadata-cache prototype has a trust boundary: a privileged actor able to rewrite bytes while preserving inode, size, mtime, and ctime could evade the commit fast path. A production design should document that assumption or use a stronger persistent verification mechanism.

This optimization does not address model latency, web/tool latency, workspace snapshot cost, history serialization, or the separate 240s no-progress failure observed after a final captured context.
closed_recent.title: Trajectory CAS commit validation grows quadratically in long agent runs

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

In the `feat/jiuwenswarm` remote Shell Execution flow, the API polls the Runner after the Runner accepts a job. If a status request throws because of a transient communication error, the current implementation can finalize the local record as `unknown / unconfirmed`. This means the remote result has not been confirmed; it does **not** prove that the remote job failed or that the full Agent/skill workflow passed.

## Trigger confirmed from the code

- In `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`, a `getShellExecution` exception reaches the outer error handler and calls `finish`, turning an accepted execution into `unknown / unconfirmed`. A transient observation error is not sufficiently separated from an authoritative remote terminal state.
- Once the local record is terminal, the normal `execution_status` path does not reconcile that record with the Runner using the original Execution ID. Executions left behind by API restarts or Runner reconnections also need an explicit reconciliation policy.
- The underlying reason for an SSH/Runner status request error still needs investigation. Without a correlated error cause and channel logs, `fetch failed` alone does not establish whether the NPU job, SSH connection, or server failed.

## Suggested reproduction

1. Submit a long-running Shell Execution to a remote Runner and confirm that the Runner accepted it.
2. Make only one **status request** fail transiently while keeping the remote job running.
3. Verify that the API keeps polling the **same Execution ID**, obtains the Runner's authoritative result after connectivity returns, and does not resubmit the command.
4. Also cover consecutive failures, API restart, Runner reconnection, and the complete Agent → skill → NPU artifact flow. See the related end-to-end test in #168.

## Expected fix and acceptance criteria

- Retry recoverable observation errors within a bound, resetting the consecutive-failure count after a successful query. If the result remains unavailable after the threshold, preserve the uncertainty explicitly instead of reporting success or a job failure.
- Provide safe Runner-authoritative reconciliation for `unknown` and restart-orphaned executions without replaying the command.
- Log a correlatable Execution ID, underlying error cause/code, consecutive-failure count, and Runner connection state so an observation-path failure can be distinguished from an actual job failure.
- Cover fault injection in CI without an NPU, and validate the final artifacts through the full Agent/skill workflow in an NPU-enabled environment.

closed_recent.body:
## What to change

On a large screen the Session conversation is too narrow, and it sits on the left. The composer under it is a different width. User messages should be a bubble on the right.

This is layout only. Do not change what a message contains, the right-hand artifact panel, or the narrow-screen stacking behavior.

## Current layout

The conversation pane is the left track of `.content-grid` (`apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`). The right track is a fixed 390px panel.

Inside the conversation pane:

- Each `.message` and the run timeline are capped at `820px` and are not centered, so on a wide pane they stay on the left. The same `820px` cap is repeated for the message skeleton, process records, and several timeline blocks (`conversation.css`, `timeline.css`, `process-records.css`, `feedback.css`).
- The composer does not use that cap. It stretches across the pane with `margin: 0 max(28px, 5vw) 28px`, so on a large screen it is wider than the transcript above it.
- A user turn is the same left grid as an assistant turn: a 40px avatar column, then the body. `.message.user .markdown-body` is only an inline block with a sunk background. It is not on the right.

## What other agents do

Public pages do not publish a single official pixel width. The pattern that matches this request:

- **Doubao (doubao.com).** The transcript and the input share one centered column (`--center-content-max-width`, `--content-max-width`, `--chat-area-max-width` on the chat route). The column stays centered in the area beside the left navigation as the window grows; it is not the full window. User sends are a separate right-aligned bubble. Community style scripts refer to a stock send-message cap around `max-w-650`, and they right-align that bubble with `margin-left: auto`. The stock column is what people widen with userscripts; one width slider starts at 760px, another forces 1600px. Those overrides are “make it full width,” which is not what we want. A public recreation of the Doubao column uses `max-width: 1000px`.
- **WorkBuddy.** The published UI is a left task list, a center conversation, and an optional right results panel. The input sits at the bottom of that same center column, so the transcript and the input are one width. The docs do not give a pixel width or say which side a user message sits on.
- **Trae.** Side chat is the IDE panel on the right (Command+U / Ctrl+U). Its width is the panel the user drags, not a centered reading column. It is a poor template for this screen.

## Target

On a wide conversation pane, one centered column holds the transcript and the composer. Make it a little wider than 820px, and do not let it fill the pane.

Use **1000px** as the shared max width (`min(1000px, 100%)`, centered with `margin-inline: auto`). That is the modest step implied by “a little wider,” and it matches the 1000px Doubao-style column rather than the 1600px full-width userscripts. Put the number in one custom property and point the transcript, timeline, process records, skeleton, and composer at it, so the old `820px` copies cannot drift apart.

The composer’s outer width is that column. Its inner padding can stay. Short viewports keep today’s full-width behavior, including the ~900px case where the sidebar must not cover the conversation.

User messages, inside that column:

- The bubble sits on the right.
- A short message is only as wide as its text. A long message wraps and may use the column width, but it still starts from the right.
- Assistant replies stay on the left and use the column width.
- Do not leave the user avatar in the left gutter while the bubble is on the right. Keep the avatar with the bubble, or drop the user avatar if it fights the bubble. Assistant avatars stay on the left.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width where the conversation pane is clearly wider than 1000px, the transcript and the composer are the same width, centered in the pane, and that width is 1000px rather than 820px or the full pane.
- A short user message is a bubble on the right of that column. An assistant message stays on the left.
- Below the width of the column, the column fills the pane and the composer still matches it. The existing narrow layout, including the sidebar at about 900px, still fits on the first screen.
- The right artifact panel stays 390px.
- A Web layout test or the existing conversation render test covers the shared column and the right-aligned user bubble.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Center a wider conversation column and right-align user bubbles

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #95](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/95) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Let the agent run a data analysis, and when a permission approval pops up midway, understand it quickly and make a decision.

## What I saw instead

Under the default approval policy, when the agent prepares to run a Python script in the sandbox to analyze a CSV, the conversation pauses with a permission card: "[Code] Execute Python script", showing the code and three buttons: `Allow once`, `Always allow matching items`, `Deny`.

## Why this is confusing

- Nothing explains what "matching items" actually matches (the same script? the same tool call? scoped to this session or broader?), so users are afraid to click it.
- The user just asked "analyze my data" and is now asked for permission, which feels like something went wrong.
- Until a choice is made the analysis just sits there, and the card does not explain the "waiting" state.

Note: the composer area already offers an "always allow" switch — this issue is not about adding a master switch. The focus is the **wording of the approval card itself and the explanation of the matching scope**.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- The card states each option's exact effect and scope in one sentence (e.g. "Allow once" lets only this call through; "Always allow matching items" stops asking for which calls within which scope — copy must match the actual behavior).
- The consequence of "Deny" is spelled out (the operation is skipped and the agent receives the denial).

Design note: first pin down the precise semantics of the three options in the current approval model, then write the card copy to match; a shortcut on the card to flip "always allow" can be evaluated as a follow-up enhancement.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Permission approval card wording is unclear and "Always allow matching items" does not explain its scope

## Problem

PR #431 (Fixes #41) collects an optional **Research description** at project creation and persists it on `Project.description` (trimmed, ≤2000 chars). After creation there is no UI that shows the description, and `UpdateProjectRequest` / project settings do not allow editing it. Users who fill the field cannot verify or change what was saved.

This is intentionally out of scope for #41 (creation-dialog presentation only) and is tracked here as a follow-up.

## Expected

- Project list and/or project settings show the stored research description when present.
- Users can edit (or clear) the description after creation via the normal project settings/rename flow.
- Blank/whitespace clears the field (same trim-and-omit semantics as create).

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Description visible after create
- **Preconditions:** Build at or after #431; signed-in workbench.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open **Add project**.
  2. Enter name `Desc-visible` and description `Compare tumor vs normal samples.`
  3. Create without expanding Advanced settings.
  4. Open the new project’s settings / detail surface where project metadata is shown.
- **Expected pass criteria:** The text `Compare tumor vs normal samples.` is visible without calling the API manually.

### Case 2 — Edit and clear
- **Preconditions:** A project with a non-empty `description` exists.
- **Steps:**
  1. Edit description to `Updated RNA-seq note` and save.
  2. Reload / reopen settings.
  3. Clear the description (empty / whitespace) and save.
- **Expected pass criteria:** Step 2 shows the updated text; after step 3 the description is absent/`undefined` on the project payload and hidden in UI.

### Case 3 — Unrelated project unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Two projects A (with description) and B (without).
- **Steps:** Edit A’s description only.
- **Expected pass criteria:** B still has no description; A’s other fields (name, settingsOverrides) unchanged aside from description.

## Context

- Related: #41, PR #431
- Schema today: `Project.description?` on create only; `UpdateProjectRequest` has no `description`

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #26](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (Chinese original of this issue). ### 🚀 Background Description Research agents often produce scripts, logs, configs, and prose (`.py`, `.r`, `.sh`, `.txt`, `.log`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.sql`, …). Users need to read those files in the artifact panel, not download them or jump to a new browser tab. The current viewer has two gaps: 1. **Plain-text artifacts have almost no in-app preview.** Catalog kinds only cover dataset / figure / html / json / latex / markdown / notebook / report / structure. Files such as `.py`, `.txt`, and `.log` fall into `other`. `ArtifactModal` loads only a few scientific kinds as text; `other` has no preview branch, so opening them is often a blank panel. In the workspace file sidebar, only `.md` uses the in-app Markdown reader; everything else is handed to `window.open` and the browser. 2. **Existing source / raw views are not a code-reading experience.** JSON, LaTeX source, Markdown source, CSV raw, and notebook code are plain `
`: no language highlighting, no line numbers, and long files are hard to scan or compare.

The viewer should:

- open plain-text files in-app;
- syntax-highlight common file types;
- show line numbers.

This is a viewing-experience request only. It does not change artifact registration, versioning, or provenance semantics.

### Design Ideas

Keep the existing specialized previews (Markdown render, tables, images, PDF/HTML iframe, molecular structure, notebook cells). Add one shared path for “read as source.”

Suggested behavior:

- Open recognizable UTF-8 text in-app — not a blank panel, and not a new browser tab by default.
- Pick a highlight language from the extension (and `mediaType` if needed). At least cover common research/engineering types:
  - plain text: `.txt`, `.log`, `.out`, `.err`
  - code: `.py`, `.r` / `.R`, `.jl`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.sh` / `.bash`, `.sql`, `.c` / `.h` / `.cpp`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`
  - config / data source: `.json`, `.yaml` / `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.xml`, `.css`, `.html`
  - document source: `.md`, `.tex`
- Unmatched extensions that are still text: show as plain text, still with line numbers.
- Binaries, images, PDFs, Office files, etc. keep the current specialized viewer or download; do not force them through a text decoder.
- Markdown / table / notebook specialized previews stay; their “Source / Raw” views should reuse the same highlight + line-number component.
- Oversized files keep truncated preview (reuse the existing ~100_000 character cap) and tell the user they can download the full file.
- Highlighter library and whether to add `kind=text/code` are implementation choices, as long as the user gets highlighted text with line numbers. Do not change the artifact catalog or provenance semantics just to enable highlighting.

Out of scope:

- editing or saving files in the viewer;
- turning every file into a source view (images still show as images, CSVs still show as tables);
- a full IDE (folding, go-to-definition, diagnostics).

### Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API is expected. The viewer should keep using the existing artifact-version content and workspace-file read endpoints.

Possible internal adjustments (for implementation, not a product contract):

- load `other` / uncategorized text as text instead of skipping it as binary;
- if extension classification gains a `text`/`code` kind, use it only for preview routing and do not change the meaning of existing scientific kinds.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Artifact panel `ArtifactModal`: main catalog preview; `other` text must be readable.
- Workspace file tree: clicking `.py` / `.txt` etc. should open the same in-app text view, not only a new browser tab.
- Existing source views: JSON raw, Markdown/LaTeX source, CSV raw, notebook code, provenance scripts/logs — good candidates to reuse the same component.
- Artifact classification (`classifyScientificArtifact`): there is no text/code kind today; do not mis-label `.py` as dataset/report.
- i18n: new buttons / empty states / truncation copy must go through the existing message catalog.
- E2E: artifact panel, workspace file open, and existing Markdown/table/structure previews all need regression.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- Open `.txt`: in-app full text (or truncation notice), line numbers; highlighting optional.
- Open `.py` / `.yaml` / `.json` and other common types: matching syntax highlighting, line numbers aligned with source lines (at least line 1 and the last visible line).
- Unknown extension, UTF-8 text: still opens as plain text with line numbers.
- Images, PDFs, structure files, other non-text: unchanged, not treated as source.
- Markdown artifacts: default remains rendered; Source view has highlighting and line numbers.
- Huge text: preview truncates, offers download, page stays responsive.
- Empty file: stable empty state, no error.

Regression:

- Markdown reports, CSV/JSON tables, images, HTML, notebooks, and molecular-structure previews still work.
- Workspace `.md` still uses the Markdown reader.
- Artifact download, version switching, and the provenance page still work.

Web E2E (required after changing the user-visible viewer):

- Open a text artifact in the panel; screenshot the highlighted, numbered end state.
- Open `.py` or `.txt` from the workspace tree; confirm in-app viewing rather than relying only on a new browser tab.
- Regression on one existing specialized preview (Markdown or CSV).

Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: support viewing plain-text artifacts, syntax highlighting for common file types, and line numbers.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Artifact viewer should preview plain text with syntax highlighting and line numbers

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Summary

When a subagent emits several independent biomedical MCP tool calls in one model response, ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler` executes them one at a time. The workspace registers opaque MCP tools without an `isConcurrencySafe` classifier, so the registry marks them `exclusive` even when JiuwenSwarm submits the requests concurrently. This adds avoidable latency to read-only literature searches. See the 2026-10-12 root-cause comment below for the stage trace and evidence boundary.

### Reproduction

1. Configure a public biomedical MCP source such as PubMed, allowing at least two concurrent source requests.
2. Have a ScienceDiscovery `task` subagent request six independent PubMed MCP searches in one model turn. Test both `allow` and `ask` (approve all six for the latter).
3. Compare the model batch, JiuwenSwarm/MCP SDK request starts, ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` classification, and broker start/end timestamps.

### Observed

In a DA-13-3 local E2E trace, one model SSE summary reported `toolCalls: 6` and `finishReason: tool_calls`. The six approvals were posted close together, but each MCP search started only after the previous search finished. Across the full subagent trace, 49 literature MCP invocations (42 PubMed, 7 Europe PMC) had **zero pairwise execution overlap**; their individual durations summed to 166.6 s. Broker `queueWaitMs` was 0, so its rate/concurrency queue does not explain the serialization. A representative six-call batch took 14.59 s wall time for 12.13 s summed tool execution.

A different DA-13-3 no-subagent trace shows that the main agent's built-in calls can overlap: six `free_search` calls summed to 88.6 s but occupied 21.9 s of union wall time; 24 `fetch_webpage` calls summed to 42.1 s but occupied 15.3 s. These are different tools and workloads, so this is evidence that overlap is possible, **not** a direct speed comparison.

### Expected

Independent read-only calls explicitly classified as concurrency-safe should run concurrently within the source's configured limits. Under `ask`, each call must still receive its own authorization decision; denied calls remain denied.

### Confirmed serialization path

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` does not declare `isConcurrencySafe` for opaque MCP tools. The existing workspace test explicitly checks this default.
- `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` `executionMode` returns `exclusive` when that classifier is absent.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` `ToolScheduler.run` waits for earlier same-batch calls whenever their execution mode is not `parallel`, before the call reaches the broker.
- Stage instrumentation confirmed that six PubMed calls overlap at the JiuwenSwarm tool and MCP SDK request entries under `allow`, while their broker intervals remain serial. The `ask` resume path adds latency but does not cause the common serialization.

### Measured scheduler control and performance boundary

**Product-path dispatch:** In the controlled six-PubMed-call `allow` probes, the original broker calls started one after another. With the read-only concurrency opt-in, all six began within 44 ms and the source broker then applied its own queue/concurrency limits. The batches took 12.09 s and 7.22 s respectively, but their successful-result counts differed (2/6 versus 1/6); those wall times are **not** a clean successful-workload speed comparison.

**Network-free scheduler control:** A fake JiuwenSwarm adapter submitted the same six fixed-success, MCP-like calls in one model response. Each call took 150 ms; a local two-permit limiter simulated the PubMed source concurrency ceiling. Across five repetitions per mode, every call succeeded:

| Classification | Six-call batch span, five runs | Median | Max active |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exclusive | 921.2–925.6 ms | 923.4 ms | 1 |
| Parallel-safe | 451.5–454.4 ms | 452.6 ms | 2 |

This measures about a 51% shorter batch span in ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler`, with the simulated source limit intact. It does not include the real MCP broker, model, or provider. The temporary diagnostic test was removed after running.

**Real-provider support outside ScienceDiscovery:** A separate no-model harness requested the same six public PubMed topics, including eSearch and eSummary, with at most two search jobs and at most two HTTP requests per second. In serial/parallel/parallel/serial order, the batch results were 10.031 s (6/6), 6.797 s (5/6; one HTTP 429), 6.344 s (6/6), and 11.359 s (6/6). The fully successful parallel block was quicker than either fully successful serial block. This supports the scheduling direction but is **not** a product E2E before/after or evidence of a success-rate improvement. [Methods and per-run data](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/262#issuecomment-6119154713).

**Whole-run boundary:** In the earlier DA-13-3 trace, 49 literature MCP calls occupied 189.6 s across ten contiguous batches. An optimistic two-concurrent-per-source schedule estimates 89.2 s, or about **100.4 s potential saving**; that remains a scheduling estimate, not a measured whole-run improvement. The 962.5 s E2E also includes different research work and model turns. A stable-provider, same-workload MCP integration benchmark is still needed before claiming an end-to-end speedup.

### Suggested acceptance test

Classify only known read-only MCP operations as parallel-safe; keep opaque/mutating tools exclusive. Use six independent read-only MCP calls emitted in one model turn under both `allow` and `ask`. Assert broker execution intervals overlap while respecting per-source concurrency/rate limits. Also cover mixed allow/deny decisions, preapproved calls, and correct replay after interruption.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Observed in local ScienceDiscovery E2E checkouts on 2026-10-09 (Windows host + WSL Linux runtime, x86_64).
- ScienceDiscovery API/adapter with installed JiuwenSwarm/OpenJiuwen runtime; public PubMed and Europe PMC MCP tools.
- PubMed source governance allowed up to two concurrent requests and three requests per second; broker reported `queueWaitMs: 0` for the observed calls.
- The model provider is not needed for reproduction: a deterministic model stub that emits one batch of six independent MCP `tool_calls` would isolate this behavior.
- No private API key or raw trace is attached.

### Additional Information

Related: #230 documents a separate CAS commit-validation bottleneck. The MCP serialization here remains observable with that optimization applied and also under `allow`. The 100.4 s figure above remains a bounded estimate; the new scheduler and provider controls do not replace a same-workload MCP integration benchmark.

### Version Information

Observed on the 2026-10-09 ScienceDiscovery experimental E2E checkout based on commit `4ece4d3` plus the local CAS commit-validation experiment discussed in #230. The 2026-10-12 controlled probe used a separate isolated checkout based on `4cf846f`; installed runtime metadata reported `openjiuwen 0.1.17` and editable `workswarm 0.2.5b1`. This report identifies the ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` policy in the tested checkout; it does not claim that every MCP operation is safe to run concurrently.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: ScienceDiscovery serializes independent read-only MCP searches

## Problem

Daily real-research shards fail during dependency preparation on the current `ubuntu-latest` image (Ubuntu 26.04, CPython 3.14.4), before any model calls. `.ci/prepare-real-research.sh` creates a venv using the runner interpreter and installs `numpy==2.2.6` and `scipy==1.15.3`. These versions fall back to source builds; SciPy then fails with `ERROR: Dependency "OpenBLAS" not found (tried pkg-config and cmake)`.

The same main commit (`7ee6c1d0bcc8374062364d51b3f4dfdf87a1396d`) passed dependency preparation on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12.3 on October 20 and failed on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14.4 on October 21. The October 22 and 23 scheduled runs repeat this failure. Current main (`0b74e53b`) still has the same numerical dependency pins.

Evidence: [October 21 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39666641312), [October 23 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40014929958).

## Required behavior

Support the new Ubuntu image and Python 3.14 rather than downgrading the runner or interpreter. Update the benchmark dependency preparation to a compatible, reproducible dependency set and check its direct consumers.

## Acceptance criteria

- The benchmark numerical dependencies install successfully on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 without an accidental source-build requirement for the obsolete pins.
- DRB and Biomni benchmark preparation and evaluator imports remain compatible with the selected dependencies.
- Add focused validation that catches this compatibility failure without making model calls.
- Keep the real-case assertions and evidence requirements intact. Model gateway billing failures and previously fixed runner cleanup behavior are outside this change.
closed_recent.title: fix(ci): support real-research prerequisites on Ubuntu 26.04 and Python 3.14

- **Reviewer Specialist:** On · **Automatic review:** On · level **Quick**

### User prompt (exact)
```text
Do a brief literature scan on CRISPR base editing for sickle cell disease. Summarize 3–5 key recent findings with citations, then write a short markdown report artifact. Keep it focused.
```

![user prompt in timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/01-user-prompt.png)

## What went wrong (locate here)
1. Open artifact after the run → Reviewer card says **Quick review passed**: “The applicable citation format and Artifact provenance checks passed.” Locked hash `b19742549423`.
2. Review record has `checks: [\"citation\"]`, `findings: []`, `decision: ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED`, `createdAt`→`finishedAt` ≈ **72ms**.

![Quick review passed — format/provenance only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/02-review-passed.png)

![Automatic review still On](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/03-automatic-review-on.png)

```json
{
  "checks": ["citation"],
  "decision": "ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED",
  "findings": [],
  "reviewLevel": "quick",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-19T14:33:02.574Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-10-19T14:33:02.646Z"
}
```

## Why this is a bug (not “effect”)
UI presents **PASSED** as if the report was substantively reviewed. Format-only ACCEPT with no “format-only / claim checks skipped” reason violates #323 acceptance (“explicit review outcome … or visible skip reason”).

## Expected
- Either run claim-fidelity checks in Quick, **or**
- Label outcome clearly as **format-only** / skip deeper checks with reason — never look like full verification.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Format-only Quick cannot display as undifferentiated “Quick review passed” for literature reports.
- [ ] Skip/partial reasons visible when claim checks do not run.
- [ ] Literature auto-review outcome distinguishes format vs claim-checked.

Related: #323, #413.
closed_recent.title: Bug: Quick automatic review accepts literature reports on citation format only (no claim fidelity)

### Checklist

- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Description

When a session is deleted, a confirmation dialog is shown that asks the user to type the session name and click the permanent-delete button. After entering the correct session name and clicking the permanent-delete button, the frontend reports a request error:

```
session not found
```

However, the session is in fact already deleted on the backend (it is gone from the session list after refreshing). In addition, the confirmation dialog does not close after the error is shown, so the UI is stuck on the dialog and the user has to dismiss it manually, and it is unclear whether the deletion actually succeeded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start ScienceDiscovery and open a project that contains at least one session.
2. Trigger the delete action on a session so that the delete confirmation dialog appears.
3. Type the exact name of the session to be deleted into the input of the dialog.
4. Click the permanent-delete button.

### Expected behavior

- The session is deleted without any error.
- The delete confirmation dialog closes automatically after the deletion succeeds.
- The session list refreshes and no longer shows the deleted session.

### Actual behavior

- A request error `session not found` is shown in the UI.
- The session is nevertheless deleted (it disappears from the list / after refreshing the page).
- The delete confirmation dialog stays open and is not dismissed.


### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows (x86_64)
- Deployment: local source mode, running from the latest main branch source (not the prepackaged binary)
- Service started with `./ScienceDiscovery serve`, UI accessed at http://127.0.0.1:4310
- Browser: Chromium-based desktop browser

### Additional Information

- The session is gone after refreshing the page, so the deletion itself succeeds on the backend; the `session not found` error and the fact that the dialog stays open appear to be a frontend state/refresh issue after the delete request returns.
- Expected fix: treat the response as success (or refresh the session list) and always close the confirmation dialog once the delete request completes.

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery: latest main branch (built and run from source)

### Problem

Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain literal `<think>` tags.

These tags appear as part of the visible title instead of a clean summary of the conversation. This makes session titles confusing and harder to scan.

The issue is intermittent; the exact trigger has not yet been identified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session and send a message.
2. Wait for the session title to be automatically generated.
3. Check the generated title.
4. Occasionally, the title contains literal `<think>` tags.

### Actual behavior

The generated session title includes `<think>` markup.

### Expected behavior

Automatically generated session titles should contain only a concise, readable summary of the conversation, without reasoning tags or reasoning content.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Automatically generated titles never display `<think>` or `</think>` tags.

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
Follow-up discovered during the repository-wide review of #295; related to #288 and #291. Suggested priority: **P2**.

A failed model connection can silently undo a successful settings change made by another tab or API client while the connection test is running. The wizard restores the entire global-settings snapshot captured before the attempt, including fields it did not change.

This is **pre-existing**, not a regression introduced by #295. The same browser/API reproduction failed on both the base commit `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310` and PR revision `45366a904edc7c57e69d36ce79b944e75b382d45`. The rollback code remains unchanged in the latest PR revision `d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635`.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated instance, the real API/store, and a local model endpoint that returns an authentication failure. No real provider credentials are needed.

1. Start with no registered models and persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
2. Open System settings → Models and connect a custom provider. Let the wizard successfully read global settings, create the provider, and register its first model. The backend automatically selects this first model as the global default.
3. While `POST /api/models/:id/test` is pending, use a second API client to read the current overrides and successfully write them back with only `thinkingEffort` changed to `"low"`. Preserve the current temporary `modelId` in this write.
4. Let the connection test return an authentication failure.
5. Read back `GET /api/settings`.

Observed interleaving, with the generated model ID abbreviated:

| Stage | Persisted overrides |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state / wizard snapshot | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |
| Successful concurrent write | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"low","modelId":"temporary-model"}` |
| Wizard rollback | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |

**Actual:** the concurrent `"low"` setting is silently replaced by the old `"high"` value.

**Expected:** undo only this attempt's default-model change when it is still owned by the attempt; preserve the other client's `"low"` setting and every other unrelated override.

The browser reproduction intercepts the model-test request only to schedule a second, successful write through the real settings API before allowing the failing model test to proceed. It uses the actual App, wizard, HTTP API, and store.

## Cause and implementation boundary

[`ModelConnectWizard.restoreSavedOverrides`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L360-L377) calls `replaceGlobalSettings(savedOverrides)` on failure. This replaces the whole settings object with a snapshot taken before provider creation and model testing.

The backend needs the attempt's automatic default cleared before it can delete the temporary model, but restoring unrelated fields is unnecessary. The same unconditional rollback also runs when existing models meant the attempt did not change the default.

The [documented settings boundary](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md#L220-L232) already provides a catalog-level settings mutex and revision-checked plugin writes. Classic PUT intentionally remains last-writer-wins. This issue concerns the wizard's stale whole-object compensation; it does not require changing all classic PUT semantics.

A frontend-only fresh GET followed by another whole-object PUT still leaves a read/write race. Use an atomic conditional undo or equivalent version/ownership check at the existing server-side settings boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed connection preserves unrelated global-setting changes committed while that connection is in progress, including explicit empty connector selections.
- [ ] Rollback changes `modelId` only if the current default still belongs to this attempt; a newer default chosen by another writer is not overwritten.
- [ ] If the attempt never changed the global default, cleanup does not restore the old global-settings snapshot.
- [ ] In the uncontended first-model failure case, the temporary automatic default is safely undone and only the attempt's provider/models are deleted; existing references remain protected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic integration regression test using real settings persistence and an interleaved second writer. Check persisted settings after rollback and reopening the store, rather than only asserting mock delete calls.
- [ ] Cover both an unrelated-field edit and a concurrent default-model change, while retaining #295's test that a failed initial settings read creates no provider/model.

This is separate from #291: here the wizard's initial settings read succeeds, and the loss occurs during later failure rollback after another writer has saved successfully.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Model connection rollback overwrites concurrent global settings changes

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
The sandbox network consent card added in #381 (Fixes #324) offers **Allow once / Allow same type / Deny**. For a `sandbox_network` request the second button doesn't say what it covers. I checked on #381 head `fb2fe785`: choosing **Allow same type** for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443` does **not** widen to other hosts. A later request for `api.crossref.org:443` in the same run still raised its own card, because the resource is a per-host/run digest. Users can still reasonably read "same type" as "all sandbox network access", which is broader than what is actually granted.

## Expected
For `sandbox_network` cards, the user can tell exactly what each button grants. Either:
- rename the button for this action (e.g. "Allow these hosts for this conversation"), with a short scope hint, or
- hide it, if repeat consent for the exact same host set isn't a useful flow.

## Context
- Refs #381, #324.
- The button label comes from the shared key `permissions.allowMatching`, which every permission type uses. The fix should be action-specific, not a global rename.
- Repro: Ask approval mode → model calls `request_sandbox_network` for host A → **Allow same type** → model requests host B in the same run → a new card appears for B.

## Verification cases
1. **Label reads its real scope**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `none`; the model calls `request_sandbox_network` with `hosts: ["eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443"]`.
   - Steps: Open the pending card in the conversation.
   - Expected: The card shows exactly one card for that host. The second button is either missing or its label names the host scope (not "Allow same type"). Allow once and Deny are unchanged.
2. **Grant never widens to another host (regression)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1.
   - Steps: Click the second button (whatever it is called) for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443`. In the same run the model then requests `api.crossref.org:443`.
   - Expected: A **new** card appears for `api.crossref.org:443`. The second host is not auto-allowed, and there are 2 `sandbox_network` permission requests in total.
3. **Other permission types unaffected**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; the model calls `run_shell`.
   - Steps: Open the "Run a shell script" card.
   - Expected: Its buttons keep the current labels (Allow once / Allow same type / Deny) and behaviour.
4. **Global settings untouched**
   - Steps: Run case 2. Compare `GET /api/sandbox-network-settings` before and after.
   - Expected: The settings are identical.
closed_recent.title: Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear for one-shot sandbox network grants

closed_recent.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
closed_recent.body:
## Correction (2026-10-22T04:2xZ)

This issue was first filed as an "intermittent CI load flake". **That was wrong.** The failure is deterministic and the root cause is a runner image change. The earlier hypothesis (concurrency/load) is withdrawn, and the "same test passes in the CI-test run" evidence was also invalid — `UT` was skipped in that run.

## What actually happens

GitHub rolled `ubuntu-latest` from **ubuntu-24.04** to **ubuntu-26.04** between 2026-10-21T10:15Z and 2026-10-22T02:22Z. The pruning path builds its "busy" set from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe`:

```
packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:106
busy=$(for process in /proc/[0-9]*; do readlink "$process/exe" 2>/dev/null || true; done)
```

On ubuntu-26.04 that link no longer reports the binary a live process is executing, so the pruning pass sees an **in-use binary as stale and deletes it**. This is product code, not only a test helper: on 26.04 the same logic would delete a binary that is currently running.

## Evidence

| when (UTC) | job | runner image | `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-21T10:16Z | `119165996742` (#467 merge group) | **ubuntu-24.04** | 2661 ms, all tests pass |
| 2026-10-22T03:31Z | `119621422198` (#468) | **ubuntu-26.04** | 3 `/bin/sh`, `/bin/dash`, `/bin/bash` cases fail |

- Runner version is `2.338.0` in both jobs; only the image changed.
- Failing run [39716847675](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39716847675), job `119621422198`, step `Run UT`: planned 4441 / executed 4441 / passed 4438 / **failed 3** / skipped 0.
- Failure artifact `ut/tagged/group-141/worker-1-events.jsonl`: actual has an extra `'b' x 64` — the busy binary was pruned. The other 4 tests in the file pass.
- `merge-gate` (job `119626303432`) only aggregates: `CI gate failed: ut: failure`.
- Every PR after the switch shows the same signature: #269 #316 #460 #463 #465 #466 #467 #468.

## Impact

`UT` is a required check, so **no PR can enter the merge queue** for reasons unrelated to its own diff — the pipeline is blocked repo-wide.

## Suggested fix

1. Short term (unblocks the queue): pin the UT job to `ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:194` uses `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`).
2. Correct fix: stop deriving "busy" from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe` alone. Compare device+inode via `stat -L /proc/<pid>/exe` against the file being pruned (works when the link target is not readable), and log the observed `busy` set when a removal is skipped, so the next platform change is diagnosable from CI logs.
3. Add a regression test that fails if a running binary is pruned — the existing test is the right shape, but it needs to run on the platforms we actually support.
closed_recent.title: bug(executor): pruning treats live binaries as stale on ubuntu-26.04 runners (busy detection uses readlink /proc/<pid>/exe)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require “sandbox already unavailable” before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still “ready”; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for “prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent.”

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Agent-first direct execution (skip-sandbox by Agent + user consent)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

原生主 Agent（`runtime-core` AgentLoop）支持一轮多个 `tool_calls`，默认可并行约 10 路（`SCIENCE_AGENT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS`）。

Codex / Claude / ACP **specialist-runtime** 则走结构化 `platformDecision`：schema 只有单个 `tool` 字段（`string | null`），文案与循环均为「Request ONE platform tool → 校验 → 执行一个 → 回灌 → 下一轮」。这不是全平台总契约，只是 specialist 路径约定。

体验后果：自由 brief（尤其 DSV 兼容端点）易报 `Codex returned an invalid platform decision`；任务被拆成多轮，延迟与首败噪音上升。

## 目标

放开 specialist 路径「一轮只能一个平台工具」的硬限制，使其更接近主 Agent 的多工具能力；同时保留权限总线（原生 shell/改文件仍应走平台工具，不得悄悄打开 `shell_tool` 绕过）。

## 建议方向（实现可选，验收看行为）

- Schema 支持一轮多个 tool 请求（数组或等价结构），执行循环按序或可并行（exclusive 工具同轮串行即可）。
- 非法/半合法输出：纠错重试或自动拆轮，减少 `invalid platform decision` 首败。
- 若需分档：可按 runtime kind / 兼容端点默认保守，官方端点更宽；**不要**仅暴露一个无说明的全局布尔就结束。

## 验收标准

- [ ] specialist decision 契约允许多 tool（文档 + schema + 执行循环一致）。
- [ ] 至少一条自动化测试：一轮 decision 含 ≥2 个合法平台工具时可完成执行（或明确的有序执行），且权限/审计仍走平台路径。
- [ ] 非法 JSON / 多意图胡写时有明确失败或纠错，不静默丢工具。
- [ ] 不恢复 Codex 原生 `shell_tool` / 未授权改文件作为捷径。
- [ ] 与 DSV 等兼容端点联调：自由 brief 的 `invalid platform decision` 首败率相对现状有可描述改进（测试或手测步骤写清）。

## 非目标

- 不改主 Agent 并行上限策略（已有）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 runtime 选择 / 加密配 key / Specialist CLI 卡片（见 #455）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/codex.ts` — `decisionSchema`（单 `tool`）
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/decisions.ts` — `platformDecisionSchema`
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` / `tool-scheduler.ts` — 主 Agent 多 tool
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` — `maxParallelToolCalls`
closed_recent.title: feat(specialist-runtime): 放开一轮仅一个平台工具的硬限制

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

Phase2/3 合入后，旧版 `normalizeSpecialistInput` 白名单重建会**静默丢掉** `runtime`（HTTP 仍 201，看起来像创建成功但没有 Codex）。当前源码已修复：`store` 会保留并校验 `runtime`，非法则 400（`SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`）。

日常 CI 已有 UT 覆盖（`services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` 的 create/update/reload 保留 `runtime`；`phase3.test.ts` 多 kind 保留 + 拒凭据字段）。但 **HTTP 层契约偏薄**：没有断言 `POST/PATCH /api/specialists` 响应里的 `runtime`，也没有断言非法字段 → 400。Journey 脚本能间接暴露问题，但默认不进可重复 CI。

## 目标

补上可进 CI 的 HTTP（或等价集成）用例，防止后续改动再次把 `runtime` 从 create/update 路径丢掉。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `POST /api/specialists` 带合法 `runtime: { kind: "codex" }`（及/或 `claude-code` / `acp`）→ **2xx**，且 **响应 body 含同等 `runtime.kind`**（及已声明的非密钥元数据）。
- [ ] `PATCH`（或 update）只改 `description` 等无关字段后，**`runtime` 仍保留**。
- [ ] 带未知凭据字段（如 `apiKey`）或非法 `kind` → **400**，错误可识别为 runtime 配置无效（与现有 `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID` 对齐）。
- [ ] 用例挂在默认可重复门禁（UT/集成，**非**仅手工 journey）；失败条件明确、可本地复现。
- [ ] 不把真实密钥写进测试；不依赖外部 DeepSeek/Codex 网络。

## 非目标

- 不解决「旧 dist / 缓存包缺 `specialist-runtime`」的运维错配提示（可另开）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 UI / 主 Agent 代配 / Specialist CLI 卡片（见姊妹产品 issue）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — `normalizeSpecialistInput` → `normalizeSpecialistRuntime`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/config.ts` — `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` / `phase3.test.ts`
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — 该 code → 400

## What happened

On a session that is still open, the Tasks panel shows `Session not found`, and the same string appears as a request-error toast.

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` polls `getAgentActivity(sessionId)` every 2 seconds. On failure it sets the panel alert to the error message and leaves the previously loaded execution list in place. The screenshot matches that: the session heading is visible, the execution list is populated, and an alert says `Session not found`.

Failure pages from 2026-10-06:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288), DRB-59. Heading `DRB-59 autonomous research` was visible. The Tasks panel showed `Executions 32` and an alert `Session not found`. A second toast was the invalid `run_shell` arguments error. The needs-attention banner also said `Session not found`.
- Same run, DRB-62. Heading `DRB-62 autonomous research` was visible, with `Executions 20` and the same alert, plus the `interaction round execution failed` toast.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020), TC-E2E-01. Heading `BRCA1 team signoff` was visible, with 17 artifacts, `Executions 115`, and resume buttons for stopped subagents. The only request-error toast was `Session not found`.

Many API handlers return 404 `Session not found` when `store.getSession` misses. Which of those handlers the poll hit is not in the Actions log.

## Expected

While the session page is open and its execution list is shown, the activity poll does not report `Session not found` for that session. A 404 for a different id is attributed to that id.

## Evidence limits

This alert was on the failure screens above. The benchmark metrics for DRB-59 and DRB-62 say the main run status was `failed` for a different recorded request error. The team case was still `running` when its budget expired. This issue does not claim that the 404 is what stopped those runs.
