closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
## Description

When the Nightly workflow runs UT and ST with the `daily` profile, both test jobs produce raw coverage data, but the Coverage job does not receive the corresponding artifacts. As a result, coverage merging fails and the coverage summary is not updated.

Affected run:

- Nightly run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35919083156
- Commit: `9c5a5097336ab5342050dc07f9b14c3ccfce9cd0`
- Actual UT output: `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- Actual ST output: `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

The UT and ST jobs themselves completed successfully and wrote coverage data. The failure occurs while handing that data off to the Coverage job.

## Root cause

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` includes the profile name in the output label for profiles other than `pr`:

```js
const label = dimensions.length
  ? 'query'
  : profileName === 'pr'
    ? slice
    : `${profileName}-${slice}`;
```

This produces the following paths:

- `pr + ut` → `.ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + ut` → `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + st` → `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

However, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` still uses profile-independent upload paths:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage
```

and:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/st/tagged/coverage
```

When Nightly selects the `daily` profile, neither hard-coded path exists. `actions/upload-artifact` therefore reports that no files were found and does not create the `ut-coverage` or `st-coverage` artifact. The Coverage job cannot download those artifacts, merges zero Node.js and Python files, and fails.

This is not a dashboard input-path issue. The data is never uploaded as a workflow artifact, and a later job cannot access the previous job's local workspace directly.

## Regression timeline

- PR #148 introduced the `daily` profile and the `daily-ut` / `daily-st` output naming:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/148
- PR #150 changed Coverage to reuse data produced by the UT/ST jobs, but used hard-coded `ut` / `st` upload paths that do not account for non-`pr` profiles:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/150
- PR #158 enabled hidden-file uploads for the result artifacts, but did not update the coverage artifact paths:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/158

The previous successful Nightly run was:

- https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35782010015

That run started before PR #150 was merged, so it did not use the current UT/ST coverage-artifact handoff. The `daily-ut` naming introduced by PR #148 is intentional; the regression is the profile-independent artifact path added by PR #150.

## Suggested fix

Avoid hard-coding the `ut` and `st` result directories in the workflow. Possible approaches include:

1. Compute the actual result directory from `${{ inputs.profile || 'pr' }}` and upload coverage from that directory.
2. Have the test runner expose the resolved coverage path as an explicit step output.
3. Use a constrained glob that covers `ut`, `daily-ut`, `st`, and `daily-st` without mixing data from unrelated profiles or slices.

An explicitly computed path is preferable because it avoids accidentally merging data from multiple profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pr` profile continues to upload and merge UT/ST coverage.
- Nightly with the `daily` profile uploads coverage from `daily-ut` and `daily-st`.
- The Coverage job downloads `ut-coverage` and `st-coverage` and generates non-empty Node.js and Python summaries.
- If UT or ST produces no coverage, the summary identifies the missing layer instead of reporting a misleading zero-file merge.
- The Release workflow continues to skip coverage generation and upload.
closed_recent.title: bug(ci): Nightly coverage artifacts are not uploaded for the daily profile

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

Pushing a version tag starts `.github/workflows/release.yml`. After the L5 gate passes, the `publish` job runs `gh release create` and the GitHub Release becomes public immediately. Nobody reviews the gate result, the generated notes, or the attached binaries before the release shows up on the Releases page.

## Desired flow

Keep the current order up to the gate: tag push, resolve the version, run the release gate. When the gate is green, create the GitHub Release as a **draft** (`gh release create --draft`). A person with write access reviews that draft and publishes it from the Releases page. That publish action is the human review. Do not add a GitHub Environment required-reviewer gate.

## Behavior to preserve

- The tag filter, version parsing, and the hyphen-means-prerelease rule stay. When the version contains a hyphen, pass `--prerelease` together with `--draft`. Publishing the draft later must leave that prerelease flag in place, so a prerelease still does not become Latest.
- A failed gate still creates no Release and uploads no assets. The git tag remains.
- If a release for that tag already exists, whether it is a draft or already published, keep today's path: `gh release upload --clobber` only. Do not publish a draft from the workflow, do not turn a published release back into a draft, and do not run `gh release edit --draft=false`.
- The publish job stays idempotent. A re-run after a failed upload must not be blocked by a draft the first attempt already created.
- Keep publishing the binaries the gate already smoke-tested. Do not rebuild them in the publish job. Keep the SHA256 check and the requirement that both architectures are present.
- Do not add required reviewers to the `nightly-ci-ds` environment. Merge-queue, nightly, and release real-E2E jobs share it for model credentials. Putting a reviewer on it would pause those jobs.
- `scripts/release-notes.mjs` already skips drafts when it chooses the previous release (`previousTagFrom` drops `isDraft`). Leave that unless a test shows this change breaks note generation. A draft must not become the comparison baseline for a later release.

## Docs that currently describe immediate publication

Update only the sentences that say a successful gate publishes a public, downloadable Release:

- The header comments in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a tag push "publishes" the release, and assets "become downloadable" once the called workflow is green).
- The L5 row in `.ci/README.md` ("Blocks Release/assets").
- The L5 row in `.agents/skills/ci/SKILL.md`, which says failure blocks Release/assets publication.

New meaning: the gate blocks creating the draft Release and its assets. The draft is not a public release until a person publishes it. The tag is still created before the workflow runs, and a failed gate still does not delete that tag.

## Out of scope

- Do not move, delete, or re-push existing tags, including `v0.3.0-rc1`.
- Do not re-run or edit a Release workflow run that has already started.
- The new behavior applies to tag pushes after this change is on the default branch.

## Acceptance

- `gh release create` in the publish job includes `--draft`.
- The already-exists branch only replaces assets with `gh release upload --clobber`.
- Prerelease detection is unchanged, and a hyphenated version is still created as a prerelease draft.
- The three docs above match this behavior.
- `nightly-ci-ds` has no new protection rules.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Create the GitHub Release as a draft after the release gate

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is still locked below the fix for CVE-2026-104850, and this repository uses the affected OAuth client.

## Current pin

`services/api` depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `^1.30.0`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `1.30.0`. The advisory is fixed in 1.31.0 on the 1.x line, and in `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.2.0 on the 2.x line.

## What the advisory covers

From 1.12.0 until those fix versions, the SDK's OAuth client lets the MCP server it is talking to choose which authorization server receives stored credentials. Stored credentials are not bound to the authorization server they belong to. A malicious or compromised MCP server can name its own authorization server in protected-resource metadata. Without another user step, the client can send that server the `refresh_token` and `client_secret` saved from an earlier sign-in.

## Why this tree is in scope

`services/api/src/mcp/oauth.ts` builds an `OAuthClientProvider` for custom MCP servers. The provider persists client information and bearer tokens, and it keeps a refresh token across token refreshes. That is the client shape the advisory describes.

## Expected

Upgrade `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to 1.31.0 or newer and keep custom-MCP OAuth sign-in working. Until that upgrade, connect OAuth-enabled MCP clients only to servers the operator trusts.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/134
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-104850

## Current pin

`apps/web` depends on `katex` `^0.16.47`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `katex@0.16.47`. The advisory is fixed in 0.18.2.

## What the advisory covers

From KaTeX 0.11.0 until 0.18.2, ordinary property access treats inherited properties on the renderer options, the trust setting, and namespace lookup as values the caller set. KaTeX does not itself pollute `Object.prototype`, and rendering an expression alone does not run script. If the prototype is already polluted, or an attacker controls the options object's prototype, a math expression can inherit a trust flag and emit links that a page then inserts.

Depend on KaTeX 0.18.2 or newer.

closed_recent.body:
## What is wrong

In Web settings, the free-engine group is titled:

- English: `Free search engines (tried after paid)`
- Chinese: `免费搜索引擎（付费之后尝试）`

The Chinese parenthetical reads as “try these only after you have paid.” A reader can think the free engines are locked until a paid plan is purchased. They are not. DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave’s public result pages need no API key and no paid provider. Search tries a keyed paid provider first when one is configured, then these engines. With no paid key, only the enabled free engines run.

The English parenthetical is the source of that translation. “Tried after paid” is also easy to read as “after payment,” rather than “after the keyed paid providers.”

The longer help text above the groups already states the real order. The group title contradicts that reading.

## Where

- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, key `webSettings.freeLegend` (both locales)
- Rendered by `apps/web/src/WebSettingsEditor.tsx` as the free-engine fieldset legend
- `apps/web/tests/WebSettingsEditor.test.tsx` asserts the current English legend and must change with it

Search order, provider keys, and which engines are requested stay as they are. `docs/zh/reference/web-tools.md` already describes the order and does not use this title.

## Suggested copy

Keep one fact in the title: these engines do not need a key. Keep the attempt order in the hint under the group, so it is not lost and is not phrased as a payment requirement.

- `webSettings.freeLegend`
  - English: `Free search engines (no API key)`
  - Chinese: `免费搜索引擎（无需密钥）`
- `webSettings.freeHint`
  - English: `No API key is required, and a paid provider is not required. Keyed paid providers are tried first; these engines are tried, in the order shown, only when those return no results. A switched-off engine is never requested.`
  - Chinese: `无需密钥，也不需要先开通付费服务。已保存密钥的付费服务商会先尝试；它们没有返回结果时，再按显示顺序尝试这里仍开启的引擎。已关闭的引擎不会被请求。`

A shorter title is fine if it cannot be read as “available only after payment,” and if the English and Chinese titles say the same thing.

## Acceptance

- The Chinese title no longer says `付费之后尝试`, and does not otherwise say that payment is required before these engines can be used.
- The English title no longer says `tried after paid`.
- The hint under the group still says that a switched-off engine is never requested, and that keyed paid providers are tried first when they are configured.
- The Web settings render test matches the new English title.
- No change to which engine is called, or to the paid-then-free attempt order.

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Problem

After deploying ScienceDiscovery from source, users cannot reliably access the application by opening its local web address directly.

They must first find the `Open to sign in` URL in the deployment logs and open that specific link. Otherwise, the web page reports an error because the browser has not received the required local authentication information.

This behavior is difficult to discover and creates an unnecessary setup step:

- Users may not know that the startup logs contain a required sign-in link.
- The link can be missed among other service logs.
- Users may assume the deployment failed when opening the local address produces an error.
- The workflow is inconvenient for remote deployments, background processes, and users who no longer have the original terminal output.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy and start ScienceDiscovery from source.
2. Open the local ScienceDiscovery web address directly in a browser.
3. Observe that the application cannot be used successfully and reports an error.
4. Return to the deployment logs and locate the `Open to sign in` URL.
5. Open that URL and observe that the application then works.

### Expected behavior

After a successful source deployment, users should be able to open the advertised local web address directly and use ScienceDiscovery without copying a special sign-in link from the startup logs.

Local authentication should be initialized automatically or handled through the web interface while preserving the existing security boundary.

### Suggested improvement

Remove the requirement to retrieve the initial sign-in URL from deployment logs. For example, the application could automatically establish the local browser session, redirect users through the required local authentication flow, or provide an authentication setup page when they open the regular application URL.

The startup logs may continue to print a convenient URL, but opening that exact URL should not be required for normal use.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can access a newly started source deployment from its regular local web address.
- [ ] Users do not need to search the deployment logs for an `Open to sign in` link.
- [ ] Opening the regular address does not produce an authentication-related error during first use.
- [ ] The behavior works when the service runs in the background and the original terminal output is unavailable.
- [ ] Local access remains protected by the intended authentication mechanism.
- [ ] Documentation no longer instructs users to retrieve a required sign-in link from startup logs.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Source deployments require users to find and open a sign-in link from the startup logs

## What happened

Several real-E2E failures show up in GitHub Actions as only this assertion:

```text
Error: Main run must complete and reference a readable nonempty final artifact
Expected: "passed"
Received: "failed"
```

`delivery.status` comes from `deliveryStatus(runStatus, delivered)` in `test/helpers/real-delivery.mjs`. An empty delivered-artifact list returns `"failed"`. That string does not say whether the run status was `failed`, `running`, or `completed`, and it does not include `run.error`.

The assertion is at `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` (the `expect(delivery.status, "Main run must complete and reference a readable nonempty final artifact")` check) and the same check in `test/science-research-team-real.spec.ts`. The DeepResearch spec stores the assertion text into `metrics.error` in the `catch` block, so the attached benchmark metrics also lose the product error.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), DRB-59, DRB-62, and DRB-75 all printed that assertion. The failure-page text was different for each:

- DRB-75: gateway HTTP 500, `Database error, please contact the administrator`.
- DRB-59: `Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell)`.
- DRB-62: `interaction round execution failed`.

`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts` already throws ``Main run ${run.status}: ${run.error}``, so PUCT-COMPRESS printed the HTTP 500 in the Actions log. The DeepResearch and team specs do not.

## Expected

When `delivery.status` is not `"passed"`, the Actions log includes the run status and the product error string that the page already shows. An empty artifact list and a gateway 500 remain distinguishable without opening the trace.

## Evidence limits

`collectFinalDelivery` returns `run_status`, `answer`, `artifacts`, and content-read errors. For these failures `delivery.errors` was empty because no artifact was selected. The product error was on the page, not in that array.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
Repeated literature connector failures amplify latency across parallel research agents

Real E2E runs on `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `1a0cb9d5` show a non-fatal but significant research-efficiency problem. Agents eventually deliver reports using alternative sources, but continue querying unavailable/rate-limited connectors across independent branches.

## Observations

The experiment ran four cases concurrently, with native task dispatch and Swarm execution, memory graph disabled, and 24 GiB per case. These are observed counts, not a controlled concurrency experiment.

| Run | arXiv failures | Details | Other academic connector failures |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| DRB-62 repeat 1 | 65 | 60 HTTP 406; 5 slot-wait timeouts | 0 Europe PMC/PubMed |
| DRB-62 repeat 2 | 100 | 30 HTTP 406; 46 HTTP 429; 24 slot-wait timeouts | 14 Europe PMC; 6 PubMed |
| DRB-64 repeat 1 | 59 | All arXiv invocations failed | 2 PubMed |
| DRB-64 repeat 2 | 80 | All arXiv invocations failed | 29 Europe PMC; 3 PubMed |

DRB-62 repeat 2 included agent-issued `sleep 30`, `sleep 90`, and `sleep 150` followed by retries. Connector errors included `HTTP 406 Not Acceptable from export.arxiv.org`, `HTTP 429 Unknown Error from export.arxiv.org`, and `arxiv is rate limited and no slot became free within the wait window`. Some upstream failures were surfaced as `retryable:false`, but later calls to the same source still occurred.

Generation time increased from 18.8 to 69.1 minutes for DRB-62 and from 33.2 to 51.2 minutes for DRB-64. This is **not** an attribution of the whole increase to connectors: expanded research scope, synthesis work, and a separate stream disconnect also contributed.

## Investigation / improvement scope

- Diagnose 406 separately from 429: request/endpoint rejection should not be treated as ordinary rate limiting. Verify the actual upstream requests and responses before choosing a fix.
- Make source cooldown/health visible across sibling agents and, where appropriate, concurrent case workers. Confirm existing rate-limit scope before adding another mechanism.
- Honor Retry-After where available; provide bounded admission waits and explicit retry timing. Avoid multiple agents independently sleeping and repeating requests against a persistently failing source.
- Provide actionable fallback guidance without silently changing scholarly evidence requirements.
- Keep low-volume structured diagnostics: source, sanitized endpoint, status, wait duration, retry decision, request/run correlation IDs; never log credentials.

## Reproduction and acceptance

1. Run DRB-62/64 with parallel literature branches and inspect per-source invocation status plus queue waits. The production upstream failure is intermittent, so this alone is not a deterministic reproducer.
2. Add deterministic connector fault injection for sustained 406, repeated 429 with Retry-After, and slot exhaustion across concurrent callers.
3. Verify failures are reported honestly, repeated requests/waits are bounded, cooldown is shared at the intended scope, recovery occurs after cooldown, and alternative sources remain usable.

Local retained evidence (available on the experiment host): `/root/sciencediscovery-real9-3x-20260926/DRB-{62,64}/repeat-{1,2}/data/mcp-invocations/` and `results/artifacts/*/child-trajectories.json`. These paths are not publicly accessible; the aggregate evidence above is included to make the issue independently understandable.

Priority: non-fatal Harness efficiency/reliability follow-up. TC-E2E Judge stability is being fixed separately.

## Summary

Uploading a PDF through the workspace **Drop files** control does not go through the paper-reader pipeline. Paper reader stays at **0 parsed**, and the agent only sees a raw file (often with almost no extractable scientific content unless it scrapes bytes itself).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, new session in a data-analysis project.
2. Drop `experiment_notes.pdf` (+ optional CSV) via **Drop files**.
3. Ask the agent to read the PDF notes and fit kinetics from the CSV (no network).
4. Observe: Paper reader counter remains **0 parsed**. Agent reports extracting only the single plain line from the PDF and explicitly notes missing protocol/units/replicates. Units come from the CSV header, not from structured paper parse.

Observed Scenario 1 Case B (session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**), 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Dropping a PDF into the workspace should either:
  - enqueue it for paper-reader parsing (same as the dedicated paper input), **or**
  - clearly label the upload as “file only / not paper-parsed” so users do not assume literature extraction ran.
- If Drop files is intentionally file-only, the empty/paper UI should not imply paper intake for that artifact.

## Actual

PDF is a workspace file only. Paper reader stays **0 parsed**. Structured literature extraction does not run on Drop-files PDFs.

## Priority

**Medium–High** for any “upload paper + analyze” flow; easy to misread as a successful paper ingest.

## Related

Not the same as empty-session CSV intro (#328). Speaks to intake path consistency between Drop files and paper-reader.

## Problem
In the desktop app Model registry flow, if the **first** model connection attempt fails, fixing the model/provider settings and trying **Save & connect** again still fails. Only after **restarting ScienceDiscovery** does the same (corrected) configuration connect successfully.

## Expected
After the user corrects invalid or incomplete model settings, a subsequent **Save & connect** (or equivalent reconnect) should succeed without requiring a full ScienceDiscovery restart, as long as the corrected config is valid.

     3. Correct the settings to a known-good configuration; Save & connect again **without** restarting ScienceDiscovery.
     4. Restart ScienceDiscovery; open Model registry and Save & connect with the same corrected settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Step 3 succeeds (or fails only with a fresh, accurate error for a still-bad config). Requiring step 4 for an otherwise valid config is a fail.

items.body:
## Summary

On the L5 real E2E run ([38734441039](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38734441039), commit `768688fa`, product code identical to `844947da`, judge `deepseek-flash` at temperature 0), BiomniBench-da-13-3 and BiomniBench-da-14-1 scores move much more than the other research cases. Each case was scored four times (three initial runs plus one rerun of the low attempt). All four scores count.

| Case | Scores | Mean |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| da-13-3 | 78 / 59 / 78 / 100 | 78.75 |
| da-14-1 | 83 / 100 / 100 / 93 | 94.00 |

The spread is not one cause. Some points move because a later answer actually meets a written requirement. The rest move because the same kind of answer receives different grades. This issue tracks the case and rubric changes. It does not ask for another research rerun.

The formal L5 numbers are in the test-result comment on #343: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/343#issuecomment-6207027843

## What changed across the four grades

The judge reads both the trace and the answer. Each of the eight answers was scored once. Levels below are A/B across the four runs, in order.

| Case | Criterion | Levels | Where the points go | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| da-13-3 | 3, rank significant proteins by absolute effect size | B / B / B / A | rerun +13 | The runs. The first three rank by adjusted p. The rerun lists a top set by absolute estimate for each phenotype in the trace. |
| da-13-3 | 4, biological explanation of the shared proteins | A / B / A / A | run 2 −14 | Ambiguous rubric, applied inconsistently. None of the four answers states the mechanism the A level asks for. Run 2 is the one marked B. |
| da-13-3 | 5, place the result back in the study frame | B / B / B / A | rerun +9 | The runs. Only the rerun states that the proteome tracks a treatment-driven increase in fat mass and that body composition and hormones act together, with a citation. |
| da-13-3 | 6, source reliability | A / B / A / A | run 2 −5 | Ambiguous rubric. All four answers have a reference list and some unsourced functional claims. Run 2 has the fullest citations and is the only B. |
| da-14-1 | Not the rubric's 21 endotype scores | 38, 26, 38, then 37 columns reduced to 26 | no score gap by itself | Both. The task text the agent sees does not say 21, and the rubric does not name which 21 columns. Every run still fails to narrow to that set. |
| da-14-1 | 1, load and check the score columns | B / A / A / B | run 1 and the rerun, −7 each | Ambiguous rubric. A 38-column answer is B once and A once. A 26-column answer is also A once and B once. The completeness notes are similar. |
| da-14-1 | 2, correlation matrix | B / A / A / A | run 1 −10 | Ambiguous rubric. Runs 1 and 3 both compute a full 38×38 Spearman matrix. One is marked B for not being 21×21. The other is marked A for being broader than 21×21. |

Point values used for the check: da-13-3 criteria 1–6 are A/B = 15/8, 15/7, 25/12, 27/13, 18/9, 0/−5. da-14-1 criteria 1–2 are A/B = 15/8, 20/10. Each scorecard sums to the published total.

## What this does not separate

Temperature is 0 and each request returned on the first try, but every request had a different trace and answer. That does not measure how often the judge would change its grade given the same input.

## Follow-up

- Do not rerun the research tasks to chase these scores.
- Score each of the eight existing answers several times, unchanged, and report how often the grade moves.
- Name the 21 endotype-score columns in the task text or in the rubric.
- Rewrite da-13-3 criteria 4 and 6 so an A is a checklist a second reader can mark without guessing.

Evidence is the `quality-scorecard.json`, `answer.txt`, and `trace.md` artifacts on run 38734441039 (`real-e2e-evidence-a2-research-1-r1` and `-r3` for da-13-3 attempt 2; `real-e2e-evidence-a1-research-2-r1` and `-r4` for da-14-1 attempt 1; the other two attempts are the matching `-r1` artifacts).

> Converted from bug → feature per HongyeZhou (2026-10-27): this is a product/UX presentation improvement, not a hard defect.

## Feature request
When tool calls fail then recover mid-run, the default timeline narrative shows raw **failed** tool cards before a later success. #335 expected a clearer “retrying with fixed args” (or equivalent) presentation for the same logical operation. PRs #345 / #551 addressed missing required `prompt` on `task` before a deep createSubagent throw; they did **not** deliver the general failure→retry UI narrative (S6).

## Expected
When there is clear association evidence that a later call is a bounded correction of the same logical tool operation, the UI updates in place (or equivalent merged presentation): default view is a concise result; attempt count / errors / recovery detail are available on demand. Unrecoverable failures keep a clear reason. Real execution history and audit evidence are not rewritten as pure success. Do not blindly replay side-effecting operations to reduce cards.

## Verification cases

1. **In-place recovery presentation**
   - **Preconditions:** A recoverable invalid-argument or soft-fail path that retries within one logical operation (browser or hermetic UI fixture).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Trigger a tool call that fails then succeeds on a bounded correction.
     2. Inspect the timeline/card for that operation.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Default view is not a stack of contradictory failed+success cards for the same operation; recovery state/result is shown in place; history of attempts remains inspectable; independent operations are not wrongly merged.

2. **Side-effect boundary**
   - **Preconditions:** A tool invocation that may have already executed with side effects before observation failed.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Observe recovery/UI merge behavior.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** No blind resubmit of committed side-effecting work solely to tidy the timeline; audit/failure records stay consistent.

## Context
- Env: _not provided_ for a fresh UI journey this filing; scope from #335 expected narrative and product phase-3 note on that Issue.
- Refs: Parent #335; PRs #345 / #551 (merged) for prompt-path only.
- Notes: Related UX umbrella #330 is adjacent (timeline hierarchy) but not a substitute for this recovery-presentation bug.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #102](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/102) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

### 🚀 Background Description

ScienceDiscovery’s primary entry today is local `serve` plus a browser UI (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`). The agent runs inside the product’s own control plane: the Web UI submits work, the API orchestrates Runs, the sandbox executes code, and MCP connects external tools. Users who already live in Zed, VS Code, JetBrains, or other editors cannot plug ScienceDiscovery in as a standard coding agent; they have to leave the editor and open a browser.

The [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) is an open standard for communication between editors (Clients) and coding agents. Zed published it in 2025; it is now an Apache 2.0 standard. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 (typically over stdio) for initialization, sessions, prompt turns, streaming updates, permissions, and cancellation — LSP for coding agents. Any compliant Client can drive any compliant Agent without a per-editor private integration. The stable wire protocol is **ACP v1** (`protocolVersion` negotiated in `initialize`). ACP v2 docs shipped as Draft in 2026-07 and are **not** the default target of this issue.

ACP and the product’s existing MCP sit on different layers and do not replace each other:

| | ACP | MCP (already in the product) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connects | editor / IDE ↔ coding agent | agent / host ↔ tool and data servers |
| Standardizes | how to launch, drive, and render an agent session | how to discover and call external tools |

This repository has no ACP implementation (no `agent-client-protocol`, no stdio JSON-RPC agent entry). Nearby issues are not this work:

- GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23) / the HTTP CLI: a **CLI client of `serve`**, not an editor↔agent protocol;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): an internal pluggable-capability / Pending Mode design, not external ACP.

User-observable outcome: in an ACP-capable editor, select ScienceDiscovery, prompt against the current workspace, see streaming output and tool calls, approve sensitive actions through ACP permissions, and still use the product’s sandbox, scientific connectors, and Skills — without opening the browser.

### Design Ideas

**Default role: ScienceDiscovery as an ACP Agent** (the editor is the Client). That matches “put the research agent inside standard editors.” Whether to also be an ACP Client (drive Claude Code / Gemini CLI / etc. from this product’s UI) is an open question and must not block phase 1.

Phase 1 should implement the **ACP v1 baseline methods** (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview):

1. **Transport**: the editor spawns this product’s ACP subprocess; JSON-RPC 2.0 newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout. Do not bind ACP to the existing HTTP `:4310` control plane by default.
2. **Lifecycle**: `initialize` (version and capability negotiation) → optional `authenticate` → `session/new` (or `session/load` when advertised) → `session/prompt` / `session/update` / `session/cancel`.
3. **Session mapping**: one ACP session maps to a recoverable Project/Session/Run context in the product; workspace paths follow ACP’s absolute-path rule.
4. **Permissions and sandbox**: Client `session/request_permission` and optional `fs/*` / `terminal/*` must align with existing permission cards and the Bubblewrap/Seatbelt sandbox. The default security posture must not be looser than the Web UI; ACP must not become a bypass around the sandbox.
5. **Capability advertisement**: `initialize` must report only capabilities that are actually implemented (`loadSession`, image prompts, MCP passthrough, …). Research-specific features (literature connectors, artifacts, memory graph) that have no v1 field should use ACP `_meta` / `_`-prefixed custom methods and be documented — do not invent a private JSON-RPC.
6. **Discoverability (can follow)**: ship a launch command and manifest editors can configure. Listing in the [ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) is not decided.

**Alternatives considered**

- Extra subcommands on the HTTP CLI (#23) without ACP methods: editors still cannot connect.
- ACP Client only, never an Agent: users still cannot use ScienceDiscovery inside a standard editor.
- Wrapping the product’s private event stream and calling it ACP: no interoperability with Zed / VS Code / JetBrains clients.
- Targeting ACP v2 Draft as the only goal in phase 1: v2 is still draft; implement against the stable spec at implementation time, with v1 as the default acceptance line.

**Open questions (need a decision before implementation)**

- Whether to ship an ACP Client in the same phase;
- Whether phase 1 lists the agent in the ACP Registry (the registry currently requires authentication support);
- How ACP cwd / workspace maps to a product Project, and whether a full Gateway/Runner stack is required when `serve` is not already running;
- Whether permission prompts are owned by the editor’s ACP UI or still fall back to in-product permission cards.

### Involved Public APIs

- **ACP wire protocol**: expose ACP v1 JSON-RPC over stdio to editors. This is a new external contract, not an alias of the existing REST/SSE API.
- **Existing HTTP control plane**: may be reused locally for Project/Session/Run, but users must not have to open a browser before ACP works. If the ACP process embeds or starts the control plane, that should be one launch command.
- **MCP**: stays on the agent↔tools axis; do not multiplex MCP stdio and ACP stdio on the same pipe.
- **No anonymous public ACP service**: default remains trusted local/workstation use, consistent with “not a multi-user production service.”

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Launcher / CLI: add an ACP Agent entry alongside `serve` and GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23); they do not replace each other;
- Session / Run / permissions / sandbox: ACP prompt turns must hit the same execution and governance path;
- MCP: an ACP session should still use configured MCP servers;
- Web UI: not a required surface for this issue; whether ACP sessions appear in the web session list is undecided;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): the internal capability framework may be reused if the composition layer is in the way; acceptance is external ACP interop, not the internal plugin protocol.

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Protocol conformance**

- [ ] Complete `initialize` against a reference ACP Client (or the official schema / SDK): negotiate v1 (or the then-stable version); advertised capabilities match behavior;
- [ ] `session/new` → `session/prompt` completes one scientific turn (user message, streaming `session/update`, explicit stop reason);
- [ ] `session/cancel` interrupts an in-flight prompt turn;
- [ ] Privileged tool calls go through `session/request_permission` and do not run when denied;
- [ ] Errors use JSON-RPC 2.0 `error` objects; notifications have no response.

**Product constraints**

- [ ] Python / shell execution stays in the existing sandbox; the ACP path is not looser than the Web UI;
- [ ] Tokens, API keys, and session bodies do not leak into ACP logs or unauthenticated client traffic;
- [ ] Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

**Interop / user journey**

- [ ] In at least one real ACP Client (e.g. Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): configure the launch command → prompt against the open workspace → see streaming text and at least one tool call;
- [ ] Focused unit tests for JSON-RPC dispatch, failed version negotiation, and unauthenticated calls if `authenticate` is enabled;
- [ ] Docs include a Client configuration example (launch command, workspace, auth).

### Additional Information

Public spec and repos:

- Protocol overview: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview
- Schema / reference implementation: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol
- Registry: https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry

The product entry remains `./ScienceDiscovery serve` plus the browser. This issue adds an editor-spawned ACP Agent process, not another private chat protocol.

## Problem

PR #552 delivers standalone (inbox / 最近会话) chats and project folds, but membership is fixed at create time. Users still cannot move an existing recent conversation into a new or existing project without losing history or artifacts. That remaining acceptance item from #305 is out of scope for #552.

## Expected

A reader can move a standalone (recent / inbox) conversation into a new or existing project, and optionally move between projects or back to Recent, without losing messages, artifacts, or workspace accounting. Navigation and session lists stay consistent (no duplicate rows).

## Verification cases

1. **Move into existing project**
   - **Preconditions:** One Recent/inbox session with messages and at least one artifact; project P already exists.
   - **Steps:** From that session, choose move into project P (or equivalent UI).
   - **Expected / pass:** Session appears under P; history and artifacts intact; no longer listed under 最近会话; session bar / active project shows P.

2. **Move into newly created project**
   - **Preconditions:** One standalone session with history.
   - **Steps:** Move → create project with name only → confirm.
   - **Expected / pass:** Project created; session inside it; history/artifacts intact; gone from Recent.

3. **Move between projects / back to Recent**
   - **Preconditions:** Session already under a project.
   - **Steps:** Move to another project, then back to Recent (if supported).
   - **Expected / pass:** Membership updates; no duplicate rows in sidebar; workspace path and accounting remain consistent.

4. **E2E first-run remainder of #305**
   - **Preconditions:** Fresh user with no projects.
   - **Steps:** Start chat without a project → later move that chat into a project.
   - **Expected / pass:** Covers the #305 E2E acceptance remainder that #552 intentionally deferred.

## Context

- Refs #305 (remaining AC: organize / move conversations into projects later).
- Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/552 (`bde9143`); not blocking that PR.

## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话开启 Automatic review（`reviewerAutomaticReviewEnabled=true`，`reviewMode=auto`，specialist=`quick`）。

- 第一轮 run 结束后主交付（4 实例真实 `predictions.npy`）**缺失**，报告写 blocked
- Artifact：`REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 触发 `reviewer_checkpoint` → **PASSED / ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED**，findings 空
- 审阅 JSON 仅 citation 类 check（与文献 case 的 Quick 行为一致，参见 #414）
- 续跑产出真实 cl3/cl5/mop_sc npy 并改写报告后，**未自动重审**；磁盘上旧 ACCEPT 仍对应「blocked」叙事

## 问题是什么

1. **交付物缺失仍 ACCEPT**：复现任务的成功标准是 `output/{instance}/predictions.npy`，Quick 几乎只看 citation 格式，拦不住「没复现成功」。
2. **报告/审阅不同步**：工件已更新，Automatic review 不因新版本自动失效或重跑；用户看到的仍是过期 ACCEPT。

## 我们怎么规避的

- 不以 review ACCEPT 作为复现成功判据；宿主侧用 numpy 核对 npy shape / K，并手改 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 写清真实现状。
- 体验结论单独记录，不依赖审阅绿勾。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 复现 / 计算类报告：Quick 之外至少校验「声明的交付路径是否存在、非空」；缺失则 **不能** ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED。
2. Artifact 新版本落盘后：旧 review 标记 stale，或自动触发重审；UI 明确「审阅对应的是哪一版」。
3. 与 #414（文献 claim fidelity）区分但可共用：按 artifact 类型选审查准则，而不是一律 citation-only。

## 相关

- #414 Bug: Quick automatic review accepts literature reports on citation format only

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## Symptom

`PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` still accepts `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, and `assessorActivity` / `assessorStability` / `assessorSustainability`. Those values pass bounds validation, are written to the catalog, are returned verbatim by `GET /api/settings/idea-tree`, and `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` still exposes them to callers.

No research run ever reads them. The engine overwrites all of them from the research template and the exploration intensity before the run starts. A caller therefore gets a completely silent no-op: the request returns 200, the value reads back unchanged, the type definition says it is configurable — and nothing about the run changes.

## Reproduction

1. `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` with body `{"maxRounds": 10, "candidatesPerRound": 5}` → 200, and the response echoes `maxRounds: 10`, `candidatesPerRound: 5`.
2. `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` → still 10 and 5.
3. Start an Idea Tree research run with `explorationIntensity` set to `standard`.
4. The run does 3 rounds and asks for at most 3 candidates per round — the `standard` preset. The 10 and the 5 have no effect, and nothing reports that.

**Expected:** either the two values take effect, or the endpoint rejects them / says they are no longer configurable.
**Actual:** accepted, validated, persisted, read back, then silently discarded.

## Mechanism

The budget fields are overwritten wholesale by the intensity preset:

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:149` builds the run's settings with `apply_intensity(c.settings.model_dump(), c.settings.explorationIntensity)`.
- `apply_intensity` in `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/templates.py:51` returns `{**settings, **INTENSITIES[intensity], 'explorationIntensity': intensity}`. The preset is spread last, so it always wins over whatever the caller stored.
- `INTENSITIES` supplies `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound` and `maxSearchRounds` (plus `maxActiveDirections`, `explorationSlots` and `candidateConcurrency`, which are preset-only and were never part of the schema).

The assessor configuration is superseded by the template instead:

- `assessors()` in `research.py` returns the assessor list straight from the template snapshot, and `role_prompt()` resolves assessor roles from the same place.
- Scoring uses `weights = [spec['weight'] for spec in self.assessors()]` (`research.py:341`), so the weights also come from the template.
- The three assessor fields in settings therefore take part in no assessment at all.

The write path's validation is fully intact, which is precisely the problem: `normalizeIdeaTreeSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts:519`) bounds `maxRounds` to 1..100 and `candidatesPerRound` to 1..20, then persists them.

## Scope

One schema now mixes two kinds of field, and the type definitions give no way to tell them apart:

**Dead (overwritten or superseded)**
`maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, `assessorActivity`, `assessorStability`, `assessorSustainability` (including their `weight`, `systemPrompt` and `scoringCriteria`).

**Still effective**
`maxDepth`, `maxNodes`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `scoreDirection`, `designSystemPrompt`, `aggregatorSystemPrompt`, `propagateInsightSystemPrompt`.

## Traces the migration left behind

1. **The assessor weights are validated twice and read zero times.** On the TypeScript side, `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:568` throws `Assessor weights must sum to 1.0` when all three weights are supplied. On the Python side, the `Settings.weights` model validator in `research_service.py` requires `Assessment weights must sum to 1` and additionally checks the type and length of `systemPrompt` / `scoringCriteria`. Both guard data that has no reader.
2. **The front end kept an empty validation hook.** `ideaTreeWeightsValid()` (`apps/web/src/IdeaTreeSettingsEditor.tsx:29`) now returns `true` for any draft, yet it is still the precondition on the save action at `apps/web/src/App.tsx:2611`.
3. **The shapes do not even line up.** Settings hard-code three assessors — activity, stability, sustainability — while the default template `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1` has `scientificValidity`, `evidenceReadiness` and `feasibility`. Only `water-treatment-materials/v1` matches the settings' three.

## Suggested resolution

Two directions, depending on whether template + intensity is the intended contract:

1. **It is.** Remove the overwritten fields from `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest` and `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails`, stop persisting them, and delete the now-unreachable weight validation (both the TypeScript and the Python copy) along with the `ideaTreeWeightsValid` stub. The interface would then say what the runtime does.
2. **It is not.** Make `apply_intensity` treat the preset as defaults rather than overrides — fill only the fields the caller did not set explicitly, so explicit configuration keeps working.

Either way, a test that pins the persisted settings against the settings the engine actually runs with would be worth adding; otherwise the next change to an intensity preset drifts the same silent way.

## Note

The mocked E2E journey `journey-idea-tree-fixture` used to configure a run through the budget inputs that were removed from the settings pane. It has been rewritten separately to configure template + intensity. This issue is about the API/schema contract itself, not that test.

Tracked on GitCode as https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/100.
items.title: Idea Tree settings: budget and assessor fields are still validated and persisted, but the runtime always overwrites them from the template/intensity preset

## 范围与证据

汇总 [2026-10-24 Nightly run 40121906605](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605) 的三项剩余问题。运行版本：`9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`。

#514 / #515 修复的 Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 依赖准备已通过，本次不再作为阻塞项。以下区分实际运行结果与源码诊断，不据此认定所有 main CI 都失败。

## 1. real research-8 的会话标题断言未跟随显示规则更新

[失败 job 120955308760](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955308760) 已实际执行该用例，在点击 Add session 后失败：

- [`issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts:221`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/test/issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts#L219-L228) 期望 `Untitled session`，实际为 `Untitled session 2`。
- #510 已合入同一 Project 多个未命名会话显示序号的行为，实际标题与该规则一致。当前证据支持“测试期望过时”，不能据此认定产品的计划/子任务功能损坏。
- 此前的计划、follow-up、reload 断言已通过；失败后的切回原会话及位置保持断言尚未执行，不能算通过。
- #511 仍讨论编号集合与排序的 UX 口径，本 issue 不替它决定方案，只修复测试对已实现显示规则的错误假设。

## 2. 已执行失败的分片被汇总成 NOT_RUN

[research-8 结果 artifact 12574909042](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12574909042) 的 `e2e-real/tagged/summary.json` 明确记录：

- planned=1、executed=1、passed=0、failed=1；
- 该身份的 `outcome=FAIL`。

但 [汇总 job 120992446082](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120992446082) 输出 executed=18/19、passed=18，并将该用例标为 `NOT_RUN`。

源码诊断：[`.ci/real-report.mjs:19-24`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/.ci/real-report.mjs#L19-L24) 在失败分片的 `results.push(...summary.results)` 之前抛出 `SHARD_FAILED`，丢掉了其已执行结果。需要保留身份、版本、digest 等校验通过的失败证据，同时继续让 gate 失败。该运行应准确呈现 19 executed、18 passed、1 failed，而不是将执行失败混同为未运行。

## 3. 两项 UT 等待完成超时，原因待查

[UT job 120955273894](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955273894)：4754 planned / 4754 executed / 4752 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped。

[UT artifact 12572160563](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12572160563) 中的实际失败：

- `ut/tagged/group-279/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` 的 `a measured run is staged before the sidecar is asked to start`，报 `timed out waiting for the run to settle`。
- `ut/tagged/group-343/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/server.test.ts` 的 `running sessions accept queued runs and start them after the active run completes`，报等待 run 进入 `completed` 超时。

[同一 SHA 较早的 UT job 120785725594](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40064771478/job/120785725594) 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上 4754/4754 通过。现有证据不能区分测试时序、环境或产品状态推进问题，不认定为负载抖动或确定性回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 会话切换测试按当前显示规则及明确的 Session 身份校验，补齐“新增会话 → 切回原会话 → 原计划/时间线位置保持”的验证；不删除原行为断言。
- [ ] 为汇总器补充“分片实际执行但失败”的无模型回归测试，保留 executed/failed 计数和失败身份；身份不匹配、缺失、重复、跳过等情况仍不得放行。
- [ ] 使用上述已有结果验证汇总应为 19 executed / 18 passed / 1 failed，退出码仍非零；不通过跳过失败分片把 gate 改绿。
- [ ] 分别定位两项 UT 超时，保留最后运行状态及相关事件等诊断证据，补充针对性回归验证；仅延长超时或重跑成功不能作为已定位的证据。

本 issue 基于已有日志、artifact 与源码核对，未触发新的付费模型调用或 CI 重跑。

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.
items.title: bug: Embedded JiuwenSwarm must not adopt standalone config via env or discovery

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
PR #460 isolates the embedded JiuwenSwarm default local runtime under `$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm` and documents Docker’s persisted HOME layout. Local coexistence was verified; the **Docker persisted-volume restart** journey was **BLOCKED** (no container engine/socket on the author host) and remains an explicit leftover acceptance item on #257 / #460.

## Expected
After a container restart that keeps the documented persisted volume, ScienceDiscovery’s embedded Swarm registry, workspaces, and related runtime state remain under the SD-owned layout, still isolated from any standalone Swarm data, and SD continues to use its own instance endpoints without adopting a sibling standalone instance.

## Verification cases

1. **Docker volume restart persistence**
   - **Preconditions:** Container-capable host; ScienceDiscovery Docker path with persisted volume as documented after #460; disposable standalone Swarm data available to prove non-interference if co-tested.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start SD via the Docker path; record embedded registry/workspace identity and a distinguishing config marker.
     2. Restart the container with the same persisted volume.
     3. Confirm SD still binds to the same embedded instance data and does not read/write standalone Swarm registry/config.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Persisted SD state survives restart; isolation from standalone Swarm holds; no silent reconnect to another Swarm service.

## Context
- Env: Author host for #460 lacked container engine/socket; residual Docker journey _not provided_ here beyond that BLOCKED note.
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Local default-namespace isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks Docker restart verification only.

## Overview

This issue is the **October 2026 release calendar** for the ScienceDiscovery community. It is intended to serve as the **pinned, single source of truth** for release milestones and community review meetings.

**Key milestones**
- **Oct 10:** `v0.3.0` release kickoff and `v0.3.0-rc1` requirements review.
- **Oct 16:** `v0.3.0-rc1` release exit.
- **Oct 30:** `v0.3.0` official release exit.

| Requirement | Scope | Target release(s) | Tracking issue | Owner | Review level |

## October schedule

## Community review meetings

The community review meetings on **Oct 13, 20, 22, and 27** cover:

- **Design review** — review technical design and architecture changes.
- **Code review** — discuss implementation quality, correctness, and readiness to merge.

## Purpose

Track the remaining research-team budget and cancellation integration validation for v0.4.0, split from #239 at the user's request. The classification fix in #239 is implemented by merged PR #426 (`7b93f92e898dca1798595fd2fa320c23887e1565`). Closing #239 does not mean the full BRCA1 journey has been revalidated.

## Existing evidence

On a post-merge snapshot (`0c6fa3fb47ccac3b69e870ac7fddc4ee00a51853`), these commands passed 61/61 tests with no paid model calls:

```sh
node --import tsx --test test/helpers/real-delivery.unit.ts scripts/real-e2e-scoring.test.mjs .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs
```

They cover active delivery classification, terminal missing-output failures, scoring, and safe result packaging. They do not execute the full team-spec timeout branch or establish its persisted metrics/cancellation outcomes. PR #426's L3 evidence is not a replacement for the L4 BRCA1 journey.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add and run a deterministic integration test using a local model stub and a short budget, exercising the actual team journey timeout path rather than only helper functions.
- [ ] Verify persisted `team-metrics.json` distinguishes budget exhaustion (`integration=timed_out`) from terminal delivery failure and retains budget, elapsed duration, cancellation request, shutdown outcome, and actual terminal status.
- [ ] Verify cleanup stops the main run, children, pending wakeups, and relevant executions; retain diagnostic evidence on cleanup failure.
- [ ] Cover the terminal race: cancellation coincides with completion, while budget-exhaustion attribution remains correct.
- [ ] Preserve normal delivery contracts: successful completion requires readable, nonempty final artifacts; terminal missing/empty/unreadable output remains a delivery failure.
- [ ] Run or inspect a post-fix L4/Nightly `TC-E2E-01` BRCA1 journey at its configured team budget. Record the immutable SHA, command/configuration, final artifacts, persisted metrics, cancellation outcomes where applicable, and actual passed/failed/blocked/skipped counts. A successful normal completion alone does not cover the timeout branch.

## Execution constraints

The current instruction permits only verification without paid model calls. Do not start a billable model/judge run without authorization; an already scheduled post-fix Nightly may provide the real-journey evidence. Keep unexecuted scenarios explicitly pending.

## Scope

This is validation follow-up for v0.4.0. Any newly discovered product defect should be documented with reproduction evidence and linked here. Related: #239, #426.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What happened

A long real research run can end with only this text on the page:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · interaction round execution failed
```

The sentence before the dot is `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`. The detail after the dot is the fixed string `interaction round execution failed`. In the DeepAgent interaction-round handler that string replaces the caught exception: the handler logs the exception and returns `error_code=round_execution_error` with that fixed message. The original exception does not reach the page or the E2E log.

Observed runs, both with an empty final answer and `delivery.status` `"failed"`:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-62**, 23.7 minutes. One subagent completed. The session had `literature_sources.json` and showed 271K usage and 20 executions. The required `deepresearchbench-62.md` was not delivered. Run status was `failed`.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`6d3c49a8`), **DRB-58**, 21.0 minutes. Run status was `failed`. The session had `literature_sources.json`, `hgt_animals_sources.md`, and `hgt_plants_sources.md`. One child was `completed` and another was still `running`. A PubMed call had returned HTTP 429 from `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov`. Literature-connector 429s are already tracked in #208.

The same DRB-62 passed on the beta run (36.1 minutes), and the same DRB-58 passed on the main run (51.0 minutes). The model and gateway had already served those sessions for about 20 minutes, so this is not a wrong API key or a missing model id.

## Expected

The failed round keeps the underlying exception message (gateway status, tool error, or runtime exception) in the run error that the page and the test can read. A round that ran for many minutes is not described only as a model-configuration rejection.

## Evidence limits

The server log for these two runs was not retrieved, so the exception that was swallowed is not known. The page text and the run status are known.
items.title: bug: A failed model round is shown only as "interaction round execution failed"

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
items.title: [Bug]: Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

### Problem

2. **The website installation page lacks a version selector and defaults to an outdated version.** Version 0.3 is available, but the installation page still defaults to 0.2. Users cannot select a release version directly on the page and may install an older version unintentionally.

- Default to the latest stable release, currently 0.3.
- Keep download links and installation commands consistent with the selected version.
- Update the default version when a new stable release becomes available.

- [ ] The website installation page provides a version selector.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Background

We want to automate the workflow from issue submission through code changes, review, and PR merge. This requires clear repository conventions so contributors and automation can determine whether an issue is ready for implementation, whether a change meets its acceptance criteria, and whether a PR is ready to merge.

The existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers development setup, test commands, E2E testing, and some PR requirements. Extend it with issue, commit, review, and merge conventions, supported by templates and checks that all contributors can use.

### Scope

#### 1. Issue requirements

Provide templates for feature requests, bug reports, and other supported issue types. Identify required and conditional fields:

- Background, the problem to solve, and the expected outcome.
- Functional specifications, including inputs, outputs, behavior, boundary conditions, and applicable compatibility requirements.
- Scope and explicit exclusions.
- Verifiable acceptance scenarios with preconditions, actions, and expected results. Cover success, failure, permissions, and recovery where relevant.
- Reproduction steps, environment, actual behavior, and expected behavior for bug reports.
- Dependencies, open questions, and blockers that must be resolved before implementation.

Include a complete example and define when an issue is ready for development. Clarify ambiguities that affect implementation or acceptance before work begins. Update the issue when the specification changes during implementation.

#### 2. Commit and PR requirements

Document branch, commit, and PR conventions:

- Follow the existing fork and target-branch workflow, and define naming and commit message formats.
- Link the PR to its issue and explain the reason, resulting behavior, and scope.
- Map each issue acceptance criterion to its implementation and validation result.
- Provide reproducible test commands, results, and supporting evidence. Distinguish tests that were not run, failed, were blocked, or were skipped.
- Describe compatibility impact, configuration changes, data migration, and rollback where applicable.
- Update affected documentation and follow the existing release label requirements.

#### 3. Review and merge requirements

Provide a shared review checklist and define:

- Checks for specification compliance, acceptance coverage, correctness, module boundaries, and applicable security and compatibility requirements.
- The distinction between blocking findings and suggestions, including how findings are resolved.
- Responsibilities for automated and human review, including approval authority.
- Which checks and approvals must be repeated after a PR changes.
- Conditions for entering the merge queue and completing the merge, consistent with the existing CI and `merge-gate` mechanism.

#### 4. Rule checks

Maintain a rule list that states applicability, verification method, execution stage, and failure handling for each rule. Include:

- Required issue and PR information and their linkage.
- Type checks, tests, user-perspective E2E testing, and documentation checks.
- License headers, sensitive information, temporary files, and generated files.
- Module dependency boundaries and compatibility requirements.
- Required checks, review decisions, and unresolved blockers.

Enforce rules through templates or CI where they can be checked programmatically. Provide explicit instructions for rules that require human judgment. Unavailable test prerequisites must be reported as blocked. Document the reason, approver, and follow-up for any exception.

### Deliverables

- Extend `CONTRIBUTING.md` as the common entry point, linking to separate documents where needed.
- Add issue templates, a PR template, and a review checklist.
- Provide a feature issue example and a corresponding PR acceptance report example.
- Map rules to automated checks, distinguishing existing checks, checks added in this work, and follow-up work.
- Resolve duplicated or conflicting guidance and identify where each rule is maintained.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contributors can find issue, commit, PR, review, and merge requirements from one entry point.
- [ ] The feature template requires functional specifications and verifiable acceptance scenarios; the bug template requires reproduction details.
- [ ] The PR template requires an issue link, per-criterion acceptance results, and test evidence.
- [ ] The review checklist defines blocking findings, approval responsibilities, and re-review requirements.
- [ ] Merge conditions are consistent with the existing CI, merge queue, and `merge-gate` contract.
- [ ] Important rules specify applicability, verification, and failure or exception handling.
- [ ] At least one complete issue-to-PR example is included.
- [ ] New or changed templates and automated checks are validated, and documentation checks pass.

This issue covers the guidelines, templates, and agreed checks. Implementation of the complete automation system can be tracked separately.
items.title: Complete contribution guidelines for the workflow from issues to PR merge

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
A Windows durability fix for CAS directory `fsync` (`O_RDWR` on `win32` because `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle) and `toNamespacedPath` for SQLite paths landed inside the conversational-configuration protocol PR (#553), mixed with unrelated schema/protocol work. On Linux the `win32` branch is never taken, so CI here cannot exercise the failure mode (silently weaker directory sync if the open/handle is wrong).

## Expected
- CAS Windows durable-directory sync ships in its own small PR (or clearly scoped commit series) with Windows verification attached.
- Configuration/protocol PRs do not carry unrelated CAS durability changes.

## Verification cases
1. **Writable-directory sync on Windows**
   - Preconditions: Windows host; CAS `VersionStore` / `RefStore` initialized on a normal NTFS directory.
   - Steps: Create/update a live ref that triggers `syncDirectory`; confirm no throw from `open(..., O_RDWR|O_DIRECTORY)` + `handle.sync()`.
   - Expected / pass: Operation succeeds; refs.sqlite and object dirs remain consistent after process kill mid-write (WAL + FULL sync still hold).
2. **Long / namespaced path**
   - Preconditions: Windows; store path that needs `\\?\` / namespaced form (deep or near-MAX_PATH tree).
   - Steps: Open `RefStore` / lease DBs via the same helpers.
   - Expected / pass: `DatabaseSync(toNamespacedPath(...))` opens; no path-not-found solely from missing namespace prefix.
3. **Negative — read-only directory**
   - Preconditions: Directory without write ACL for the process.
   - Steps: Trigger `syncDirectory`.
   - Expected / pass: Failure is loud (thrown/propagated), not a silent no-op sync; caller sees the error.
4. **Linux unchanged**
   - Preconditions: Linux CI/dev.
   - Steps: Same CAS unit/integration paths as today.
   - Expected / pass: Still uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`; no behavioral change.

## Context
Refs #553 (CAS hunks in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`, `workspace-lease.ts`, `workspace-lifecycle.ts`). Spotted during review of the four-PR configuration stack; out of scope for the shared configuration protocol.
items.title: CAS: isolate Windows durable-directory sync (O_RDWR + toNamespacedPath) from feature stacks

## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #91](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/91) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Start the server and confirm "I can actually run analyses now".

## What I saw instead

- On Linux, when sandbox (bwrap) probing fails (e.g. the host disables unprivileged user namespaces), `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` only prints a `WARNING` line; `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` ignores the result, keeps starting, and finally prints `ScienceDiscovery is ready at ...`.
- The green connection dot in the top bar only means the frontend can talk to the local API (`Connection OK`). It says nothing about sandbox availability, the scientific Python environment, or model quota.
- Users believe everything is ready, then the run fails mid-analysis — often with raw low-level errors.

## Why this is confusing

"Ready" and the green light create false confidence; the failure happens only after the user has invested time writing a prompt and uploading data.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- When startup preflight finds the sandbox unusable, surface a prominent in-app notice ("analyses cannot run in this environment", with the reason) instead of a single terminal warning.
- Separate "frontend connected" from "compute ready" in the status indicator.
- Open question (needs a product decision): when compute is unavailable, should the app block new analyses entirely, or allow read-only browsing of past sessions and artifacts? The two strategies differ a lot in UX; decide before implementing.

Design note: the preflight result already exists in the startup chain (`runPreflight`); what is missing is exposing it to the web UI and layering the status display.
items.title: [Feature]: Sandbox unavailability only warns in the terminal while serve still reports ready; surface real compute readiness
