stale.author: Birfy
stale.body:
## Summary

Remote execution today reaches exactly two kinds of target: a machine you can SSH into, and a Slurm cluster. There is no way to run a job on cloud compute — no serverless GPU, no Kubernetes, no cloud VM. A researcher without an HPC allocation or a GPU workstation has no path to accelerated compute at all.

## Current state

The remote-compute model is already well factored, which is why this is an extension rather than a rewrite:

- `RemoteHostConnectionKind = "direct" | "ssh"` — the product either deploys a Runner SEA over SSH (verified host key, SHA-256 checked upload, HTTP tunneled through SSH) or connects to a runner the user started.
- `RemoteJobCard` carries `command`, `inputPaths`, `outputs`, `resources`, `targetAlias`, and `mode: "slurm" | "ssh"`.
- Jobs pass through an approval step (`approvedAt`) before anything runs.
- The host probe records CPU, memory, architecture, scratch paths, and whether Slurm is present — and accepts Linux only.
- Ascend NPU has a dedicated host broker.

So the concepts a cloud backend needs — a job card, declared inputs and outputs, a resource request, an approval gate, a target registry — all exist. What is missing is a third `mode`.

## Why it matters

The Slurm and SSH paths assume the user already has institutional compute. Everyone else — an individual researcher, a small lab, anyone whose cluster queue is full — is limited to the local sandbox. Meanwhile a comparable open-source workbench offers user-owned serverless GPU runs bound to an approved image digest, which is exactly the "I need a GPU for twenty minutes" case we cannot serve.

## Proposal

### 1. A `cloud` job mode behind the existing card + approval model

Define a small provider interface — submit(image digest, command, inputs, resources) → poll status → fetch outputs → report cost — and let backends implement it. The job card, the approval UI, and the output staging stay as they are.

### 2. First backend: Kubernetes Job

Recommended as the first implementation, ahead of any specific vendor:

- works against on-prem clusters, every major cloud, and local clusters for testing;
- no vendor lock-in in a project whose selling point is being model- and vendor-agnostic;
- resource requests, GPU scheduling, and namespaces map cleanly onto `RemoteJobResources`;
- credentials are the user's own kubeconfig, not a service we broker.

A serverless GPU provider can follow once the interface has one real implementation behind it.

### 3. Keep the security contract explicit

Cloud execution is a bigger step than SSH to a known host, because **data leaves the workstation**. So:

- the approval card must show exactly which files are uploaded, where, and to whose account;
- image references must be content-addressed digests, not mutable tags;
- credentials stay user-owned; the product must never proxy compute through an account we control;
- an air-gapped deployment must be able to disable cloud targets entirely;
- show an estimated cost before approval — the governance and quota machinery already exists to hang this on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A third job mode exists alongside `ssh` and `slurm`, reusing the current job-card and approval flow.
- [ ] At least one backend runs a GPU job end to end: inputs uploaded, job executed, outputs retrieved into the workspace.
- [ ] The approval card states what data leaves the machine and where it goes.
- [ ] Image references are digests.
- [ ] Cloud targets can be disabled by policy for restricted deployments.
- [ ] Failure modes — quota exceeded, image pull failure, job evicted — surface as actionable errors, not a stalled job.

## Open questions

- Kubernetes first, or a serverless GPU provider first for time-to-value?
- Should the cloud backend reuse the Runner SEA inside the container, or invoke the sandboxed executor directly?
- How should cost estimation work when pricing is provider-specific — a per-target rate the user configures?
- Does the Ascend NPU broker share this interface, or stay a separate path?
stale.title: [Feature]: Support general cloud compute as a third remote job mode

stale.author: hsliuustc0106
stale.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
stale.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

stale.author: Birfy
stale.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery can already evolve the things a user brings it — a program, a prompt, a protocol. It cannot evolve **itself**. I would like RSI support: given a dataset of tasks, search over the agent's own harness — system prompt fragments, specialist instructions, skill methodology, tool and skill selection — score each variant by running it against that dataset, and surface the winner for a human to adopt.

The search machinery for this already exists in `services/evolve`. What is missing is the candidate being the harness, the evaluation being an agent run, and a reviewed promotion step.

## What is already there

This is deliberately an extension, not a new engine.

- **The search sidecar**, `services/evolve`, runs on `agentdescent>=0.4.6` — `evolve()` / `async_evolve()`, `FlatPuct`, the ledger, the verifier and the policies — behind two engines: flat-PUCT tree search (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`).
- **Non-program candidates are first class.** `text_candidate.py` exists precisely because "a prompt or an abstract has no docstring", and `judge_domain.py` states its purpose plainly: it "is what makes `/evolve` work on things that are not programs over tables: a prompt, an abstract, a protocol, a plan". Evolving prompt text is not a new capability — it is the existing one pointed at a different file.
- **Four scoring seams**, already cut: `scorecard_domain` (a metric over a dataset), `test_gate_domain` (a suite's pass rate), `script_domain` (a scorer the drafting model writes), `judge_domain` (a rubric read by a model).
- **Anti-reward-hacking is already solved once.** `test_gate_domain` freezes in two layers — a proposal filter over `frozen` globs in the prompt, and enforcement below it — with the upstream note this issue should quote rather than restate: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."* That is the single most important property RSI needs, and the pattern is in the tree.
- **Held-out splitting exists.** `create_evolve_run` already accepts `caseSplit` with `gateGroups`, `rolloutGroups` and `testGroups`, which is the shape needed to keep a harness from overfitting the tasks it was tuned on.
- **Trajectories are recorded.** `packages/trajectory` captures per-session entries with the context blocks that were actually sent, which is the raw material for judging whether a harness change helped.
- **Parts of the harness are already frozen.** Built-in specialists reject edits to `instructions` / `description` / `name` / `connectorIds` / `enabledSkillIds`; only `enabled` is user-mutable. RSI has to open that door deliberately rather than by accident.

## What is missing

1. **The candidate is never the harness.** Today a candidate is one text-shaped artifact the user owns. The agent's own scaffolding lives elsewhere and is not reachable by a search: prompt assembly (`packages/context/src/prompt-renderer.ts`, `assembler.ts`), specialist instructions (`packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`), skill methodology (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), and the skill/connector selection for a run.

2. **There is no task-dataset scoring mode.** `scorecard_domain` scores a *program* over a table. RSI needs to score a *harness* over a set of tasks, where each evaluation is a full agent run with its own tool calls, sandboxed execution and artifacts. That is a different cost class and needs its own domain.

3. **There is no promotion path.** An improved harness must be diffable, reviewable, versioned and revertible. Nothing should ever be self-applied.

## Proposal

### 1. A harness candidate

A bundle rather than a single blob: prompt fragments, one or more specialist instruction sets, selected skills, and the run settings that go with them. The mutation prompt sees the bundle and rewrites part of it; the ledger records which part changed, so a win is attributable to something specific.

### 2. A `task_dataset` domain

A dataset entry is a task plus whatever the existing four modes need to score its outcome — a metric, a test suite, a scoring script, or a rubric. Evaluating one candidate means running the agent over the split and aggregating. Reuse `caseSplit` so the reported number comes from tasks the search did not tune against.

The honest problem here is cost: one candidate equals N agent runs, each with model calls and sandboxed execution. The design needs a budget per generation and an early-abandon policy, not just a score.

### 3. Freeze the things a self-improving search must not touch

Same two-layer shape `test_gate_domain` already uses, with a wider frozen set:

- the task dataset and its expected outcomes;
- the scorer, whichever mode it is;
- the permission, sandbox and approval layers — a harness that scores better by asking for fewer confirmations is not better;
- the evolve sidecar's own code and the freeze list itself.

A candidate that edits any of these is rejected at the proposal filter, not merely penalized.

### 4. Promotion is a human step

The winner lands as a reviewable proposal: a diff against the current harness, the score with its held-out number, and the trajectory evidence behind it. Adoption is explicit, versioned and revertible. The skill review flow and the built-in specialists' read-only rules already establish that shape; RSI should reuse it rather than invent a second one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search can take the agent's harness as its candidate, not only a user artifact.
- [ ] A task dataset can be supplied, and a candidate is scored by running the agent over it.
- [ ] The reported score comes from a held-out split.
- [ ] The dataset, the scorer, and the permission/sandbox layers are frozen against modification by the search, enforced at the proposal filter.
- [ ] An improved harness appears as a reviewable, versioned proposal and is never self-applied.
- [ ] Reverting to the previous harness is one action.
- [ ] A run states its budget and stops at it.

## Open questions

- Should a run evolve one specialist at a time, or the whole bundle? One at a time attributes wins more cleanly; the whole bundle can find interactions.
- Where does a task dataset live — a repository artifact, a workspace file, or a first-class store object?
- Which engine fits better? PUCT refines one starting point; OpenEvolve's islands keep diversity, which may matter more when a prompt change can be good in one dimension and harmful in another.
- What is the minimum dataset size where a win is believable rather than noise, given the non-determinism the judge mode already documents?
- Should this reuse `/evolve-design`'s checkpointed design conversation, or have its own entry point?

Related: [#50](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/50) — the engines can be started but not observed or stopped from the CLI, which matters more for a search whose evaluations are full agent runs.
stale.title: [Feature]: RSI — evolve the agent's own harness against a task dataset, reusing the agentdescent search

stale.author: zy95-12
stale.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.
stale.title: [RFC] Collect community requirements for E2E test scenarios

stale.author: zhaozhaozz
stale.body:
### Background

ScienceDiscovery does not have a recognizable product icon.

The browser tab has a title and no favicon. `apps/web/index.html` has no `rel="icon"` in `<head>`, so the product is indistinguishable from a generic page among bookmarks and tabs.

The in-app brand mark is a generic flask outline (`BrandIcon` in `apps/web/src/icons.tsx`) on an accent square. It fills the slot, but it is not a mark for this product, and it does not read at a 16px tab or bookmark size.

The README opens with a text title and a UI animation. It has no product mark.

### Expected

One product icon, the same mark in all of these places:

1. Browser favicon (at least 16×16 and 32×32, legible on both light and dark tab bars).
2. The in-app brand slot (today’s `.brand-mark`), replacing the generic flask outline.
3. The top of the English and Chinese READMEs, as a product mark. It does not replace the existing UI animation.

The mark has to stay recognizable at small sizes. Do not rely on hairline strokes alone. The drawing, colors, and whether it includes a wordmark are not decided here; this issue does not pre-select a design.

### Out of scope

- The icon is not a control that opens settings.
- The product name and copy stay as they are.
- A desktop or installer icon, if one is needed, belongs with [#34](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/34) (a native desktop window). It does not block the favicon and the in-app mark.

### Acceptance

- [ ] After opening the local web app, the browser tab shows the product icon, not the browser’s default page icon.
- [ ] The sidebar brand slot uses the same mark, not the generic flask outline.
- [ ] The English and Chinese READMEs show the same mark at the top, and the existing UI animation remains.
- [ ] The small icon stays legible on a light UI and on a dark system tab bar.
- [ ] The icon ships in the repository (for example an SVG source plus the small favicon sizes). It does not depend on an external URL.

### Environment

Against current `main` of `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `apps/web/index.html` has no favicon, and `BrandIcon` is a flask outline.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Parallel research agents already share arXiv concurrency/pacing, but later calls could still queue behind a known upstream failure and repeated 406 responses had no endpoint-health suppression. This change shares health and cooldown within one service process, bounds admission and actual attempts, and permits one recovery probe after cooldown.

Fixes #208

## Behavior

- Preserve existing concurrency and request intervals. Governed calls make one MCP attempt, so internal retries cannot bypass pacing while holding a slot. Missing queue limits now default to 8 waiters / 20 seconds, capped by the tool timeout.
- Share 429 cooldown by upstream group and effective endpoint/authentication digest, honoring Retry-After in seconds or HTTP-date. Without a hint, backoff starts at 1 second and caps at 30 seconds. Reject affected waiters immediately and return retry timing instead of independent sleeps.
- Keep request-specific or unattributed 406 local. Three distinct, consecutive, provider-attributed endpoint refusals within one minute trigger source/tool suppression: 30-second initial cooldown, capped at 120 seconds. Repeated identical inputs do not reach the threshold.
- Admit one post-cooldown probe; success restores access, failure continues bounded suppression, and cancellation releases the slot and probe permit. Credential changes remain isolated; other sources continue working.
- Return a short unavailable/blocked explanation plus structured timing, same-kind alternative source IDs and citation/evidence guidance. Never claim an uncalled alternative or unavailable content was retrieved. Sanitize provider metadata and diagnostics. No distributed state, infrastructure or new user controls.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`.

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Affected Node UT and deterministic broker/transport fault injection | 117 | 117 | 117 | 0 / 0 |
| Bundled Python MCP tests, including HTTP failure attribution and Retry-After | 30 | 30 | 30 | 0 / 0 |
| Production API user journey | 5 | 5 | 5 | 0 / 0 |

Commands: `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm docs:check`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, targeted `node --import tsx --test` for data-source, tool registry, public-biomed manifests and affected API MCP suites, and Python unittest discovery under `services/gateway/tests`.

Documentation validation: 172 files linted, 144 Markdown files link-checked. Static architecture boundaries: 297 package source files checked.

Baseline regression at `87a87dd36e404cdbc809761991e05e21aa911b8a`: after an injected 429, a later agent round returned a queue timeout without shared retry timing. The same regression passes with fail-fast shared cooldown and no additional upstream attempt.

An extra architecture-wrapper run passed 68/69 script tests; its unrelated RACE contract test could not initialize the default uv cache in the sandbox. The standalone architecture boundary checker passes. Full `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and mocked browser `ci:e2e` were not run: validation targets the changed backend and production API path. No real arXiv/PubMed, real models, DRB or Nightly evaluations were run.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** — `node test/api/source-health-journey.mjs`, production API process and official SDK HTTP MCP fixtures; no in-process API replacement or model calls. Tested SHA: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`.

| User scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configure isolated sources and two research sessions | Real API startup and usable local sources | PASS |
| Concurrent 429 and a later agent round | Shared cooldown and bounded return without amplification | PASS: 9 user calls produced 1 MCP attempt; persisted audit includes retry timing |
| Failed recovery probe, then upstream recovery | One probe during continued failure; later real results | PASS: one failed probe, then two successful accesses |
| Request-specific versus persistent endpoint 406 | Request errors remain local; sustained rejection suppresses later calls | PASS: 4 request-specific failures remain callable; 3 distinct endpoint refusals trigger suppression; later round makes 0 attempts |
| Credentials and healthy source isolation | New credentials can attempt; original cooldown persists; healthy source works | PASS: isolated attempt, preserved original cooldown and real healthy-source result; no credentials in audit |

The journey asserts the short unavailable-source explanation and honest blocked feedback. Broker fault injection additionally verifies queue exhaustion/timeouts, cancellation, probe cancellation, recovery with changed failure status, continued source pacing, available scholarly fallback and unchanged citation/full-text evidence boundaries.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Parallel research avoids repeated waits and calls to a known failing source; diagnostics distinguish throttling and endpoint refusal while preserving evidence requirements.
Compatibility and migration: No user migration. Internal broker queue defaults are now bounded; generic ResourceRateLimiter optional dimensions remain available. State is process-local and resets on restart.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
PDFs dropped into the workspace currently remain raw files. This change sends PDFs identified by MIME type or file extension through the existing `papers/upload` pipeline, so extracted text, tables and provenance are available in the current session. CSV and other attachments keep the existing workspace upload path.

Fixes #333

## Changes

- Reuse `uploadPaper` for Drop files and file-picker PDFs; retain per-file errors and continue processing the rest of a mixed batch.
- Refresh the workspace after extraction, guard against applying upload results to another session, and update the English and Chinese drop hints.
- Extend paper-upload coverage to read extracted tables and execute the session agent's actual `read_file` tool against extracted text.
- Add a real-parser browser journey for PDF + CSV drag-and-drop, in-app protocol reading, CSV preview, MIME/extension detection and invalid-PDF recovery. The existing raw Artifact preview fixture now seeds its minimal PDF through the generic workspace API; its PDF preview assertions remain in place.

## Validation

Tested head: `34282896af3460ff53726962c582910db785860c`.

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Web UT: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` | 1060 | 1060 | 1060 | 0 / 0 |
| Paper and workspace-upload UT: `node --import tsx --test src/papers.test.ts src/workspace-upload.test.ts` in `services/api` | 12 | 12 | 12 | 0 / 0 |
| Paper-upload integration: `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='PDF upload extracts' src/server.test.ts` in `services/api` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Targeted browser journeys, command below | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| Architecture/script checks: `pnpm architecture:check` | 69 | 69 | 69 | 0 / 0 |

`pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, E2E metadata validation and `git diff --check` also passed. Architecture boundaries checked 295 package source files.

Local validation used the targeted checks above. Full `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and `ci:e2e` slices were not run locally: this task requested scoped verification, and the executor/adapter behavior is unchanged. Live-model layers were not run because this flow requires no model calls.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** — 3 planned, 3 executed, 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on the tested head above. Chromium used the isolated product Web/API with the real local paper worker; no real models or remote paper sources were used. The PDF journey ran at 1280 × 720, DPR 1.

Command, from the pinned `.e2e` environment with an isolated `E2E_BASE_URL` and `E2E_API_TOKEN`:

```sh
npm run test:mocked -- journey-drop-pdf.spec.ts journey-artifact-source-preview.spec.ts
```

| Scenario | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Drop PDF + CSV | One succeeded paper in the current session; only the PDF enters paper intake; CSV remains an ordinary attachment. |
| Read parsed protocol | In-app Markdown contains the extracted temperature, replicates, units and rate constant; CSV opens in the existing table viewer. |
| Invalid PDF + valid MIME-identified PDF + CSV | The invalid file reports failure; the next PDF is parsed and the CSV is saved. |
| Existing Artifact and workspace previews | Both existing browser journeys pass, including raw PDF and CSV previews. |
| Agent access, integration check | The actual session `read_file` tool returns the parsed scientific text. No full agent Run was invoked. |

![The dropped PDF's parsed protocol is readable in the current session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fa0ce13-7a82-4602-a5fb-ff2b45ae86a6)

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: Dropped PDFs are automatically parsed as papers and their extraction results are available to the user and session agent. Other attachments keep their current behavior. No migration is required.

## 问题

`scripts/check-architecture.mjs` 在 Windows 环境下会因为 `path.join()` 产生反斜杠路径，而 `component-boundaries.mjs` 使用 `node:path` 的 `posix` 模块处理路径，导致在 Windows 上查找不到对应文件。

## 改动

将 `path.join(path, entry.name)` 替换为模板字符串，确保生成正斜杠路径。

```diff
- const sourceFiles = entries.filter(...).map((entry) => path.join(path, entry.name));
+ const sourceFiles = entries.filter(...).map((entry) => `${path}/${entry.name}`);
```

## 影响范围

- `scripts/check-architecture.mjs`
- `scripts/build-windows.md`（Windows 构建指南）

## 测试

- [x] Windows 本地验证 `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` 通过
- [ ] CI 通过

## 关联 Issue

- Fixes #476

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head
`4bf3ff891beb4ff0c8e9bf2776dc5882e28a551f` is a merge of `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928` and `origin/main` `f4ceca57b74b7f5a10b4f8f77313513a09886c02`. The merge tree matches a clean merge. No conflict was resolved by hand. `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`, and the CLA steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are unchanged from `3bde9d39`. The CLA paragraph in `.ci/README.md` is unchanged; other README edits came in from `main`.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
Nightly real-model E2E treated a single transient model-gateway HTTP 500/503 the same as a product run that finished and failed to deliver, so one provider outage failed the whole Daily gate while other cases in the same job still passed. This change keeps the provider error visible, soft-classifies those faults, optionally repeats an early fault once, and leaves product failures hard-failing.

**The required real-E2E check now has a floor: a planned case that only faulted is an unverified case, and the check does not pass on it.** A soft classification is not a soft green.

After the optional early repeat, a case that passes on the repeat is a genuine `PASS` and the check may go green; a case that still faults keeps the `PROVIDER_FAULT` status and makes the check non-pass.

Closes #232

## The gate floor

| Outcome | Status | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every planned case passed | `PASS` | 0 |
| A provider fault remains, no product failure | `PROVIDER_FAULT` | non-zero |
| A product failure | `FAIL` | non-zero |

The two failure kinds stay apart: a provider fault is still reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT: <case>` and never as `FAIL: <case>`, and a product failure is never softened into an outage. Neither one is a pass. The floor is the same in every place that decides, for the daily, merge L3 and release L5 profiles alike — no profile can turn an outage into a green required check:

- **`verifyResults`** (`test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`): the exit code is 1 whenever a provider fault or a product problem remains; the status is `PROVIDER_FAULT` for a fault, `FAIL` for a product failure, `PASS` only for a run without either.
- **the worker** (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`): a repeat that did not work is audited in the accounting (`PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_FAILED`, `PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_REPORT_MISSING`) instead of only in the log; a batch that faulted as a whole is probed with a couple of repeats instead of re-running every case; a worker whose only failures were provider faults is not double-counted as an opaque worker failure, and the summary's exit code is 1 while a fault remains.
- **the suite reconcile** (`.ci/real-report.mjs`): a provider-fault shard is valid evidence — the identity checks still apply — whose results are folded into the suite accounting; the suite's exit code comes from that accounting, so a remaining fault makes it non-zero. The provider-fault problems stay visible instead of being flattened into an opaque `SHARD_FAILED`, and a shard cannot hide a fault behind a `PASS` it did not earn.
- **the shared-plan summary** (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`): a provider fault is a problem of its own, `planned == executed == passed` is still required, and `passed + provider faults == planned` is no longer enough for green.

## The detector

The provider context has to name the gateway itself: its `181001` model-call code, the wording of a failed model call, the API it answers on, or its own routing failure. Bare words — "provider", "llm", "gateway", "upstream" — are not context: a product delivery failure that mentions one beside a `500` is the product's own failure and stays a `FAIL`. A delivery miss or an assertion diff is the product's own report in the first place and is never soft-classified.

The gateway's own report is unchanged: the `181001` model-call code, the openAI API stream error and the routing failures recorded in the Nightly of 2026-10-06 are still detected as provider faults, and the provider's text is still kept verbatim.

## What changed
- `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`: the tightened provider context, the product-report reject, and the audit codes a failed repeat leaves behind.
- `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`: the exit-code floor in `verifyResults`; the status of a provider fault stays `PROVIDER_FAULT`.
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`: the audited repeat, the capped outage probe, and the worker-failure pairing with the attempt whose exit code it explains.
- `.ci/real-report.mjs`: the reconcile keeps a provider-fault shard's evidence and the suite's exit code follows the accounting.
- `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`: a provider fault is a problem of its own.
- Docs in `.ci/README.md` and `test/support/tagged/README.md`.
- Tests in `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.

Product agent loop, model client, and run orchestration are untouched: only the CI harness and its accounting changed.

## Scenario coverage
| ID | Scenario | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | Gateway HTTP 500 / `new_api_error` / 181001 | `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` | `PROVIDER_FAULT`, text preserved |
| S2 | Gateway HTTP 503 channel / `model_not_found` | same | `PROVIDER_FAULT` |
| S3 | Product delivery failure | same | hard `FAIL`, exit 1 |
| S4 | Mixed job (PASS + provider fault; PASS + product FAIL) | same + reconcile | passes stay PASS; the job does not pass |
| S5 | 401 / 429 / semantic | same | never soft-classified |
| S6 | Mocked visible-gateway-error journey (#234) | hermetic: still `@mocked`/`@model:mock`; never soft-classified | unchanged |
| S7 | All cases faulted, none passed | same + reconcile | status `PROVIDER_FAULT`, exit 1, no `FAIL:` problem |
| S8 | A product failure that quotes a provider status | same | stays a product `FAIL` |
| S9 | A repeat that did not work | same | audited under the provider-fault family, exit 1 |
| S10 | The shared-plan summary over a faulted layer | same (spawned over a temp results dir) | exit 1, fault visible in the table |

## Validation
| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Own S1–S10 (`.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`) | PASS 18/18 |
| `.ci/*.test.mjs` (incl. new) | PASS 101/101 |
| L1 | PASS 4/4 |
| UT | 4857 planned/executed, 4849 PASS, 8 FAIL — the same pre-existing box environment classes as on the base commit (OpenSSH key derivation, workspace host path, scientific R/Python egress, runner NPU broker); the same files fail on the clean tree, and no provider-fault case fails |
| ST | PASS 24/24 |
| L3 merge/e2e-real legacy | PASS 9/9 on `7ec0b43a0e56c7c7c2784fae7a813d0e50f4fe20` |

## E2E user journeys
PASS on SHA `7ec0b43a0e56c7c7c2784fae7a813d0e50f4fe20`; API / real-model; profile `merge`, backend `legacy`, `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`.

Command: `pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy`

| Journey | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L3-response: Short response and stream completion | pass | PASS |
| L3-tool: A real command result reaches the final answer | pass | PASS |
| L3-files: Read and edit a workspace file without changing its neighbour | pass | PASS |
| L3-memory: Reopen a Session and recall its previous turn | pass | PASS |
| L3-artifact: A delivered version remains readable after follow-up | pass | PASS |
| L3-workspace: Relative file writes stay in the selected Session | pass | PASS |
| L3-cancel: Cancel a live run and continue the session | pass | PASS |
| L3-runner-wait: real model requests user help and resumes after cancellation | pass | PASS |
| L3-runner-finish: real model honors the request to explain failure without waiting | pass | PASS |

Counts: passed 9 / failed 0 / blocked 0 / skipped 0. Tagged summary: status `PASS`, exit code 0, provider faults 0.

Issue acceptance is covered: a gateway 500/503 is visible as a provider error (S1, S2); it does not mean the same as a product delivery miss (S3, S8); the cases that passed in the same job stay passes (S4); the gate does not treat an outage or an incomplete verification as success (S7, S9, S10 — the floor); and no business main-path file changed.

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Resolve environment mode on the remote Runner itself. Reject forwarding a host-local custom proxy to a remote Runner, with recovery guidance.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace build and typecheck | Passed before rebase; upstream changes are E2E helpers/tests/docs only |
| Proxy transport, diagnostics and Runner environment tests | 28 passed |
| Model, downloader, Runner client and resolver regression tests | 41 passed |
| Targeted settings persistence / Runner policy propagation | 3 passed (overlaps Runner regression coverage) |
| Adapter hermetic tests | 234 passed; live gateway and real-model test files excluded |
| Proxy settings component tests | 4 passed |
| L1 checks | 4 passed on the rebased head |
| Browser settings journeys | 2 passed in 36.6s on the rebased head |
| Swarm mocked contracts | 9 passed before final rebase; unchanged product code |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

items.body:
Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and the scientific memory graph.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy with the imported conversation and evidence. New research preserves the original snapshot. The compact continuation action appears beside the composer notice; the copy-origin notice disappears after 10 seconds.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies; complete exports include broader history and trajectory details. File selections, export profiles, counts, and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- User messages have a copy action; the existing assistant copy action is retained. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply, including after restart and for branches of branches.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence and discloses unavailable history; it never replaces a missing historical file with a later version. Busy sessions are rejected, request retries are idempotent, and imported snapshots remain protected.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the local graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration.

## Validation

Tested commit: `4e198ebe9ea9161d826827af816df59a09d02fb1`, based on official `main` at `9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`. Exactly one feature commit; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Targeted feature regressions: 50 Node tests passed (21 package/API/import/branch cases and 29 UI-control/trajectory cases), plus 2 scientific-memory Python tests passed. These are targeted results, not a passing full UT layer.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: failed during Node collection with `NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED` after the collector's 120,000 ms timeout; no plan was produced and no tests executed. The same full-layer command on pristine official `main` failed at the same collection timeout.
- `pnpm ci:st`: 24 planned, 24 executed, 17 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped. Pristine official `main` has the same counts and the same seven failed planned identities: five specialist-runtime/ACP cases, the Evolve Python-runtime download reaching the worker timeout, and the Swarm SDK contract command. Nested SDK results differ: the candidate reports 26 failed / 53 passed / 1 teardown error, while main reports 25 failed / 54 passed; both also report 20 passed subtests. The candidate has an additional timeout in `test_http_disconnect_propagates_cancellation_to_adapter`; this runtime validation difference remains unresolved. The SDK check completed normally before the local wait limit; it was not reported as a pass or skipped.
- No test assertions were weakened or cases skipped to obtain a passing result. Runtime failures and browser coverage gaps remain open; this PR stays Draft.

## E2E user journeys

**FAIL / incomplete coverage**, on the tested commit above, using the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend and local mocked models. `pnpm ci:e2e` reports 103 planned, 9 reported/executed, 7 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped; 94 identities were not run. One of the two reported failures is an interrupted case, not a completed assertion failure.

Command: `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/runtime pnpm ci:e2e`, after dependencies, full build, bubblewrap, and the pinned Chromium were prepared in an isolated detached worktree.

| Batch | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research, 20 planned | Healthy isolated stack, then research journeys | BLOCKED before browser execution: scientific memory did not become healthy within the startup script's 10-second wait. |
| Standard, 77 planned | Healthy gateway, valid serialized ordering, then UI journeys | Reporter raised `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST`; the gateway also timed out during WebSocket opening handshake. Network guard passed, the first inline-card case failed, and the unhealthy run was manually interrupted: 1 passed / 1 failed / 1 interrupted / 74 not run. The tagged summary counts the interruption as FAIL. Supplemental Swarm `history` recorded FAIL; remaining supplemental checks were stopped. |
| Literature, 6 planned | Offline literature-source contracts complete through the local product stack | 6 executed, 6 passed. |

The changed user goals are importing and inspecting evidence, continuing a snapshot in a writable session, previewing/downloading workspace files, inspecting trajectory/export scopes, copying a user message, and branching from a reply with navigation back to its source. Expected outcomes are persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable branches, and return to the source reply. These changed UI journeys remain **unverified by browser E2E** because of the blocked/interrupted batches. The targeted package/API tests are regression tests, not external-client API or local-stack journey certification; that additional journey coverage also remains open.

Baseline: the same full E2E entry point on pristine official main reports 101 planned, 0 reported/executed/passed/failed/skipped, with all identities unreported and the layer FAIL. Research and standard failed JiuwenSwarm AgentServer startup. Literature collided on a dynamically chosen Swarm port with the concurrent candidate startup; this is a test isolation limitation, not evidence of identical product failures. Dead baseline startup waits were manually terminated after logs established that their apps had exited. No assertions, retries, or case selectors were weakened to produce these results. No real/paid model journey was run.

## Scope and release

Local startup changes in `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts`, and `.env` are excluded. These files and the existing local stash are preserved.

Release category: `release:feature`.
Compatibility: legacy evidence packages remain importable; absent historical evidence is disclosed rather than invented. Keep this PR as a draft pending complete runtime validation and review.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/engine-commands.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm typecheck` — no errors
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0

Unconfirmed shell status observations were written as provenance execution runs with `status: "failed"`. Skill distillation and the memory graph then treated a lost observation as a job failure, and that failed run stayed forever because runs are append-only even after shell-execution reconciliation adopted the Runner's real outcome. This change records those observations as `unconfirmed` instead, keeps real failed/cancelled outcomes as such, and lets readers see a later adopted committed result for the same Execution ID without replaying the command.

## Provenance status and readers
- Extend `ExecutionRun.status` with `"unconfirmed"`.
- Observation/dispatch error path uses `lostOutcomeStatus` → `unconfirmed` (abort still `cancelled`).
- Readers (`settledExecutionRun` / `effectiveExecutionRuns` / `settledExecutionRuns`) and skill distillation use settled runs only; the memory graph skips `unconfirmed`.

## Adopt committed Runner outcome
- `ShellExecutions.adoptCommittedOutcome` and `ProvenanceRecorder.adoptShellOutcome` append a real settled run for the same Execution ID (no replay).
- Outcome adopter is wired after `store.load()` so API fixtures keep a initialized Shell Execution store.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.
