- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Description

When a session is deleted, a confirmation dialog is shown that asks the user to type the session name and click the permanent-delete button. After entering the correct session name and clicking the permanent-delete button, the frontend reports a request error:

```
session not found
```

However, the session is in fact already deleted on the backend (it is gone from the session list after refreshing). In addition, the confirmation dialog does not close after the error is shown, so the UI is stuck on the dialog and the user has to dismiss it manually, and it is unclear whether the deletion actually succeeded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start ScienceDiscovery and open a project that contains at least one session.
2. Trigger the delete action on a session so that the delete confirmation dialog appears.
3. Type the exact name of the session to be deleted into the input of the dialog.
4. Click the permanent-delete button.

### Expected behavior

- The session is deleted without any error.
- The delete confirmation dialog closes automatically after the deletion succeeds.
- The session list refreshes and no longer shows the deleted session.

### Actual behavior

- A request error `session not found` is shown in the UI.
- The session is nevertheless deleted (it disappears from the list / after refreshing the page).
- The delete confirmation dialog stays open and is not dismissed.


### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows (x86_64)
- Deployment: local source mode, running from the latest main branch source (not the prepackaged binary)
- Service started with `./ScienceDiscovery serve`, UI accessed at http://127.0.0.1:4310
- Browser: Chromium-based desktop browser

### Additional Information

- The session is gone after refreshing the page, so the deletion itself succeeds on the backend; the `session not found` error and the fact that the dialog stays open appear to be a frontend state/refresh issue after the delete request returns.
- Expected fix: treat the response as success (or refresh the session list) and always close the confirmation dialog once the delete request completes.

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery: latest main branch (built and run from source)

### Problem

Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain literal `<think>` tags.

These tags appear as part of the visible title instead of a clean summary of the conversation. This makes session titles confusing and harder to scan.

The issue is intermittent; the exact trigger has not yet been identified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session and send a message.
2. Wait for the session title to be automatically generated.
3. Check the generated title.
4. Occasionally, the title contains literal `<think>` tags.

### Actual behavior

The generated session title includes `<think>` markup.

### Expected behavior

Automatically generated session titles should contain only a concise, readable summary of the conversation, without reasoning tags or reasoning content.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Automatically generated titles never display `<think>` or `</think>` tags.

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
Follow-up discovered during the repository-wide review of #295; related to #288 and #291. Suggested priority: **P2**.

A failed model connection can silently undo a successful settings change made by another tab or API client while the connection test is running. The wizard restores the entire global-settings snapshot captured before the attempt, including fields it did not change.

This is **pre-existing**, not a regression introduced by #295. The same browser/API reproduction failed on both the base commit `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310` and PR revision `45366a904edc7c57e69d36ce79b944e75b382d45`. The rollback code remains unchanged in the latest PR revision `d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635`.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated instance, the real API/store, and a local model endpoint that returns an authentication failure. No real provider credentials are needed.

1. Start with no registered models and persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
2. Open System settings → Models and connect a custom provider. Let the wizard successfully read global settings, create the provider, and register its first model. The backend automatically selects this first model as the global default.
3. While `POST /api/models/:id/test` is pending, use a second API client to read the current overrides and successfully write them back with only `thinkingEffort` changed to `"low"`. Preserve the current temporary `modelId` in this write.
4. Let the connection test return an authentication failure.
5. Read back `GET /api/settings`.

Observed interleaving, with the generated model ID abbreviated:

| Stage | Persisted overrides |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state / wizard snapshot | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |
| Successful concurrent write | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"low","modelId":"temporary-model"}` |
| Wizard rollback | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |

**Actual:** the concurrent `"low"` setting is silently replaced by the old `"high"` value.

**Expected:** undo only this attempt's default-model change when it is still owned by the attempt; preserve the other client's `"low"` setting and every other unrelated override.

The browser reproduction intercepts the model-test request only to schedule a second, successful write through the real settings API before allowing the failing model test to proceed. It uses the actual App, wizard, HTTP API, and store.

## Cause and implementation boundary

[`ModelConnectWizard.restoreSavedOverrides`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L360-L377) calls `replaceGlobalSettings(savedOverrides)` on failure. This replaces the whole settings object with a snapshot taken before provider creation and model testing.

The backend needs the attempt's automatic default cleared before it can delete the temporary model, but restoring unrelated fields is unnecessary. The same unconditional rollback also runs when existing models meant the attempt did not change the default.

The [documented settings boundary](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md#L220-L232) already provides a catalog-level settings mutex and revision-checked plugin writes. Classic PUT intentionally remains last-writer-wins. This issue concerns the wizard's stale whole-object compensation; it does not require changing all classic PUT semantics.

A frontend-only fresh GET followed by another whole-object PUT still leaves a read/write race. Use an atomic conditional undo or equivalent version/ownership check at the existing server-side settings boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed connection preserves unrelated global-setting changes committed while that connection is in progress, including explicit empty connector selections.
- [ ] Rollback changes `modelId` only if the current default still belongs to this attempt; a newer default chosen by another writer is not overwritten.
- [ ] If the attempt never changed the global default, cleanup does not restore the old global-settings snapshot.
- [ ] In the uncontended first-model failure case, the temporary automatic default is safely undone and only the attempt's provider/models are deleted; existing references remain protected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic integration regression test using real settings persistence and an interleaved second writer. Check persisted settings after rollback and reopening the store, rather than only asserting mock delete calls.
- [ ] Cover both an unrelated-field edit and a concurrent default-model change, while retaining #295's test that a failed initial settings read creates no provider/model.

This is separate from #291: here the wizard's initial settings read succeeds, and the loss occurs during later failure rollback after another writer has saved successfully.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Model connection rollback overwrites concurrent global settings changes

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
The sandbox network consent card added in #381 (Fixes #324) offers **Allow once / Allow same type / Deny**. For a `sandbox_network` request the second button doesn't say what it covers. I checked on #381 head `fb2fe785`: choosing **Allow same type** for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443` does **not** widen to other hosts. A later request for `api.crossref.org:443` in the same run still raised its own card, because the resource is a per-host/run digest. Users can still reasonably read "same type" as "all sandbox network access", which is broader than what is actually granted.

## Expected
For `sandbox_network` cards, the user can tell exactly what each button grants. Either:
- rename the button for this action (e.g. "Allow these hosts for this conversation"), with a short scope hint, or
- hide it, if repeat consent for the exact same host set isn't a useful flow.

## Context
- Refs #381, #324.
- The button label comes from the shared key `permissions.allowMatching`, which every permission type uses. The fix should be action-specific, not a global rename.
- Repro: Ask approval mode → model calls `request_sandbox_network` for host A → **Allow same type** → model requests host B in the same run → a new card appears for B.

## Verification cases
1. **Label reads its real scope**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `none`; the model calls `request_sandbox_network` with `hosts: ["eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443"]`.
   - Steps: Open the pending card in the conversation.
   - Expected: The card shows exactly one card for that host. The second button is either missing or its label names the host scope (not "Allow same type"). Allow once and Deny are unchanged.
2. **Grant never widens to another host (regression)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1.
   - Steps: Click the second button (whatever it is called) for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443`. In the same run the model then requests `api.crossref.org:443`.
   - Expected: A **new** card appears for `api.crossref.org:443`. The second host is not auto-allowed, and there are 2 `sandbox_network` permission requests in total.
3. **Other permission types unaffected**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; the model calls `run_shell`.
   - Steps: Open the "Run a shell script" card.
   - Expected: Its buttons keep the current labels (Allow once / Allow same type / Deny) and behaviour.
4. **Global settings untouched**
   - Steps: Run case 2. Compare `GET /api/sandbox-network-settings` before and after.
   - Expected: The settings are identical.
closed_recent.title: Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear for one-shot sandbox network grants

closed_recent.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
closed_recent.body:
## Correction (2026-10-22T04:2xZ)

This issue was first filed as an "intermittent CI load flake". **That was wrong.** The failure is deterministic and the root cause is a runner image change. The earlier hypothesis (concurrency/load) is withdrawn, and the "same test passes in the CI-test run" evidence was also invalid — `UT` was skipped in that run.

## What actually happens

GitHub rolled `ubuntu-latest` from **ubuntu-24.04** to **ubuntu-26.04** between 2026-10-21T10:15Z and 2026-10-22T02:22Z. The pruning path builds its "busy" set from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe`:

```
packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:106
busy=$(for process in /proc/[0-9]*; do readlink "$process/exe" 2>/dev/null || true; done)
```

On ubuntu-26.04 that link no longer reports the binary a live process is executing, so the pruning pass sees an **in-use binary as stale and deletes it**. This is product code, not only a test helper: on 26.04 the same logic would delete a binary that is currently running.

## Evidence

| when (UTC) | job | runner image | `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-21T10:16Z | `119165996742` (#467 merge group) | **ubuntu-24.04** | 2661 ms, all tests pass |
| 2026-10-22T03:31Z | `119621422198` (#468) | **ubuntu-26.04** | 3 `/bin/sh`, `/bin/dash`, `/bin/bash` cases fail |

- Runner version is `2.338.0` in both jobs; only the image changed.
- Failing run [39716847675](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39716847675), job `119621422198`, step `Run UT`: planned 4441 / executed 4441 / passed 4438 / **failed 3** / skipped 0.
- Failure artifact `ut/tagged/group-141/worker-1-events.jsonl`: actual has an extra `'b' x 64` — the busy binary was pruned. The other 4 tests in the file pass.
- `merge-gate` (job `119626303432`) only aggregates: `CI gate failed: ut: failure`.
- Every PR after the switch shows the same signature: #269 #316 #460 #463 #465 #466 #467 #468.

## Impact

`UT` is a required check, so **no PR can enter the merge queue** for reasons unrelated to its own diff — the pipeline is blocked repo-wide.

## Suggested fix

1. Short term (unblocks the queue): pin the UT job to `ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:194` uses `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`).
2. Correct fix: stop deriving "busy" from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe` alone. Compare device+inode via `stat -L /proc/<pid>/exe` against the file being pruned (works when the link target is not readable), and log the observed `busy` set when a removal is skipped, so the next platform change is diagnosable from CI logs.
3. Add a regression test that fails if a running binary is pruned — the existing test is the right shape, but it needs to run on the platforms we actually support.
closed_recent.title: bug(executor): pruning treats live binaries as stale on ubuntu-26.04 runners (busy detection uses readlink /proc/<pid>/exe)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require “sandbox already unavailable” before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still “ready”; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for “prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent.”

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Agent-first direct execution (skip-sandbox by Agent + user consent)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

原生主 Agent（`runtime-core` AgentLoop）支持一轮多个 `tool_calls`，默认可并行约 10 路（`SCIENCE_AGENT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS`）。

Codex / Claude / ACP **specialist-runtime** 则走结构化 `platformDecision`：schema 只有单个 `tool` 字段（`string | null`），文案与循环均为「Request ONE platform tool → 校验 → 执行一个 → 回灌 → 下一轮」。这不是全平台总契约，只是 specialist 路径约定。

体验后果：自由 brief（尤其 DSV 兼容端点）易报 `Codex returned an invalid platform decision`；任务被拆成多轮，延迟与首败噪音上升。

## 目标

放开 specialist 路径「一轮只能一个平台工具」的硬限制，使其更接近主 Agent 的多工具能力；同时保留权限总线（原生 shell/改文件仍应走平台工具，不得悄悄打开 `shell_tool` 绕过）。

## 建议方向（实现可选，验收看行为）

- Schema 支持一轮多个 tool 请求（数组或等价结构），执行循环按序或可并行（exclusive 工具同轮串行即可）。
- 非法/半合法输出：纠错重试或自动拆轮，减少 `invalid platform decision` 首败。
- 若需分档：可按 runtime kind / 兼容端点默认保守，官方端点更宽；**不要**仅暴露一个无说明的全局布尔就结束。

## 验收标准

- [ ] specialist decision 契约允许多 tool（文档 + schema + 执行循环一致）。
- [ ] 至少一条自动化测试：一轮 decision 含 ≥2 个合法平台工具时可完成执行（或明确的有序执行），且权限/审计仍走平台路径。
- [ ] 非法 JSON / 多意图胡写时有明确失败或纠错，不静默丢工具。
- [ ] 不恢复 Codex 原生 `shell_tool` / 未授权改文件作为捷径。
- [ ] 与 DSV 等兼容端点联调：自由 brief 的 `invalid platform decision` 首败率相对现状有可描述改进（测试或手测步骤写清）。

## 非目标

- 不改主 Agent 并行上限策略（已有）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 runtime 选择 / 加密配 key / Specialist CLI 卡片（见 #455）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/codex.ts` — `decisionSchema`（单 `tool`）
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/decisions.ts` — `platformDecisionSchema`
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` / `tool-scheduler.ts` — 主 Agent 多 tool
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` — `maxParallelToolCalls`
closed_recent.title: feat(specialist-runtime): 放开一轮仅一个平台工具的硬限制

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

Phase2/3 合入后，旧版 `normalizeSpecialistInput` 白名单重建会**静默丢掉** `runtime`（HTTP 仍 201，看起来像创建成功但没有 Codex）。当前源码已修复：`store` 会保留并校验 `runtime`，非法则 400（`SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`）。

日常 CI 已有 UT 覆盖（`services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` 的 create/update/reload 保留 `runtime`；`phase3.test.ts` 多 kind 保留 + 拒凭据字段）。但 **HTTP 层契约偏薄**：没有断言 `POST/PATCH /api/specialists` 响应里的 `runtime`，也没有断言非法字段 → 400。Journey 脚本能间接暴露问题，但默认不进可重复 CI。

## 目标

补上可进 CI 的 HTTP（或等价集成）用例，防止后续改动再次把 `runtime` 从 create/update 路径丢掉。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `POST /api/specialists` 带合法 `runtime: { kind: "codex" }`（及/或 `claude-code` / `acp`）→ **2xx**，且 **响应 body 含同等 `runtime.kind`**（及已声明的非密钥元数据）。
- [ ] `PATCH`（或 update）只改 `description` 等无关字段后，**`runtime` 仍保留**。
- [ ] 带未知凭据字段（如 `apiKey`）或非法 `kind` → **400**，错误可识别为 runtime 配置无效（与现有 `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID` 对齐）。
- [ ] 用例挂在默认可重复门禁（UT/集成，**非**仅手工 journey）；失败条件明确、可本地复现。
- [ ] 不把真实密钥写进测试；不依赖外部 DeepSeek/Codex 网络。

## 非目标

- 不解决「旧 dist / 缓存包缺 `specialist-runtime`」的运维错配提示（可另开）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 UI / 主 Agent 代配 / Specialist CLI 卡片（见姊妹产品 issue）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — `normalizeSpecialistInput` → `normalizeSpecialistRuntime`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/config.ts` — `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` / `phase3.test.ts`
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — 该 code → 400

## What happened

On a session that is still open, the Tasks panel shows `Session not found`, and the same string appears as a request-error toast.

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` polls `getAgentActivity(sessionId)` every 2 seconds. On failure it sets the panel alert to the error message and leaves the previously loaded execution list in place. The screenshot matches that: the session heading is visible, the execution list is populated, and an alert says `Session not found`.

Failure pages from 2026-10-06:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288), DRB-59. Heading `DRB-59 autonomous research` was visible. The Tasks panel showed `Executions 32` and an alert `Session not found`. A second toast was the invalid `run_shell` arguments error. The needs-attention banner also said `Session not found`.
- Same run, DRB-62. Heading `DRB-62 autonomous research` was visible, with `Executions 20` and the same alert, plus the `interaction round execution failed` toast.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020), TC-E2E-01. Heading `BRCA1 team signoff` was visible, with 17 artifacts, `Executions 115`, and resume buttons for stopped subagents. The only request-error toast was `Session not found`.

Many API handlers return 404 `Session not found` when `store.getSession` misses. Which of those handlers the poll hit is not in the Actions log.

## Expected

While the session page is open and its execution list is shown, the activity poll does not report `Session not found` for that session. A 404 for a different id is attributed to that id.

## Evidence limits

This alert was on the failure screens above. The benchmark metrics for DRB-59 and DRB-62 say the main run status was `failed` for a different recorded request error. The team case was still `running` when its budget expired. This issue does not claim that the 404 is what stopped those runs.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
`pnpm ci:ut` starts one JiuwenSwarm instance for the whole slice and then runs every API test file one at a time. Unit tests should start independently and run in parallel. Only a test that declares a real JiuwenSwarm instance should use one, and those tests should take that instance from a single queue.

## What happens now

`scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` installs the pinned JiuwenSwarm, starts one instance and one adapter, and exports `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` plus `SCIENCE_AGENT_ADAPTER_URL` to every process in the slice. One instance has one tool server, so a second adapter would take it from the first.

`createApiServer` reads that process environment. When the variables are set, starting the server syncs web settings to the shared adapter (up to five attempts, three seconds apart). The UT scheduler then marks every file under `services/api/` as one resource, so those files never overlap. The default worker count is 2, and the scheduler rejects a count above 4.

Of the 112 API test files, two wait on a real gateway turn (`services/api/src/server.test.ts` and `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`). Five more start the production server and reach the adapter only because the environment is process-wide (`dashboard.test.ts`, `mcp/source-api.test.ts`, `model-usage-api.test.ts`, `npu-selection-api.test.ts`, `ssh-host-api.test.ts`). The other 105 do not start that server. On one warm run the API lane took 519 seconds, which was the entire UT test wall clock, while the machine had 14 CPUs. GitHub Actions runs this job on a public `ubuntu-latest` runner.

Cases tagged `status:unreviewed` are already outside the plan. They stay there.

## Required behavior

- A unit test that does not declare a JiuwenSwarm instance starts on its own and may run at the same time as other such tests. It must not see `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` or the shared adapter URL, even if it boots `createApiServer`.
- A test that needs a real instance declares that on the test. The directory of the file is not a declaration.
- The UT layer owns one generic startup and one queue for that instance. Declaring tests run on it one at a time. The queue covers only the declaring test, not the other tests in the same file.
- Non-declaring tests use as many workers as a public GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner can sustain. Local `pnpm ci:ut` and the UT job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` use that same number. Do not take the default from the workstation CPU count. Public `ubuntu-latest` runners have 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM; confirm the current size and pin one shared default. If that width is killed for memory, lower the shared default and record why. The two environments must not diverge.
- Do not weaken an assertion, delete a test, or move a `status:unreviewed` case back into the plan to make the run green.

## Done when

- A scheduler test shows non-declaring work overlapping up to the shared worker count, and declaring work never overlapping, including across files.
- `pnpm ci:ut` passes at that worker count, and the GitHub Actions UT job runs the same entry point without a second worker override.
- The pull request names the worker count, lists the tests that declare an instance, and reports the UT numbers.
closed_recent.title: [Internal]: Run unit tests in parallel and queue only cases that declare a JiuwenSwarm instance

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Background

A mocked end-to-end turn that changes the shared tool catalog spends a long time before the model is called. Measured on 2026-10-20, commit `d245cec8d9df52e0b3a99dd5bb236507ec73746d`, journey J3 (prepare a named environment and run one calculation):

- The scripted turn is two beats: one `run_shell` (stub delay 500 ms) and one closing text. Those beats, two rejected model calls, approval, and the shell finished in about 4 seconds.
- After `POST /agent/runs` and before the first `POST /mcp`, about 20 seconds pass. The run carried 44 tools. The MCP HTTP handshake itself, once started, was 7 ms (`platform_mcp_transport_open` to `platform_mcp_connect_ready`).
- After MCP is connected and before the first `chat/completions`, about 16–18 seconds pass. No model HTTP and no `/llm/default` call happen in that window.

Across the three mocked shards that day, the pre-MCP gap appeared on 21 runs (standard 12, research 8, literature 1) and added up to about 264 seconds. The post-connect, pre-model gap on those same runs added up to about 236 seconds. Most runs do not pay this, because their tool catalog does not change. Re-check both gaps on current `origin/main` before changing code; do not treat the old timestamps as a new measurement.

## Change 1: register tool permissions once

`AgentRunner.ensure_shared_tools` calls `_apply_approvals`, which sends `permissions.tools.update` once per tool. `gateway.rpc` opens a new management WebSocket for every call. On the Swarm side each update rewrites `config.yaml` under the config lock. A new shared-server generation name (`sci` plus ten digits) makes every `(server, tool)` key look new, so none of the 44 updates are skipped. `mcp.connect` runs only after that loop, and its live probe is the first `POST /mcp`.

Required behavior:

- Persist the approval map for one generation in one write, and do not open one management WebSocket per tool.
- If the shared tool catalog is unchanged, keep the MCP server that is already connected. Do not disconnect, register, or connect again.
- Leave the MCP handshake and live probe as they are.
- Keep each tool's approval level (`allow` / `ask` / `deny`). Do not widen access.
- Do not drop an in-flight tool call. A bare `mcp.disconnect` is global; reuse must not disconnect a server that still serves a run.
- Keep retiring inactive generations so `config.yaml` does not grow without bound.

## Change 2: skip unchanged per-turn prepare

The 16–18 seconds are work inside JiuwenSwarm after the tool server is connected and before the first model request. They are not time spent writing logs.

`_update_runtime_config` runs on every user message entering the runner. It already times stages (`cwd_seed`, `rail_setters`, `tools_for_mode`, `session_tools`, `prompt_for_mode`, `memory_tools`, and the smaller switches between them) and, after they finish, logs one line when the total is at least 50 ms:

```text
[AgentServer] runtime config applied: session_id=... mode=... total_ms=... <stage breakdown>
```

The threshold override is `JIUWENSWARM_SLOW_STAGE_MS`. A new session also logs `[AgentServer] session adapter created` with `create_instance_ms` and `start_interaction_ms`. After runtime config, `sync_agent_observability` runs: unchanged config is a no-op; a config change restarts the trajectory runtime and joins writer threads.

Required behavior:

- On one slow mocked journey with a new project and session and a single shell beat, capture those existing Swarm log lines. Do not add a second logging system to measure this.
- If `total_ms` is the bulk of the gap, skip the dominant stage when cwd, tools, prompt, and memory tools are unchanged for that session. Still run it when any of those inputs change.
- If `total_ms` is only tens or hundreds of milliseconds, the gap is session-adapter creation or observability sync. Shrink that work under the same rule: unchanged inputs are not prepared again.
- Do not delete the stage log line.
- Do not change the turn's result: same tools, same prompt when inputs changed, same shell cwd when the workspace changed.

If the captured log shows the time is necessary work that cannot be skipped without changing results, stop and report the line. Do not delete that work to make the clock smaller.

Ship a JiuwenSwarm change through the mechanism this repository already uses to patch JiuwenSwarm. Do not open a pull request against the upstream JiuwenSwarm or agent-core repositories from this issue.

## Look only: other mocked end-to-end waste

Look for other mocked end-to-end time that is startup or repeated rejected work, not the scripted beats. Report the cause, a rough saving, and whether removing it would change what a test proves. Do not implement those extras in this pull request.

Out of scope unless the report shows it is the same bug:

- HTTP 400 responses from the model gateway (unsupported parameters, images, token ceiling, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls=false`). The gateway body already states the reason; the access log keeps only the status. There were 216 such responses across the three shards. They return immediately.
- J3's environment clone, about 17 seconds, which is a separate step.
- The reviewer quiet-window wait.
- Deleting long journeys, raising end-to-end workers, or changing `slowMo`.
- Unit-test scheduling (tracked separately).

## Non-goals

- Do not weaken assertions or rewrite a test to avoid a real failure.
- Do not use the local trial port 4310 or its data directory.
- A formal pull request, not a draft. Exactly one label: `release:performance`. The body includes `Fixes #<this issue>`.
- Push the branch only to the operator fork. Do not push it to the upstream repository or to the GitCode mirror.
closed_recent.title: [Performance]: Register run tools once and skip unchanged per-turn prepare

## Request

Integrate DeepSeek's official Search and Fetch APIs so ScienceDiscovery agents can search the web and retrieve page content from a specified URL through DeepSeek.

The providers listed in the current [Web tools documentation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/docs/zh/reference/web-tools.md) do not yet include DeepSeek.

## Expected support

- Add DeepSeek to the Web provider settings, with API key configuration and an enable/disable option.
- Integrate Search via `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search`, mapping titles, URLs, summaries, and other relevant results to the existing tool format for agents to use and cite.
- Integrate Fetch via `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch`, returning the page title and Markdown content.
- Reuse the existing Web permission, credential protection, caching, and audit mechanisms. Document how the integration works with both the default JiuwenSwarm backend and the product's own Web tools.
- Provide clear errors for missing credentials, authentication failures, insufficient balance, rate limits, timeouts, and fetch failures. Handle empty search results through the existing fallback logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- After DeepSeek is configured, an agent can complete the workflow: search the web → fetch a result page → answer using its content.
- No DeepSeek requests are made when it is disabled, and existing provider behavior is unchanged.
- Add tests for successful requests, empty results, and major error cases, along with configuration examples.

Reference: [DeepSeek's official Search and Fetch documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/search/).

closed_recent.body:
## What is wrong

On a large screen the artifact viewer is still a small card. It is the dialog opened from an artifact (`artifact-modal-panel` in `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css`):

- width `min(1080px, 100%)`
- only a max height, `calc(100vh - 56px)`, so a short file stays as short as its content

On a 1920px-wide window that width is about 56% of the viewport. On a 2560px window it is about 42%. Plots, tables, notebooks, and source previews then sit in a column that does not use the screen the user is looking at.

The same class is the shell for the evidence viewer and the node-detail viewer (`ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, `EvidenceModal.tsx`, `DetailModal.tsx`). They should grow with it. Confirmation dialogs and settings panels use other classes and stay small.

## What a reasonable size is

A decision dialog and a content viewer are different objects.

- Material’s dialog cap (560dp wide, 48dp from the screen edge) is for a question or a confirmation. Applying it here would make the viewer smaller.
- A content viewer should take most of the viewport and leave a visible margin, so the dimmed page and the click-outside close still read as a layer. A hard pixel cap still matters on a 4K display, or a paragraph becomes one very long line.
- WorkBuddy opens an artifact as a tab in the right-hand pane, and that pane can go fullscreen. This product’s right pane is 390px, which is too narrow to become the viewer. Growing the existing dialog is the change; do not move artifact viewing into that pane.
- This repo already treats specialized viewers as large windows: the CSV workspace is `min(1480px, 97vw)` by `min(920px, 95vh)` (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/styles.css`), and the molecule window is `min(1360px, 96vw)` by `min(880px, 93vh)`. The generic artifact dialog is the one that did not follow that pattern.

## Target

On a wide screen, size the artifact viewer like those content windows, one step larger:

- width `min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`
- height `min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`

That is 1600×960 when the window is large enough, and it shrinks with an 80px total margin when it is not. It does not go edge to edge. At `max-width: 900px` the existing rule already makes this panel full viewport; leave that rule alone.

Inside the window, prose stays readable. Markdown body copy keeps a measure of about 76ch. Tables, code, images, and plots use the window width. Do not widen a paragraph to 1600px.

The evidence title already ellipsizes at `min(560px, 60vw)`. That cap can stay. The comment above it still says the panel is about 1080px; update the comment if that block is touched.

## Out of scope

- Settings, creation, and deletion dialogs.
- The CSV workspace and the molecule window. They are already larger than 1080px.
- The 390px workspace panel.
- The conversation column width.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width of about 1920px, the artifact viewer is 1600px wide and 960px tall, centered, with the page still visible around it.
- At a width between 900px and 1600px, the viewer is the viewport minus about 80px, not stuck at 1080px.
- At 900px and below, the viewer is still the full viewport, as it is today.
- A markdown artifact’s paragraphs do not run the full 1600px. A wide table or source preview does use the window.
- Evidence and node-detail viewers use the same size. A settings dialog does not.
- A render test, or a CSS assertion next to the existing dialog styles, locks the new width and height.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Make the artifact viewer use a large screen

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require "sandbox already unavailable" before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still "ready"; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for "prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent."

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Agent-first direct execution (skip-sandbox by Agent + user consent)

closed_recent.author: ink999107
closed_recent.body:
## Environment

- Release package `sciencediscovery` **0.3.0-beta** (x86_64), started with `ScienceDiscovery serve`, Linux

## Symptom

Soon after startup the right-side task panel in the web UI shows `invalid internal token`, and the **Retry** button never recovers — the same error returns every time. Chat and agent runs work normally.

## What the shipped package does

1. The payload contains no evolve sidecar, and the launcher neither starts one nor passes `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` / `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the API (confirmed in the running API process' environment). Memory-graph gets the opposite treatment — the launcher seeds it with a per-run random token (`services/launcher/src/memory-graph.ts:27`).
2. With both variables unset the API falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:4313` with the constant token `sciencediscovery-evolve-local` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/config.ts:253-256`).
3. Whatever process happens to hold `127.0.0.1:4313` therefore receives the API's evolve traffic. In my case that port was held by another process running an evolve sidecar configured with its own token, so the calls came back `401 {"detail":"invalid internal token"}` — and the frontend relayed that raw `detail` string into the task panel, where Retry just re-issues the same call.

I verified the error did not come from my own stack's memory-graph: the launcher-generated token matches the API's on both sides, and its access log shows zero 401s. The string is in fact the loopback-auth rejection detail shared by both sidecars (`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/auth.py:40`, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/auth.py:40`) — which is why it reaches users with no hint of which service or token failed.

## Why the fallback itself is the problem

- The API ends up calling an arbitrary process that happens to bind a fixed port, authenticating with a token guessable from the public source. A sidecar that rejects it produces the unrecoverable raw error above; a process that accepts it (or runs an evolve sidecar with the token unset — auth is permissive then) would be silently used by this installation.
- Run specifications sent to the sidecar carry the LLM proxy URL and token (`llm`, `judge` fields in `services/api/src/evolution/sidecar.ts`), so whatever holds the port also receives those credentials.

## Suggestions

- Give evolve the same launcher treatment as memory-graph: start it from the payload with a per-run random token, or explicitly disable it / point the API at an operator-configured URL, so the constant fallback is never reached.
- When a sidecar call fails, report which sidecar failed instead of relaying the raw `detail` to the UI.
- Prefer per-installation fallback credentials over source constants, and avoid fixed default sidecar ports (related: #267).

Workaround I applied locally: launch with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` pointing at an unused loopback port, so the API no longer calls whatever holds 4313.
closed_recent.title: Hardcoded evolve sidecar fallback (127.0.0.1:4313 + fixed token) surfaces raw "invalid internal token" in the UI

## Summary

Every new session defaults to **Ask for dangerous actions**, even inside a project where the user already set **Always allow** on prior sessions. There is no project- or global-level default, so demos and repeated analysis require toggling the composer control every time.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 local demos (Scenarios 1–3, 2026-10-15/16):

For trusted local sandboxes and scripted demos, re-confirming every session adds friction and invites accidental runs still on Ask (more interrupt cards) or forgetting to tighten back later.

## Expected

- Remember last choice per project, **or**
- Offer a project/global default (Ask / Always allow) that new sessions inherit, with a clear per-session override.

## Priority

**Medium** usability — repeated friction, not a functional blocker.

Distinct from sandbox egress solicitation (#324).

closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable

## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session **timeline is too engineering-oriented**. Parallel tool cards, subagent workspace paths, and token/turn counters dominate the main pane, so a researcher cannot quickly see *what is happening for the research task*. Progress that does exist is buried (e.g. a sidebar tooltip like `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`) while the main area stays on a large **INPUT** dump.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, ~7 min raw screen recording):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards filled the timeline with long specialist prompts (INPUT), UUIDs / `subagents/…` paths, model name, turn counts, and token usage.
- Primary status was often just `Running` / `Tool is running…`.
- The more human-readable status (`PubMed search … · running`) appeared mainly as a **sidebar hover tooltip**, not as the main-pane headline.
- Researchers scanning the UI struggled to answer: which searcher is doing what, what failed, how many papers so far, when synthesis starts.

## Why this is a serious usability problem
This is a research workbench UX issue, not mere polish:

1. Cognitive load: engineering telemetry (paths, tokens, raw INPUT) competes with the research narrative.
2. Progress opacity: meaningful status is secondary (tooltip / deep in cards) while the main column looks like a developer console.
3. Trust: when retrieval degrades (no MCP tools, sandbox/network failures), the timeline does not make the failure mode obvious at a glance.

Related but distinct from #327 (no incremental progress at all). Here the problem is **information hierarchy / audience**: even when something is updating, the wrong details are foregrounded.

## Expected behavior
For literature / research sessions (and ideally by default for non-debug users):

1. Timeline cards should lead with a **human-readable phase** (e.g. “Searching PubMed for clinical CRISPR/SCD papers”, “Source unavailable”, “Synthesizing 5 papers”).
2. Keep subagent paths, full INPUT blobs, token/turn stats behind an expand/debug control — not the default above-the-fold view.
3. Surface parallel branches as short labeled lanes (clinical vs mechanism) rather than two giant opaque tool cards.
4. Put the same status that today only appears in the sidebar tooltip into the main timeline card header.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Default “Researcher” timeline vs optional “Developer / debug” density.
- Collapse tool INPUT by default; show a one-line summary + live status.
- Promote connector/search failures into the card status line as soon as they happen.

## Priority
**High among usability issues** for research users (serious scanability / trust problem), though not a functional crash.

## Related
- #327 — long runs only show `Tool is running…` (progress missing)
- #325 — connectors enabled but MCP tools omitted (functional bug that makes the opaque timeline worse)
- #324 — sandbox egress should ask for permission
closed_recent.title: Usability: session timeline is too engineering-heavy for researchers (tool cards, subagent paths, tokens)

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
Cancelling or disconnecting a sandboxed execution can leave that execution running until the script exits, when the machine is under CPU pressure. The caller already sees an abort error.

## Expected

After the client disconnects or the run is cancelled, the Runner kills the sandbox process group promptly. The execution leaves `activeExecutions` in a short time that does not grow with the payload.

## Actual

On an idle machine, aborting `time.sleep(30)` or `time.sleep(60)` cleared `activeExecutions` in about 75 ms. With the Runner and busy loops pinned to the same core, the same abort often took about 30250 ms for a 30-second sleep and about 60238 ms for a 60-second sleep. One 60-second case was still running after 120 seconds. The sandbox had not been killed; it ran to completion, and only then dropped out of `activeExecutions`.

`services/runner/src/executor.ts` registers the abort listener after `spawnSandboxProcess` resolves. `killSandboxProcess` then sends `SIGKILL` to the process group, which is the right signal once it runs. The kill does not run until the event loop observes the abort. A starved loop still lets the payload finish. The same path is what the product uses when a person cancels a long run in the interface.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/71
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Cancelling a run under CPU pressure can leave the sandbox running until the script exits

## Summary

Complete model API compatibility across ScienceDiscovery by strengthening protocol tests, reusing the existing model adapters throughout the framework, and checking endpoint compatibility during configuration. This is an extension of existing support, not a new parallel model-client implementation.

## Current situation and problem

The main Agent model client already implements OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. Swarm communicates with an internal Chat Completions gateway, which adapts requests to the configured upstream protocol. However, auxiliary paths such as Evolve, session naming and paper-related model calls still contain direct Chat Completions requests; inventory and verify their current behavior before changing them.

An endpoint or model name does not uniquely identify a protocol. Aggregators can expose several protocols, and apparent compatibility can conceal lost tool-call, stop-reason or reasoning state. Missing/malformed usage is a separate accounting problem and must not fail an otherwise successful task or prevent benchmark scoring. Existing usage work, including PR #304, should be reused rather than duplicated.

## Proposed scope

### 1. Strengthen UT/ST/Mock E2E coverage

Use deterministic local provider fixtures for all three supported protocol families. Cover request/history/system/tool translation; streaming text and fragmented tool arguments; tool IDs, parallel calls and result round-trips; required protocol-specific reasoning/signature state; completion versus truncation; cancellation, errors and malformed responses. Cover valid, missing and malformed usage separately, preserving unknown values rather than inventing zero usage or exact costs.

Include end-to-end mocked journeys through the Swarm gateway and affected auxiliary callers. These tests require no real model tokens. Newly added production code should in principle have 100% combined UT/ST coverage; document exact uncovered paths, reasons, risks and alternative verification. Passing Mock E2E is not UT/ST coverage proof.

### 2. Reuse existing adapters across framework callers

Inventory direct model HTTP calls, then route the in-scope Agent and auxiliary calls through the existing protocol-aware model boundary. Start with Evolve, session naming and paper-related calls, verifying actual capability and integration needs rather than blindly replacing URLs. Keep internal Chat Completions compatibility where components require it, with explicit upstream adaptation. Reuse Swarm/agent-core clients where applicable; avoid another provider router or duplicated protocol implementation.

Preserve system instructions, tool semantics, termination/truncation and error causes. Where a function genuinely cannot support a configured capability, surface a precise limitation; do not silently discard tools/parameters, change models or degrade to text-only execution.

### 3. Add configuration-time compatibility checks

For the supplied endpoint/model/credentials, expose an explicit compatibility-check action and detect which of the supported protocols work. Check actual response structure, not merely HTTP 200. Return per-protocol outcomes and independently report basic response, streaming, tool-call/result round-trip and usage availability. An endpoint may support multiple protocols; retain user selection/manual override and persist the chosen protocol rather than guessing each turn.

Use minimal bounded synthetic requests, timeouts and output limits; disclose that checks may consume paid tokens and obtain explicit user initiation/consent before requests. Separate confirmed incompatibility from authentication/authorization, rate limits, network failures and inconclusive responses. Nonstandard proxy prefixes and provider-specific headers must follow existing explicit configuration rather than guessed hostname/model rules. Recheck upon relevant endpoint/model/protocol configuration changes without silently starting chargeable probes.

## Acceptance criteria and boundaries

- Main Agent/Swarm and inventoried in-scope auxiliary callers use a shared, tested protocol adaptation path for Chat Completions, Responses and Messages; existing default configurations remain functional.
- Deterministic UT/ST/Mock journeys verify full tool-call round-trips, streaming, truncation and original error propagation, including auxiliary callers; no new paid real-LLM PR gate.
- Configuration checks show supported protocols and capability/unknown/error details; users can explicitly choose or override a result. No silent runtime protocol switching or fallback that could replay requests or corrupt history.
- Missing usage does not block Agent progress, success assertions or scoring. Usage unavailability remains visible for accounting.
- Probes, fixtures and logs redact credentials and do not send research task content; no secrets in URLs, public artifacts or browser persistence outside existing credential policy.
- Document supported protocols, configuration checks, costs, limitations and troubleshooting. Protocol compatibility does not certify the upstream model's identity, quality or routing, and cannot fix arbitrary supplier-side corruption.
- Gemini-native and Bedrock-native protocols are outside this initial scope. Automated probing does not guarantee compatibility with every nonconforming provider.
closed_recent.title: Feature: complete model API protocol compatibility and add configuration-time checks

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary
When a literature / research task needs outbound network (PubMed, arXiv, skill scripts, etc.) and the sandbox blocks egress, the agent should **ask the user for network permission** (or guide them to grant Sandbox network allowlist access) rather than proceeding blocked and falling back without a clear permission request.

## Observed behavior
On a literature-research run (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0):

- Global `/api/sandbox-network-settings` was `mode: "none"` with empty `allowedDomains`.
- Skill scripts and direct HTTP inside the sandbox failed with DNS / network denial (`Temporary failure in name resolution` to NCBI / arXiv hosts).
- The run continued without a user-facing “please grant sandbox egress for these domains” step; retrieval degraded to `web_search` only.

## Why this is a usability problem
Users who enable PubMed/arXiv connectors or kick off a literature task reasonably expect the product to either:

1. already have the needed egress, or  
2. **prompt them once** to allow the required hosts / switch Sandbox network mode,

not silently hit fail-closed sandbox policy and produce a weaker report.

## Expected behavior
When the agent (or a skill/subagent) hits a sandbox egress block that is required for the current task:

1. Surface a clear permission / settings request to the user naming the needed domains (or Sandbox network mode change).
2. Pause or offer a retry path after the user grants access, instead of only recording failures in artifacts.
3. Prefer asking over silent degradation when the user’s prompt explicitly asked for PubMed/arXiv (or similar) retrieval.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Detect sandbox network denials that match known research hosts and open a UI affordance tied to **System configuration → Sandbox network** (domain-allowlist / mode).
- Or have the control plane preflight: if session has PubMed/arXiv enabled and sandbox mode is `none`, warn or solicit allowlist before the run starts.

## Environment / repro sketch
- Product: ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Settings: sandbox network `mode: none`
- Task: CRISPR / SCD literature research requesting PubMed and/or arXiv
- Outcome: DNS/network failures in sandbox; no user prompt to grant egress; fallback to web_search

## Related
See also the review auto-run usability gap (#323).
closed_recent.title: Usability: when sandbox egress blocks research, ask the user for network permission instead of silently failing

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
A parent run that launches several `task` subagents in one turn can fail while persisting the children's results, even though the children themselves finish.

## Expected

A completed subagent handoff is stored, and the parent run stays successful. Nested fields inside the child snapshot are not treated as content-addressed references.

## Actual

The parent run ends with `Agent run failed` and the UI reports `Invalid or cross-pool reference`. The children have already finished. A later user message can receive their completion notices, but that is a new run, not a resume of the failed one.

The `task` tool returns `details: { subagent, summary }` from `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`. The native agent writes that object into a `ToolObservation` in `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts`. `ContentStore.putRecord` in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts` walks every nested object that has both `pool` and `digest`, and rejects a value that is not a complete object in the current pool. A real subagent snapshot can contain those shapes from another pool, or an incomplete reference, so the parent fails at the result boundary.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/87
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Parallel subagent results can fail the parent run with Invalid or cross-pool reference

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Enabling scientific connectors (`arxiv`, `pubmed`) on a Session persists `enabledConnectorIds`, and `/api/connectors` lists those sources, but the live agent tool set can still contain **no** `mcp__arxiv__*` / `mcp__pubmed__*` tools. Literature runs then fall back to `web_search` only. This breaks the documented contract that Session-enabled MCP sources become governed agent tools (control-plane MCP, outside the sandbox).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** local instance.
2. Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["arxiv","pubmed"]` (and typically `web`).
3. Confirm `/api/connectors` returns arXiv/PubMed manifests (`enabledByDefault: false`, `requestedCapabilities: ["mcp"]`, NCBI/arXiv `networkHosts`).
4. Run a literature workflow that activates `literature-searcher` (or ask the main agent to search PubMed/arXiv via MCP).
5. Observe run events / agent reports: **no** literature MCP tool calls; agent/subagent states that no literature-search MCP tool is present; only `web_search` (and failed `web_fetch`) are used.

Observed on session `27148ad0…`, run `dad3a25d…`.

## Expected

- If a connector id is in the Session’s effective `enabledConnectorIds` and the MCP source is **ready**, the corresponding tools (`mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>`, e.g. `mcp__pubmed__search`, `mcp__arxiv__search`) must appear in the agent/subagent tool set (native: deferred directory + promotion; JiuwenSwarm: promoted at start per docs).
- If the underlying MCP server/catalog is **unavailable** or **degraded**, enabling the connector must not look “on with tools”; the run/UI/agent should surface catalog status (or refuse the enablement path) instead of silently omitting tools while checkboxes stay enabled.

## Actual

Session JSON and connector catalog UI/API show arXiv/PubMed enabled/listed, but `createMcpWorkspaceTools` injects nothing for those sources when `McpSourceCatalog.getStatus(...).availableTools` is empty. The agent proceeds with an empty MCP tool list and no hard error tied to the enabled connectors.

## Code pointers

Injection chain (also documented in `docs/zh/developer-docs/science-connectors.md` §3):

1. **Session enablement** → `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` passes `enabledSourceIds: settingsSnapshot.enabledConnectorIds` into `createMcpWorkspaceTools` (after `filterEnabledMcpSources` for plugin master/per-connector switches).
2. **Catalog gate** → `packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` (`createMcpWorkspaceTools`): keeps only tools in `catalog.getStatus(sourceId).availableTools`. Empty `availableTools` ⇒ no tools for that source.
3. **Why `availableTools` can be empty** → `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts` (`statusFor` / `getStatus`):
   - Catalog never refreshed → status `unavailable`, `availableTools: []`, error *"MCP catalog has not been refreshed"*.
   - MCP server `biomed` missing/disabled/errored → same empty list (`transport.mcpServerId: "biomed"` in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`).
   - Remote `listTools` missing or schema-incompatible with local `mcpToolName` (e.g. `pubmed_search`, `arxiv_search`) → `degraded` / tool omitted.
4. **Startup soft-fail** → `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`: `mcpCatalog.refresh().catch(...)` only warns; API keeps running with an empty/failed catalog while `/api/connectors` still lists manifests from the registry (no status). Status lives on `/api/mcp/sources` instead.
5. **Deferred visibility** (native) → `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` marks MCP tools `deferred: true`. That only applies to tools that survived step 2; it does not explain a completely empty MCP set.

Related but separate: skill scripts under `skills/literature-searcher/scripts/*` need `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXTERNAL_URLS_PATH` / `config/external-urls.json` in the sandbox; that does **not** replace MCP injection. Skill docs say to use session MCP tools and not bundled scripts for literature search.

## Impact

- Users believe PubMed/arXiv are connected; retrieval silently degrades to web snippets.
- `literature-searcher` cannot fulfill its MCP-first contract.
- Hard to debug without checking `/api/mcp/sources` status vs Session checkboxes.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Treat “enabled but catalog unavailable/degraded” as a first-class Session/run signal (surface status next to connector toggles; emit a run warning or block start when every enabled literature source has zero `availableTools`).
- Ensure bundled `biomed` stdio MCP from `extensions_config.json` is healthy before advertising connectors as usable.
- Optionally include catalog status in `/api/connectors` so the UI cannot show “enabled” without readiness.

## Labels

bug, needs triage
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Session enabledConnectorIds (arxiv/pubmed) does not expose MCP tools to the agent

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
Revising a Markdown report can drop its Evidence chips, so the next review treats the same citations as unresolved and starts another revision loop.

## Expected

If a new version of a report still contains an `[evidenceN]` marker, and this run did not publish a replacement mapping, keep the version-scoped Evidence reference from the previous version. Do not keep a marker that the new text deleted. The first revised version should still open the Memory chips, and a quick evidence check should not report `CITATION_EVIDENCE_ALIAS_UNRESOLVED` for citations that did not change.

## Actual

After Reviewer returns `REVISE_AND_RETRY`, the lead edits the same report and declares a new artifact version without calling `declare_claim` again for the unchanged citations. The new text still shows `[evidenceN]`, but that version's `references` can be empty. The next quick check then flags every remaining marker.

`SessionStore` copies the base version's references only when `baseVersionId` is set and the caller does not pass its own `references` (`services/api/src/store.ts`). `declareWorkspaceArtifact` otherwise attaches only the references drained from this run's claim calls (`packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts`). A declaration that names the artifact and omits `base_version_id` therefore stores no references. When `base_version_id` is set, every previous reference is copied, including aliases the new text removed.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/108
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A revised report can lose Evidence chips unless base_version_id is set

- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What I was trying to do:** On a laptop screen, open a session with an in-progress Plan and read the progress in the right-hand Tasks panel (e.g. “3/8 completed · 3 in progress” and the Active badge).

**What I saw:** The Plan card in the workspace sidebar is clipped. The **Active / 进行中 badge is cut off on the right**, and the plan body runs off the edge. Progress is not fully readable at laptop width.

*(Screenshot of the clipped Plan card is in [GitCode #106](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/106).)*

The screenshot shows “Plan · main / 3/8 completed · 3 in progress” with the status badge sliced, and the English summary overflowing on the right.

**Expected**

- At typical laptop widths, the Plan card (title, progress summary, status badge, body) stays fully inside the sidebar.
- When space is tight, wrap or use the available width; do not clip the badge or body.
- Plan semantics stay the same; this is display only.

Not GitCode [#93](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/93) (left chrome stacking at ~900px). This is **clipping inside** the right-hand Plan card.

**Reproduction**

1. On a laptop resolution (≈13–14″ fullscreen, or a window clearly narrower than an external monitor), open a Session with an in-progress Plan.
2. Expand Workspace → Tasks.
3. Check whether “Plan · main” clips the status badge and body on the right edge.

Code pointer (not the acceptance surface): `.workspace-plan-section` titles use nowrap + ellipsis; the badge is nowrap. On a narrow sidebar the heading and body overflow instead of using the available width.

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Browser: Chrome
- UI language: Simplified Chinese
- Viewport: laptop screen, workspace sidebar open, Plan in progress

### Additional Information

The screenshot also shows the Tasks fold heading twice. If that shares the overflow cause, fix it here; if it is a separate duplicate fold, it can be another issue and must not block “progress is not fully visible.”

Current product UI (recent `openJiuwen/sciencediscovery` main behavior).
