## 范围与证据

汇总 [2026-10-24 Nightly run 40121906605](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605) 的三项剩余问题。运行版本：`9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`。

#514 / #515 修复的 Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 依赖准备已通过，本次不再作为阻塞项。以下区分实际运行结果与源码诊断，不据此认定所有 main CI 都失败。

## 1. real research-8 的会话标题断言未跟随显示规则更新

[失败 job 120955308760](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955308760) 已实际执行该用例，在点击 Add session 后失败：

- [`issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts:221`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/test/issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts#L219-L228) 期望 `Untitled session`，实际为 `Untitled session 2`。
- #510 已合入同一 Project 多个未命名会话显示序号的行为，实际标题与该规则一致。当前证据支持“测试期望过时”，不能据此认定产品的计划/子任务功能损坏。
- 此前的计划、follow-up、reload 断言已通过；失败后的切回原会话及位置保持断言尚未执行，不能算通过。
- #511 仍讨论编号集合与排序的 UX 口径，本 issue 不替它决定方案，只修复测试对已实现显示规则的错误假设。

## 2. 已执行失败的分片被汇总成 NOT_RUN

[research-8 结果 artifact 12574909042](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12574909042) 的 `e2e-real/tagged/summary.json` 明确记录：

- planned=1、executed=1、passed=0、failed=1；
- 该身份的 `outcome=FAIL`。

但 [汇总 job 120992446082](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120992446082) 输出 executed=18/19、passed=18，并将该用例标为 `NOT_RUN`。

源码诊断：[`.ci/real-report.mjs:19-24`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/.ci/real-report.mjs#L19-L24) 在失败分片的 `results.push(...summary.results)` 之前抛出 `SHARD_FAILED`，丢掉了其已执行结果。需要保留身份、版本、digest 等校验通过的失败证据，同时继续让 gate 失败。该运行应准确呈现 19 executed、18 passed、1 failed，而不是将执行失败混同为未运行。

## 3. 两项 UT 等待完成超时，原因待查

[UT job 120955273894](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955273894)：4754 planned / 4754 executed / 4752 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped。

[UT artifact 12572160563](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12572160563) 中的实际失败：

- `ut/tagged/group-279/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` 的 `a measured run is staged before the sidecar is asked to start`，报 `timed out waiting for the run to settle`。
- `ut/tagged/group-343/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/server.test.ts` 的 `running sessions accept queued runs and start them after the active run completes`，报等待 run 进入 `completed` 超时。

[同一 SHA 较早的 UT job 120785725594](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40064771478/job/120785725594) 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上 4754/4754 通过。现有证据不能区分测试时序、环境或产品状态推进问题，不认定为负载抖动或确定性回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 会话切换测试按当前显示规则及明确的 Session 身份校验，补齐“新增会话 → 切回原会话 → 原计划/时间线位置保持”的验证；不删除原行为断言。
- [ ] 为汇总器补充“分片实际执行但失败”的无模型回归测试，保留 executed/failed 计数和失败身份；身份不匹配、缺失、重复、跳过等情况仍不得放行。
- [ ] 使用上述已有结果验证汇总应为 19 executed / 18 passed / 1 failed，退出码仍非零；不通过跳过失败分片把 gate 改绿。
- [ ] 分别定位两项 UT 超时，保留最后运行状态及相关事件等诊断证据，补充针对性回归验证；仅延长超时或重跑成功不能作为已定位的证据。

本 issue 基于已有日志、artifact 与源码核对，未触发新的付费模型调用或 CI 重跑。

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.
items.title: bug: Embedded JiuwenSwarm must not adopt standalone config via env or discovery

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
PR #460 isolates the embedded JiuwenSwarm default local runtime under `$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm` and documents Docker’s persisted HOME layout. Local coexistence was verified; the **Docker persisted-volume restart** journey was **BLOCKED** (no container engine/socket on the author host) and remains an explicit leftover acceptance item on #257 / #460.

## Expected
After a container restart that keeps the documented persisted volume, ScienceDiscovery’s embedded Swarm registry, workspaces, and related runtime state remain under the SD-owned layout, still isolated from any standalone Swarm data, and SD continues to use its own instance endpoints without adopting a sibling standalone instance.

## Verification cases

1. **Docker volume restart persistence**
   - **Preconditions:** Container-capable host; ScienceDiscovery Docker path with persisted volume as documented after #460; disposable standalone Swarm data available to prove non-interference if co-tested.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start SD via the Docker path; record embedded registry/workspace identity and a distinguishing config marker.
     2. Restart the container with the same persisted volume.
     3. Confirm SD still binds to the same embedded instance data and does not read/write standalone Swarm registry/config.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Persisted SD state survives restart; isolation from standalone Swarm holds; no silent reconnect to another Swarm service.

## Context
- Env: Author host for #460 lacked container engine/socket; residual Docker journey _not provided_ here beyond that BLOCKED note.
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Local default-namespace isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks Docker restart verification only.

## Overview

This issue is the **October 2026 release calendar** for the ScienceDiscovery community. It is intended to serve as the **pinned, single source of truth** for release milestones and community review meetings.

**Key milestones**
- **Oct 10:** `v0.3.0` release kickoff and `v0.3.0-rc1` requirements review.
- **Oct 16:** `v0.3.0-rc1` release exit.
- **Oct 30:** `v0.3.0` official release exit.

| Requirement | Scope | Target release(s) | Tracking issue | Owner | Review level |

## October schedule

## Community review meetings

The community review meetings on **Oct 13, 20, 22, and 27** cover:

- **Design review** — review technical design and architecture changes.
- **Code review** — discuss implementation quality, correctness, and readiness to merge.

## Purpose

Track the remaining research-team budget and cancellation integration validation for v0.4.0, split from #239 at the user's request. The classification fix in #239 is implemented by merged PR #426 (`7b93f92e898dca1798595fd2fa320c23887e1565`). Closing #239 does not mean the full BRCA1 journey has been revalidated.

## Existing evidence

On a post-merge snapshot (`0c6fa3fb47ccac3b69e870ac7fddc4ee00a51853`), these commands passed 61/61 tests with no paid model calls:

```sh
node --import tsx --test test/helpers/real-delivery.unit.ts scripts/real-e2e-scoring.test.mjs .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs
```

They cover active delivery classification, terminal missing-output failures, scoring, and safe result packaging. They do not execute the full team-spec timeout branch or establish its persisted metrics/cancellation outcomes. PR #426's L3 evidence is not a replacement for the L4 BRCA1 journey.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add and run a deterministic integration test using a local model stub and a short budget, exercising the actual team journey timeout path rather than only helper functions.
- [ ] Verify persisted `team-metrics.json` distinguishes budget exhaustion (`integration=timed_out`) from terminal delivery failure and retains budget, elapsed duration, cancellation request, shutdown outcome, and actual terminal status.
- [ ] Verify cleanup stops the main run, children, pending wakeups, and relevant executions; retain diagnostic evidence on cleanup failure.
- [ ] Cover the terminal race: cancellation coincides with completion, while budget-exhaustion attribution remains correct.
- [ ] Preserve normal delivery contracts: successful completion requires readable, nonempty final artifacts; terminal missing/empty/unreadable output remains a delivery failure.
- [ ] Run or inspect a post-fix L4/Nightly `TC-E2E-01` BRCA1 journey at its configured team budget. Record the immutable SHA, command/configuration, final artifacts, persisted metrics, cancellation outcomes where applicable, and actual passed/failed/blocked/skipped counts. A successful normal completion alone does not cover the timeout branch.

## Execution constraints

The current instruction permits only verification without paid model calls. Do not start a billable model/judge run without authorization; an already scheduled post-fix Nightly may provide the real-journey evidence. Keep unexecuted scenarios explicitly pending.

## Scope

This is validation follow-up for v0.4.0. Any newly discovered product defect should be documented with reproduction evidence and linked here. Related: #239, #426.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What happened

A long real research run can end with only this text on the page:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · interaction round execution failed
```

The sentence before the dot is `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`. The detail after the dot is the fixed string `interaction round execution failed`. In the DeepAgent interaction-round handler that string replaces the caught exception: the handler logs the exception and returns `error_code=round_execution_error` with that fixed message. The original exception does not reach the page or the E2E log.

Observed runs, both with an empty final answer and `delivery.status` `"failed"`:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-62**, 23.7 minutes. One subagent completed. The session had `literature_sources.json` and showed 271K usage and 20 executions. The required `deepresearchbench-62.md` was not delivered. Run status was `failed`.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`6d3c49a8`), **DRB-58**, 21.0 minutes. Run status was `failed`. The session had `literature_sources.json`, `hgt_animals_sources.md`, and `hgt_plants_sources.md`. One child was `completed` and another was still `running`. A PubMed call had returned HTTP 429 from `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov`. Literature-connector 429s are already tracked in #208.

The same DRB-62 passed on the beta run (36.1 minutes), and the same DRB-58 passed on the main run (51.0 minutes). The model and gateway had already served those sessions for about 20 minutes, so this is not a wrong API key or a missing model id.

## Expected

The failed round keeps the underlying exception message (gateway status, tool error, or runtime exception) in the run error that the page and the test can read. A round that ran for many minutes is not described only as a model-configuration rejection.

## Evidence limits

The server log for these two runs was not retrieved, so the exception that was swallowed is not known. The page text and the run status are known.
items.title: bug: A failed model round is shown only as "interaction round execution failed"

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
items.title: [Bug]: Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

### Problem

2. **The website installation page lacks a version selector and defaults to an outdated version.** Version 0.3 is available, but the installation page still defaults to 0.2. Users cannot select a release version directly on the page and may install an older version unintentionally.

- Default to the latest stable release, currently 0.3.
- Keep download links and installation commands consistent with the selected version.
- Update the default version when a new stable release becomes available.

- [ ] The website installation page provides a version selector.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Background

We want to automate the workflow from issue submission through code changes, review, and PR merge. This requires clear repository conventions so contributors and automation can determine whether an issue is ready for implementation, whether a change meets its acceptance criteria, and whether a PR is ready to merge.

The existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers development setup, test commands, E2E testing, and some PR requirements. Extend it with issue, commit, review, and merge conventions, supported by templates and checks that all contributors can use.

### Scope

#### 1. Issue requirements

Provide templates for feature requests, bug reports, and other supported issue types. Identify required and conditional fields:

- Background, the problem to solve, and the expected outcome.
- Functional specifications, including inputs, outputs, behavior, boundary conditions, and applicable compatibility requirements.
- Scope and explicit exclusions.
- Verifiable acceptance scenarios with preconditions, actions, and expected results. Cover success, failure, permissions, and recovery where relevant.
- Reproduction steps, environment, actual behavior, and expected behavior for bug reports.
- Dependencies, open questions, and blockers that must be resolved before implementation.

Include a complete example and define when an issue is ready for development. Clarify ambiguities that affect implementation or acceptance before work begins. Update the issue when the specification changes during implementation.

#### 2. Commit and PR requirements

Document branch, commit, and PR conventions:

- Follow the existing fork and target-branch workflow, and define naming and commit message formats.
- Link the PR to its issue and explain the reason, resulting behavior, and scope.
- Map each issue acceptance criterion to its implementation and validation result.
- Provide reproducible test commands, results, and supporting evidence. Distinguish tests that were not run, failed, were blocked, or were skipped.
- Describe compatibility impact, configuration changes, data migration, and rollback where applicable.
- Update affected documentation and follow the existing release label requirements.

#### 3. Review and merge requirements

Provide a shared review checklist and define:

- Checks for specification compliance, acceptance coverage, correctness, module boundaries, and applicable security and compatibility requirements.
- The distinction between blocking findings and suggestions, including how findings are resolved.
- Responsibilities for automated and human review, including approval authority.
- Which checks and approvals must be repeated after a PR changes.
- Conditions for entering the merge queue and completing the merge, consistent with the existing CI and `merge-gate` mechanism.

#### 4. Rule checks

Maintain a rule list that states applicability, verification method, execution stage, and failure handling for each rule. Include:

- Required issue and PR information and their linkage.
- Type checks, tests, user-perspective E2E testing, and documentation checks.
- License headers, sensitive information, temporary files, and generated files.
- Module dependency boundaries and compatibility requirements.
- Required checks, review decisions, and unresolved blockers.

Enforce rules through templates or CI where they can be checked programmatically. Provide explicit instructions for rules that require human judgment. Unavailable test prerequisites must be reported as blocked. Document the reason, approver, and follow-up for any exception.

### Deliverables

- Extend `CONTRIBUTING.md` as the common entry point, linking to separate documents where needed.
- Add issue templates, a PR template, and a review checklist.
- Provide a feature issue example and a corresponding PR acceptance report example.
- Map rules to automated checks, distinguishing existing checks, checks added in this work, and follow-up work.
- Resolve duplicated or conflicting guidance and identify where each rule is maintained.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contributors can find issue, commit, PR, review, and merge requirements from one entry point.
- [ ] The feature template requires functional specifications and verifiable acceptance scenarios; the bug template requires reproduction details.
- [ ] The PR template requires an issue link, per-criterion acceptance results, and test evidence.
- [ ] The review checklist defines blocking findings, approval responsibilities, and re-review requirements.
- [ ] Merge conditions are consistent with the existing CI, merge queue, and `merge-gate` contract.
- [ ] Important rules specify applicability, verification, and failure or exception handling.
- [ ] At least one complete issue-to-PR example is included.
- [ ] New or changed templates and automated checks are validated, and documentation checks pass.

This issue covers the guidelines, templates, and agreed checks. Implementation of the complete automation system can be tracked separately.
items.title: Complete contribution guidelines for the workflow from issues to PR merge

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
A Windows durability fix for CAS directory `fsync` (`O_RDWR` on `win32` because `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle) and `toNamespacedPath` for SQLite paths landed inside the conversational-configuration protocol PR (#553), mixed with unrelated schema/protocol work. On Linux the `win32` branch is never taken, so CI here cannot exercise the failure mode (silently weaker directory sync if the open/handle is wrong).

## Expected
- CAS Windows durable-directory sync ships in its own small PR (or clearly scoped commit series) with Windows verification attached.
- Configuration/protocol PRs do not carry unrelated CAS durability changes.

## Verification cases
1. **Writable-directory sync on Windows**
   - Preconditions: Windows host; CAS `VersionStore` / `RefStore` initialized on a normal NTFS directory.
   - Steps: Create/update a live ref that triggers `syncDirectory`; confirm no throw from `open(..., O_RDWR|O_DIRECTORY)` + `handle.sync()`.
   - Expected / pass: Operation succeeds; refs.sqlite and object dirs remain consistent after process kill mid-write (WAL + FULL sync still hold).
2. **Long / namespaced path**
   - Preconditions: Windows; store path that needs `\\?\` / namespaced form (deep or near-MAX_PATH tree).
   - Steps: Open `RefStore` / lease DBs via the same helpers.
   - Expected / pass: `DatabaseSync(toNamespacedPath(...))` opens; no path-not-found solely from missing namespace prefix.
3. **Negative — read-only directory**
   - Preconditions: Directory without write ACL for the process.
   - Steps: Trigger `syncDirectory`.
   - Expected / pass: Failure is loud (thrown/propagated), not a silent no-op sync; caller sees the error.
4. **Linux unchanged**
   - Preconditions: Linux CI/dev.
   - Steps: Same CAS unit/integration paths as today.
   - Expected / pass: Still uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`; no behavioral change.

## Context
Refs #553 (CAS hunks in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`, `workspace-lease.ts`, `workspace-lifecycle.ts`). Spotted during review of the four-PR configuration stack; out of scope for the shared configuration protocol.
items.title: CAS: isolate Windows durable-directory sync (O_RDWR + toNamespacedPath) from feature stacks

## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #91](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/91) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Start the server and confirm "I can actually run analyses now".

## What I saw instead

- On Linux, when sandbox (bwrap) probing fails (e.g. the host disables unprivileged user namespaces), `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` only prints a `WARNING` line; `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` ignores the result, keeps starting, and finally prints `ScienceDiscovery is ready at ...`.
- The green connection dot in the top bar only means the frontend can talk to the local API (`Connection OK`). It says nothing about sandbox availability, the scientific Python environment, or model quota.
- Users believe everything is ready, then the run fails mid-analysis — often with raw low-level errors.

## Why this is confusing

"Ready" and the green light create false confidence; the failure happens only after the user has invested time writing a prompt and uploading data.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- When startup preflight finds the sandbox unusable, surface a prominent in-app notice ("analyses cannot run in this environment", with the reason) instead of a single terminal warning.
- Separate "frontend connected" from "compute ready" in the status indicator.
- Open question (needs a product decision): when compute is unavailable, should the app block new analyses entirely, or allow read-only browsing of past sessions and artifacts? The two strategies differ a lot in UX; decide before implementing.

Design note: the preflight result already exists in the startup chain (`runPreflight`); what is missing is exposing it to the web UI and layering the status display.
items.title: [Feature]: Sandbox unavailability only warns in the terminal while serve still reports ready; surface real compute readiness

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What happened

Nightly real-model E2E fails the whole Daily gate when a single request to the configured OpenAI-compatible model gateway returns a provider error. Other cases in the same job still pass, and the same case can pass on another run the same night.

On 2026-10-06, main Nightly run [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`) executed 10 real cases: 5 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped, in 3.0 hours. The job uses `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` and `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL=https://yibuapi.com/v1`. Playwright is configured with `retries: 0` and one worker.

Three of those failures were gateway responses, and the product already showed them:

- **DRB-75** failed in 9.3 seconds. No subagent and no tool call ran. The page showed error 181001: HTTP 500 from the gateway, body `Database error, please contact the administrator`, type `new_api_error`.
- **PUCT-COMPRESS** failed in 11.5 seconds with the same HTTP 500 text in `run.error`. No search started.
- **workspace plan and run-anchored subagent** failed after 7.0 minutes. The page already showed HTTP 503: `No available channel for model deepseek-v4-flash under group default (distributor)`, code `model_not_found`, wrapped as the same 181001 gateway error. The test then waited out a 420 second timeout for a plan section that never appeared.

The other five cases in that job passed, including DRB-58 after 51.0 minutes and TC-E2E-01 after 43.0 minutes. The same three cases passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`releases/v0.3.0.beta` at `6d3c49a8`) the same night. The previous night, that same beta commit passed all 10 real cases in [37382672011](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37382672011).

## Why this is a product/CI problem

The gateway is failing one request at a time, not the whole job. A 500 or 503 still fails the real-E2E job, which fails Nightly. There is no retry, and the suite does not record these as an external provider fault separate from a product regression.

## Expected

A transient gateway 500 or 503 is visible as that provider error. One such request does not have the same meaning as a product run that finished and failed to deliver. Cases that passed in the same job stay visible as passes.

## Evidence limits

This does not say the gateway was down for the whole job. It also does not cover the research cases that ran for about 20 minutes and then ended without a report; those are separate failures.
items.title: bug(ci): Nightly real E2E fails the gate on one transient model-gateway 500 or 503

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Summary

Biomni real E2E shows large endpoint-dependent variation in model-request latency and total generation time. Earlier runs through an OpenAI-compatible relay also ended after a terminal model turn with no text or tool call. We need enough safe wire-level diagnostics to tell an upstream empty completion from an SSE/parser defect, and to separate model/API latency from agent work.

This is distinct from #232, which records explicit HTTP 500/503 gateway errors.

## Local measurements

The two Biomni cases were run in parallel on the same Windows/WSL machine, with evaluation disabled, the `task` tool removed (no subagents), and no Jina key. `generation` is the benchmark's generation duration; request timing is the elapsed time of completed `[model-stream]` requests in `stack.log`. All rows below passed delivery. The relay run used `https://yibuapi.com/v1` with model alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the direct runs used `https://api.deepseek.com` with model alias `deepseek-flash`.

| Case | Endpoint / runs | Generation | Completed model requests | Median request | Reported total tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | relay, r5 | 37.46 min | 71 | 25.16 s | 504,634 |
| DA-13-3 | direct, r6/r7/r9/r10 | 5.71–20.67 min | 26–44 | 6.10–13.93 s | 118,066–140,022 |
| DA-14-1 | relay, r5 | 31.31 min | 63 | 20.18 s | 177,043 |
| DA-14-1 | direct, r6/r9/r10 | 20.75–35.79 min | 54–72 | 11.59–19.01 s | 191,883–284,635 |

The seven direct samples all passed delivery, with zero reported SSE parse errors or SSE error records. Earlier local relay samples had a normalized final model turn with empty text, no tool call, and `finish_reason=stop`, after which the run was marked completed without the expected deliverable. Those older samples did **not** retain raw SSE records, so they cannot establish whether the upstream service sent an empty completion or the local stream adapter lost content. The direct samples also used a local empty-turn guard and SSE parsing fixes, so the passing rate is **not** an isolated endpoint A/B result.

## Why the current evidence is insufficient

- The relay and direct runs used different model aliases. The model's chosen steps, request counts, and token totals varied substantially, so total-duration differences are not an estimate of API latency alone.
- Even with the same direct endpoint, DA-13-3 varied from 5.71 to 20.67 minutes, and DA-14-1 from 20.75 to 35.79 minutes. Agent behavior and task content remain major contributors.
- A normalized empty final turn does not reveal whether the wire response was empty, malformed, or incorrectly mapped locally.

## Requested investigation / acceptance criteria

1. Save privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts: endpoint identity and model alias, request ID, HTTP status, dispatch/headers/first byte/first SSE record/completion timestamps, SSE record and parse-error counts, final content/tool-call presence, `finish_reason`, and retry/error classification. Do not save credentials or prompt/response bodies in the default diagnostic log.
2. Treat an empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call as an error rather than a successful final answer. Preserve the upstream request ID and framing summary when this occurs.
3. Compare relay and direct endpoints with the same model, request body, workload, and concurrency. Report per-request latency distributions separately from total agent duration and token use.
4. In CI summaries, identify explicit provider failures, empty completions, and local parse/mapping failures separately from research-quality failures.

I can provide the local benchmark metrics and sanitized `[model-stream]`/`[model-sse-summary]` excerpts if useful. No API keys or prompt contents are included here.
items.title: perf(model): investigate endpoint-dependent Biomni latency and empty terminal turns

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What happened

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is a test-only variable. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1` whenever the backend is JiuwenSwarm, together with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=task`. Twelve specs then gate on it: `expect(process.env.E2E_SWARM_TASK !== "1", "BLOCKED: …").toBe(false)`. No product code reads it.

The precondition it stands for is real: these journeys exercise sub-agents delegated through the platform `task` tool (sandbox, deliverables, sub-agent cards), and some of them exercise JiuwenSwarm itself. As a switch, though, it does not do that job:

- It is a declaration, not a check. A stack started with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=jiuwenswarm`, the one configuration where the precondition fails, still passes if someone exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1`.
- In CI it is always `1` on the default backend, so it never stops anything there.
- It blocks journeys that do not depend on JiuwenSwarm. The built-in (native) loop also delegates through the platform `task` tool, but DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on it unless the variable is set by hand.
- Anyone running a real journey by hand has to remember it; three benchmark READMEs say so.
- `deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` and `biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts` write `backend: "jiuwenswarm"` into their score metrics as a constant, so a native run is labelled as JiuwenSwarm.

## Proposal

- `/health` (and `/api/health`) reports how the stack runs agent turns, from the API's own configuration: `agent: { executor: "jiuwenswarm" | "native", subagents: "task" | "jiuwenswarm" }`. The native loop always delegates through `task`. The API is the component that makes this decision in both modes; the adapter's `/agent/info` does not exist when the stack runs natively.
- One E2E helper reads it. Real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require platform `task` delegation on either executor. Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour (`swarm-*`, `literature-review-*`, `artifact-revision`) also require the `jiuwenswarm` executor. A mismatch is reported as BLOCKED with what the stack actually reported.
- `E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `run-e2e.sh`, the specs and the READMEs.
- Score metrics record the executor the stack reported, not a constant.
- `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE`, `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION`, `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY` stay. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Problem

ScienceDiscovery exposes many settings, but a user working in a conversation often does not know which page or field will unblock the current task. For example, adding a model API can require entering a service URL/key, registering a model, selecting its scope, and returning to the original request. A settings-page wizard for initial model connection was proposed in #39; this issue covers **configuration discovered during a task and completed inside the conversation**.

## Proposed experience

Keep existing valid settings and defaults. When a concrete task is blocked by a supported missing capability, or the user explicitly asks for a change:

1. The Agent explains the need in the context of the task and proposes **one specific change**. It pre-fills facts it knows and asks only for missing fields.
2. An in-conversation card shows the current → proposed value, where a resource will be saved, where it will be used (session/project/global), the target service or file, and any connection test or other external action.
3. The user fills in any remaining URL, credential, supported path, or selection and clicks **“Confirm configuration and continue”** (or declines). This one action confirms the fully visible change and the continuation intent.
4. A trusted configuration service validates, tests as disclosed, applies, and then resumes the task. A validation error remains on the card for correction. The result separately reports **saved**, **effective for the task**, and **task resumed/queued**.

For example: “This image analysis needs a vision-capable model. Add this supported model service with its API URL and key, test the selected model, save the provider in this deployment, and use the model in this session.” If an existing vision model is available, offer a one-click session selection instead.

The normal settings pages remain available for inspection and manual management. A usable default should never trigger a configuration interruption merely because another option might be better.

## V1 scope

- Select an already configured model for the current session.
- Add a model connection through an **already supported provider/protocol**, provide or repair its credential, verify it, and bind a selected model to the session. Creating a provider resource does **not** silently change the global default.
- Enable an installed, already configured connector for the session. Its later tool calls still follow the existing execution-permission rules.
- Show the same card without relying on the Agent when no model is configured or the current model's authentication has failed; preserve the user's first task and start it once configuration succeeds.
- Persist card state across refresh/reconnect and continue through a linked follow-up run when the active run's model/tool snapshot must change.

A URL alone must not be treated as a usable arbitrary REST tool. New HTTP/SSE MCP connections, OAuth, controlled file/environment imports, and deployment-wide proxy/timeout changes can follow with dedicated adapters. STDIO commands, host execution, restart-required deployment settings, and arbitrary REST adaptation need separate review.

## Design constraints

- The Agent may inspect a **redacted** capability catalog and create a structured proposal. Only a user-bound decision endpoint may approve it; the Agent must not receive a generic settings-write tool or claim user consent through another tool.
- Secrets use dedicated fields and encrypted backend storage. Plaintext keys must not enter chat messages, model context, tool traces, SSE events, ordinary logs, or browser persistence. A local browser path is not a server path; any supported file import must show the exact environment and read scope.
- Show the real save scope and effective-use scope. Prefer a session override when supported; disclose shared-resource or global effects before confirmation. Do not invent a session-only option for a system-wide setting.
- Bind approval to a proposal revision and concrete target, diff, scope, and verification plan. Re-preview after concurrent setting changes. External probes or reads require explicit disclosure; failed validation must leave the effective configuration intact.
- Do not hot-swap an in-flight run's snapshot by assumption. Finish or stop at a safe boundary, account for pending tools and side effects, then create an idempotent linked continuation using the approved new snapshot. Stop/cancel must suppress automatic continuation. Saved configuration and resumed execution are distinct states.
- An undo action should preview the reverse change and use version checks; it must not overwrite later edits or delete a shared resource still in use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing valid configuration remains unchanged and completes a task without a card.
- [ ] A supported missing model API can be entered, confirmed, verified, saved, and used to continue from the conversation, without visiting settings.
- [ ] Selecting an existing vision model changes only the intended scope; other sessions and global defaults remain unchanged.
- [ ] Invalid credentials do not replace the current working connection; a corrected submission applies once. Supported keyless local endpoints also work.
- [ ] No-model and authentication-failure entry points work without asking a broken model to diagnose itself.
- [ ] Plaintext secrets never appear in messages, events, logs, tool history, or model requests; Agent calls cannot approve a proposal.
- [ ] The displayed resource location, effective scope, target, and possible verification cost match what the backend actually does.
- [ ] Decline/cancel does not repeatedly re-prompt for the same need; a blocked task has a clear reason and any viable alternative.
- [ ] Double-clicks, refresh, SSE replay, retries, and restart recovery create at most one configuration application and one continuation run.
- [ ] Concurrent settings edits make the old proposal stale instead of overwriting the newer value.
- [ ] The old run keeps its historical snapshot; the linked continuation uses the approved new snapshot, preserves the goal and completed artifacts, and does not replay non-idempotent actions.
- [ ] Validation, save, and continuation failures have separate truthful states and phase-specific recovery.
- [ ] Stop, session switching, archival, and deletion cannot apply a proposal in the wrong session or restart a stopped task.
- [ ] Undo restores the former override/inheritance relationship without clobbering subsequent changes or removing a resource used elsewhere.
- [ ] The card supports keyboard use, accessible errors, narrow screens, and Chinese/English text.

## Relation to existing work

#39 addresses a first-connection wizard in settings; this proposal adds task-contextual, Agent-assisted configuration and continuation. The current mainline backend work in #84 (including models/settings #91, chat/runs #89, and MCP #92) should determine the final service and event integration. The product behavior above is the contract; implementation paths and API shapes from the local design draft should be reconciled with current main before coding.

---

## 中文版

### 问题

ScienceDiscovery 有不少设置。用户正在对话里完成任务时，往往不知道哪个页面、哪个字段能够解决眼前的问题。例如接入模型 API，可能要填写服务地址和密钥、注册模型、选择作用范围，再回到原任务。#39 提出的是设置页中的首次模型接入向导；本 Issue 关注的是**任务进行中发现配置缺口，并在对话内完成配置**。

### 期望交互

默认沿用已有的有效配置。只有当前任务确实缺少受支持的能力，或用户主动要求修改时，才进入以下流程：

1. Agent 结合当前任务说明原因，提出**一项明确变更**。已知信息预填，只询问缺少的字段。
2. 对话卡片展示当前值 → 建议值、资源保存位置、实际使用范围（会话／项目／全局）、目标服务或文件，以及即将执行的连接测试等外部动作。
3. 用户补齐必要的地址、凭据、受支持的路径或选择后，点击「确认配置并继续」；也可以拒绝。这一次提交确认的是卡片中完整可见的变更和接续意图。
4. 可信配置服务按卡片说明校验、测试、应用配置，再接续任务。验证失败留在原卡片修正。结果分别说明**配置已保存**、**对任务已生效**、**任务已开始接续或进入队列**，不把三者混为一谈。

例如：「本次图片分析需要支持视觉的模型。请提供受支持的模型服务地址和 API Key；我会测试所选模型，在本部署保存服务，并仅将该模型用于当前会话。」如果已有可用视觉模型，应优先给出一次确认即可完成的会话级选择。

设置页继续作为集中查看和手动维护入口。只要默认配置能完成任务，就不应仅因为存在“更优”选项而打断用户。

### 首版范围

- 为当前会话选择已配置的模型。
- 通过**已有支持的提供方／协议**添加模型连接，补充或修复凭据，验证后把所选模型绑定到会话。新建提供方资源**不等于**悄悄修改全局默认模型。
- 为会话启用已安装、已配置的连接器；之后的实际工具调用仍遵守原有执行权限规则。
- 完全没有模型，或当前模型认证失败时，由确定性的前后端检查显示同类配置卡，不依赖失效模型诊断；保留用户的第一条任务，配置成功后只启动一次。
- 刷新或重连后恢复卡片状态；当前运行的模型或工具快照必须变化时，通过关联的后续运行接续任务。

仅提供一个 URL 不能自动把任意 REST API 变成可调用工具。新建 HTTP/SSE MCP 连接、OAuth、受控文件／环境变量导入，以及部署级代理和超时设置，可在具备专用适配器后逐项扩展。STDIO 命令、宿主执行入口、需要重启的部署设置及任意 REST API 适配需要单独评审。

### 设计边界

- Agent 只能读取**脱敏的**配置能力与状态，并创建结构化提案。只有绑定用户身份的决策接口能够批准；不给 Agent 通用写设置能力，也不能通过其他工具声称「用户已同意」。
- 密钥通过专用字段交给后端并加密保存。明文不得进入聊天消息、模型上下文、工具轨迹、SSE 事件、普通日志或浏览器持久存储。浏览器所在电脑的路径不能当成服务器路径；任何受支持的文件导入都要显示具体运行环境和读取范围。
- 如实展示资源保存范围与最终使用范围。确实支持会话级覆盖时优先只改当前会话；共享资源或全局变更必须提前说明影响。不能给只有系统级设置的项目伪造「仅本会话」选项。
- 用户确认绑定提案版本以及具体目标、差异、范围和验证计划。并发修改导致旧预览过期时应重新预览；外部探测或读取应明确告知；验证失败时保留原有效配置。
- 不能假定进行中的运行可以热切换配置快照。应在安全边界处理未完成的工具和副作用，再用经批准的新快照创建幂等的关联接续运行。用户停止或取消后不得自动接续；配置已保存与任务已继续必须分别记录。
- 「撤销本次配置」应预览反向变更并检查版本，不能覆盖之后的编辑，也不能删除仍被其他会话使用的共享资源。

### 验收标准

- [ ] 已有有效配置能够直接完成任务，不弹配置卡，也不改变原配置。
- [ ] 缺少受支持的模型 API 时，用户可在对话里补齐、确认、验证、保存并接续，无须打开设置页。
- [ ] 选用已有视觉模型时，只修改明确选择的范围；其他会话及全局默认保持不变。
- [ ] 错误凭据不会替换正常连接；修正后只应用一次。受支持的无 Key 本地端点也可使用。
- [ ] 无模型与认证失败都能进入配置流程，无须让失效模型再次诊断自己。
- [ ] 明文凭据不出现在消息、事件、日志、工具历史或模型请求中；Agent 调用不能替用户批准提案。
- [ ] 卡片显示的资源位置、生效范围、目标及可能产生费用的验证动作与后端实际行为一致。
- [ ] 拒绝或取消后不针对同一需求反复打扰；任务受阻时说明原因和可行的替代路径。
- [ ] 双击、刷新、SSE 重放、重试和服务重启至多产生一次配置应用和一个接续运行。
- [ ] 其他窗口修改配置后，旧提案标记为过期并重新预览，不覆盖新值。
- [ ] 旧运行保留历史快照；关联运行使用批准的新快照、原任务目标和已完成产物，不重放已执行的非幂等动作。
- [ ] 验证失败、保存失败和接续失败分别显示真实状态，并提供对应阶段的恢复操作。
- [ ] 停止、切换会话、归档和删除不会在错误会话应用配置，也不会重新启动已停止的任务。
- [ ] 撤销恢复原覆盖或继承关系，不覆盖后续修改，也不删除仍在使用的资源。
- [ ] 卡片支持键盘操作、可访问的错误提示、窄屏布局及中英文文案。

### 与已有工作的关系

#39 聚焦设置页中的首次连接向导；本提案增加任务上下文中的 Agent 协助配置、用户确认和任务接续。主仓当前的后端工作见 #84，其中模型与设置为 #91、对话与运行为 #89、MCP 为 #92。上述产品行为是需要实现的契约；正式开发前，具体服务归属、接口和事件方案应与当前主仓架构核对。

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## Summary

This issue is the delivery design for shipping ScienceDiscovery as a **desktop application on Windows and macOS**: one installer, one window, a first-run wizard, and automatic updates — with the code-execution and sandbox story settled per platform.

It is the design-level follow-up to #34 (desktop window) and #31 (Windows support), and it answers the questions those two left open: which shell framework, what to do about a Windows sandbox, how macOS gets a binary plus signing and notarization, and how updates reach installed apps. It also supplies the update mechanism asked for in #32.

## Where the product stands today

| Platform | Current state |
|---|---|
| Linux | Released binary and source mode; the UI is a browser tab on `127.0.0.1:4310`, reached with a bearer token. |
| macOS | Source mode only, officially supported on macOS 13+; sandbox is native (Seatbelt). No binary, no installer, no signing or notarization. |
| Windows | Not supported in any form. The existing `bubblewrap` + seccomp sandbox is Linux-only, and the runner, startup script, and binary packaging all assume a Linux or Darwin host. |

The practical effect: getting to a first screen means a terminal, a token copy-paste, and a browser tab, and a large group of researchers is excluded outright.

## Goals

- Download → install → wizard → working workspace, with no terminal, no token handling, and no manual environment setup.
- Windows covered without WSL being mandatory.
- Code execution stays inside the security contract the project already states, on both platforms.
- One shell codebase, one packaging pipeline, one release pipeline for both platforms.
- Installed apps keep themselves current.

## Non-goals for v1

- No Linux desktop build (Linux stays binary + browser).
- No forked frontend: the shell loads the same `apps/web` build against the same control API.
- No remote-execution provider on macOS. The remote link itself is cross-platform; only the Linux-hosted target ships with v1.
- No multi-instance support. Ports stay fixed and unique.
- No enterprise deployment formats (no Windows MSI, no macOS pkg).

## Root decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Shell | Electron, shared by both platforms | Same runtime family as the Node backend, identical rendering engine on every platform (the UI leans on Molstar, Plotly, Cytoscape), and the window, token injection, wizard, and orderly shutdown come for free. ~200 MB of memory is the accepted cost. |
| Execution environment | Windows: provider-based, direct execution by default, WSL and remote demoted to optional plugins. macOS: Seatbelt by default, fail-closed if unavailable, no remote. | On Windows the sandbox was always an interchangeable provider, so WSL becomes a plugin rather than the foundation — users who cannot install WSL are not shut out. On macOS the sandbox is already built into the OS and available on probe. |
| Bundling | Layered | Base package ~500–700 MB and works offline; large pieces (the WSL rootfs on Windows, heavy scientific dependencies) ship as on-demand plugin volumes; macOS ships per-architecture packages. |
| Architecture matrix | Windows: x64 only, tiered by OS version. macOS: 13+, arm64 as the mainline plus an x64 build. | Windows arm64 volumes do not justify the work yet, and direct execution has no hard WSL dependency, so older Windows versions remain covered. On macOS the conda scientific stack splits by architecture and a CPython/conda environment cannot be a universal binary. |
| Ordering | Windows is the first target platform, macOS the second. | Sharing the shell, packaging, and release pipeline costs the least when done once; macOS needs no backend adaptation and has a native sandbox, so it can reach internal beta sooner. |

## Execution model

### Shared

SD already models isolation as a replaceable enum — `bubblewrap` on Linux, `seatbelt` on macOS, chosen automatically by the backend. The desktop work adds a second, orthogonal question: **where** code runs.

### Windows: an execution-provider routing layer

- A routing layer above the existing sandbox enum answers "where does code run" with `windows-direct | wsl | remote`. The two layers stay independent: routing to WSL still isolates with bubblewrap inside it; routing to direct execution falls back to the approval mode because Windows has no OS-level sandbox. The existing enum does not change — new code is layered on top, so upstream merges continue to apply.
- **Capability probing, fail-closed.** The router assumes nothing about the machine: at startup it checks whether WSL is present, whether the private sandbox instance has been imported, and whether a remote host is configured. This reuses the existing sandbox-probe mechanism, caches the result for the session, and treats anything indeterminate as unavailable rather than routing on unknown state.
- **Hot switching.** Finishing a plugin install re-probes without restarting the backend. A persistent badge shows the active mode: sandboxed, direct, or remote.
- **Direct execution path.** The `run_shell` tool is bash-syntax and the model depends on it, so the bundled starter environment includes a bash compatibility layer (the MSYS2 port). Without it, direct execution could not run code at all.
- **Provider B (WSL plugin).** A trimmed, purpose-built Linux rootfs (~200 MB: bash, bubblewrap, system libraries, python3) imported under a dedicated instance name via `wsl --import`, bypassing the Store and its 1–2 GB download. Installation is a six-step state machine (detect → platform install → rootfs import → dependency check → network check → payload placement) with a journal after each step so an interrupted install resumes. A redistribution-compliance review of the Ubuntu base is required before this work starts; if it does not clear, the base moves to Debian.
- **No dead ends.** If the plugin cannot be installed, the user keeps direct execution, gets a specific failure reason with illustrated guidance, and has one-click rollback. Uninstalling the plugin deregisters the instance, clears the rootfs, and returns to direct execution with no residue.

### macOS: native sandbox, no routing layer

- macOS is a Unix platform; the backend stack already runs there in source mode, and Seatbelt is built in. The three heaviest pieces of the Windows plan — backend adaptation, the provider routing layer plus WSL plugin system, and the unsandboxed fallback — disappear or shrink sharply here.
- The default tier **is** the full sandbox. There are no plugins to install and no mode to switch; the mode badge stays visible and reads "sandboxed".
- If Seatbelt is unavailable (MDM-managed machines, nested sandboxing), the app fails closed with an explicit error and diagnostics. It does not degrade to unsandboxed execution the way Windows does.

## Packaging, signing, and distribution

| Area | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Toolchain | electron-builder — one configuration produces both platform targets | same |
| Installer | NSIS, per-user install under `%LocalAppData%\Programs`, no UAC elevation anywhere | Standard DMG drag to `/Applications`; no permission special-casing |
| Artifact naming | `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-win-x64-setup.exe` | `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-mac-<arch>.dmg`, plus `.zip` as the update carrier and a per-arch `latest-mac.yml` |
| Signing | Current version is unsigned. The next version may add Azure Trusted Signing (OIDC short-lived credentials in CI, no certificate on disk). Identity validation is officially ~3–5 business days and can stretch to weeks if materials are bounced, so the application has to start early. | Public distribution requires Developer ID + notarization (notarytool) + stapling. Internal beta may ship ad-hoc with `xattr -cr` guidance, switching to the notarized chain as soon as it is ready. Apple account and certificate lead time applies. |
| Runtime pinning | — | The macOS build needs a pinned runtime manifest: CPython (both architectures), uv (mac wheel), micromamba (osx-arm64/osx-64), and the starter environment, all by version and hash. Today the manifest pins Linux only. |
| Distribution | All downloads are GitHub Releases assets. The website `/install` page is the primary entry point and the Releases page the secondary one; both link the same assets. No domestic object storage or custom domain. Plugin packages ship the same way. | `/install` shows two download cards and pre-selects the architecture by user agent, with manual override. |
| Updates | electron-updater reading Releases assets, stable channel only to start, `latest.yml` + blockmap for delta updates. | The zip is the update carrier: electron-updater downloads the notarized zip, replaces the `.app`, and restarts. The DMG is not part of the update flow. |
| Update-source stability | The update URL is fixed from the first public release, because installed apps have it baked in. | same |
| Interception | SmartScreen: unsigned cold starts are accepted for now, with documented "More info → Run anyway" guidance. | Gatekeeper: notarization plus stapling removes the prompt entirely; no user guidance is needed once that chain is live. |

## First run

- Three-step wizard: data directory → model configuration (preset provider → API key → live connectivity test) → done.
- On Windows the wizard goes through direct execution only: no environment preparation, no WSL involvement.
- On macOS the final step folds in the sandbox self-check. A failure shows a specific error page with diagnostics and a way to submit them, and **does not** let the user into the main UI. Ordinary users never see this page.
- Data directory defaults: Windows splits by provider — direct execution uses `%LocalAppData%`, WSL uses ext4 inside the instance for I/O performance — with a custom option and a free-space check. macOS uses `~/Library/Application Support/ScienceDiscovery` and offers a one-time migration when a source-mode `~/.sciencediscovery-data` is found.
- Model keys: Windows stores them with DPAPI, because `0600` file permissions mean nothing on NTFS. macOS keeps the existing AES-256-GCM + `0600` scheme.
- The access token is injected before the page loads; a token entry page appears only as a 401 fallback.
- Background work during first run (environment unpacking, stack start) reports real progress by file and byte count, with conservative time estimates, and gates the next step on a self-check.

## Security baseline

Shared:

- Workspace-directory allowlist; network calls require explicit authorization (egress denied by default, allowlist to permit, refusals recorded).
- A persistent badge in the UI states the execution mode.
- Supply chain: updates over HTTPS with integrity checks (sha512 in the Windows update manifest; same-chain signing and notarization for the macOS update zip). **Once signing is live, no unsigned version is published again**, and a signature-identity change is covered by a dual-identity transition window.

Windows direct execution (no sandbox):

- The permission mode is locked to "ask on dangerous operations" and the user cannot switch to "always allow". This is enforced server-side, so a modified frontend cannot bypass it. Usability is unaffected: safe operations never prompt, and dangerous-operation prompts offer "allow once" or "allow matching", so approving a class of operation stops repeated prompts.
- The stack is not multi-instance: fixed ports, loopback-only listeners; a port occupied by an unknown process is reported honestly rather than worked around.

## Compatibility

Windows:

| OS | Direct execution | WSL plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 22H2+ | yes | yes (inbox component; mirrored networking available) |
| Windows 10 2004+ | yes | yes (`wsl --install --no-distribution`) |
| Windows 10 1909 and older | yes, degraded | no — explicit "not installable" message |

macOS: 13+ on arm64 (mainline — CI smoke and e2e run here) and 13+ on x64 (package plus lightweight validation); macOS 12 and older unsupported, matching the existing source-mode floor.

Known environmental constraints to handle explicitly:

- Windows path length (260 characters) versus deep Python package trees: guide toward a shallow data directory, keep the environment root shallow, truncate over-long filenames.
- Windows antivirus tools interrupting file writes during install and update, producing incomplete installs; unsigned builds add SmartScreen on top. Document allowlisting and maintain a known-issues library.
- Windows defaulting to GBK on Chinese systems: every script must specify UTF-8 explicitly.
- macOS App Translocation and the quarantine flag before notarization: both are resolved by signing, notarizing, and stapling.
- Missing Apple Silicon builds for a minority of packages: guide users to pip.

## Non-functional budgets

| Metric | Budget | Target |
|---|---|---|
| First run, fresh install to usable main UI | ≤1 min, both platforms | Windows ~30 s on SSD (environment ships in the package, so the cost is unpacking plus stack start); macOS near-instant |
| Packaged stack start | fast | port 4310 healthy within 30 s, both platforms |
| Minor-version update | delta only | Windows blockmap delta; macOS zip delta |
| WSL plugin install | real progress, conservative estimate | rootfs import plus dependency check within a fixed bound once the first release has data |

Memory: on Windows with the WSL plugin active, write `.wslconfig` limits (4 GB / 4 processors, adjustable in the wizard) so `vmmem` cannot take half the host. Direct execution has no `vmmem`. macOS needs no mechanism. The ~200 MB Electron shell is accepted on both.

## Process model

Three kinds of process, managed by one Electron main process:

| Process | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Electron main | Native window and OS integration (Windows: tray and system menu; macOS: application menu, Cmd+Q / Cmd+W); backend lifecycle (probe, start, clean shutdown); injects the access token before page load. |
| Renderer | The existing web UI; on first run it renders the bundled local wizard page first, then the main UI. |
| Backend stack | adapter (Python front door) + API (Node, business logic) + runner (code execution: the routing target on Windows, the sandbox execution point on macOS); memory-graph, evolve, and JiuwenSwarm start on demand. |

Startup: renderer wizard first (it needs no backend) → health probe every 3 s, reusing an already-healthy stack left over from a crash instead of starting a second one → otherwise start the stack → load the UI once the stack is healthy. Request path: page → adapter `:4310` → API `:4410` → runner `:4311`. Shutdown waits for running tasks, then stops only the children this process started; a reused stack is left alone. On Windows the window minimizes to the tray by default and closing it asks for confirmation when tasks are running; on macOS closing the window keeps the application and the backend alive, matching the backend semantics that a run continues after the page is closed.

Updates: checked at startup and every 6 hours; notify, download only on confirmation, never silently upgrade in the background. Installation first waits for running tasks and confirms all child processes have exited.

## Expected new components

- `client/shell/` — the Electron shell (shared; main process branches on platform, preload handles token injection and wizard IPC, `wizard.html` and `fallback.html` are platform-neutral).
- `packages/execution-router/` — the Windows execution-provider routing layer (no macOS counterpart).
- `packages/*/platform/` — per-package platform adapters (win32 and darwin side by side, single entry point, module boundaries enforced), e.g. a secret protector that uses DPAPI on Windows and AES-256-GCM + `0600` on macOS.
- `packages/sandbox-capability/` — extend the existing probe and runtime manifest with macOS entries.
- `scripts/start-stack.mjs` — packaged stack entry point, plus `stack-platform.mjs` for platform differences.
- `build/assemble-backend.mjs`, `build/resources/`, `build/rootfs/` — backend assembly (Windows x64 and per-arch macOS), the extraResources volume, and the trimmed WSL rootfs build (Windows only).
- `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` — add the darwin section.
- `.github/workflows/` — add Windows and `macos-14` (arm64) jobs for packaging (macOS including signing and notarization) and platform regression.

## Delivery milestones

| Milestone | Platform | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Windows | Download page → setup.exe → wizard → complete a small task with SD, never touching WSL. |
| M2 | Windows | On a machine without WSL: one-click sandbox install from the plugin center → run a sandboxed task → uninstall and fall back. |
| M3 | macOS | Source stack plus shell loading 4310 (backend ready, sandbox native — if the shell runs, this works). |
| M4 | macOS | Signed and notarized DMG, double-click to use: fresh Mac → download → drag install → wizard → complete a small task with no Gatekeeper prompt at any point. |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Windows: a fresh machine installs and completes a task without WSL installed.
- [ ] Windows: the sandbox plugin installs in one click, resumes after interruption, and can be uninstalled cleanly.
- [ ] Windows: direct execution cannot be switched to "always allow", and the lock holds when the client is modified.
- [ ] macOS: a signed, notarized DMG opens with no Gatekeeper prompt and no `xattr` workaround.
- [ ] macOS: when Seatbelt is unavailable, startup fails closed with diagnostics instead of running unsandboxed.
- [ ] Both: first run reaches a usable UI within the stated budget on a fresh install.
- [ ] Both: an update lands as a delta, never silently, and never while a task is running.
- [ ] Both: the shell loads the existing `apps/web` build — no forked frontend.
- [ ] Both: quitting leaves no orphaned stack processes, and a reused stack is not stopped.

## Open questions

1. Is an Apple Developer identity available to the project for Developer ID signing and notarization? Public macOS distribution cannot ship without it, and the account lead time is real.
2. Do we start the Azure Trusted Signing application now so the next Windows version can be signed? If the answer is yes, the application has to begin ahead of the release.
3. When do we add a distribution path that is reliable from mainland China? GitHub asset downloads are workable but not dependable, and the update source is fixed once the first public release ships.
4. The shell is expected to live outside the main repository's git history. Is that acceptable to the maintainers, or should it live in-tree?
5. Telemetry is scoped to a minimal, in-app-disableable set with a published collection list (install success rate, first-run completion, Windows provider distribution and plugin install step outcomes, macOS architecture distribution, Seatbelt probe failure rate). Does that list pass review?

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Background

After a long-running tool execution fails, an Agent often has to infer completed work, reusable outputs, and possible continuation points from free-form logs. Execution state and logs alone do not provide a consistent basis for deciding where to continue.

Support recovery of failed long-running tasks: after the failure is addressed and the prerequisites are verified, the Agent can reuse completed results and continue from a supported recovery point, reducing unnecessary recomputation.

A shared, optional recovery metadata contract for tools and task adapters provides the supporting evidence. The LLM uses it to decide the next action; the framework persists and exposes it alongside the existing execution record, reusing existing execution tools and permission checks.

## Requested functionality

- Identify the original execution and expose completed stages or work units, the failed stage, and the failure reason when the task adapter can determine them.
- Reference reusable outputs and available task checkpoints using stable artifact/file/version identifiers where supported. Distinguish verified completed outputs from partial files.
- Explicitly report whether continuation is supported, unsupported, or unknown, including available continuation entry points and required inputs when supported.
- Describe conditions that must be checked before continuation, such as original execution termination, input/configuration changes, environment availability, and output validity.
- Preserve the metadata across refresh/reconnect and make it available through existing execution inspection and Agent tool results. Keep existing tools without recovery metadata compatible.
- Let the Agent inspect the evidence and choose repair, continuation, or a fresh attempt through existing execution tools and permission checks. Metadata itself must not automatically launch a replacement task.

The exact schema should follow the existing execution/tool-result architecture. Framework code should remain independent of specific scientific pipeline stages; task adapters supply domain-specific recovery information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared, documented optional recovery metadata contract is available to long-running tools/task adapters.
- [ ] At least one supported long-running task adapter or representative test fixture demonstrates completed work, failed work, reusable result/checkpoint references, and continuation prerequisites.
- [ ] The Agent can retrieve persisted metadata after reconnecting and use it to identify a supported continuation point without relying solely on free-form logs.
- [ ] Unsupported or unknown recovery capability is explicit; the framework does not invent missing checkpoints or treat file existence alone as proof of completion.
- [ ] A running or unknown original execution is not automatically resubmitted because recovery metadata was returned.
- [ ] Tests cover supported/unsupported/unknown continuation, partial or invalid outputs, changed prerequisites, and persistence/readback.

## Scope and related work

- #398 covers reconnecting to the original NPU task, recovering its state/results, and avoiding duplicate submissions. This issue supplies structured evidence for Agent decisions after a confirmed failure.
- #278 covers in-conversation configuration and task continuation.
- This first version does not include arbitrary Agent-history rollback, restoration of process/NPU memory, or implementing model-specific computational checkpointing. Actual computational continuation depends on task-program support.
- Target release: **v0.3.0, October 30, 2026**, tracked in #249.

---

## 需求背景

长任务执行失败后，Agent 往往需要从自由文本日志中推断哪些工作已经完成、哪些结果可以复用、可以从哪里继续。仅有执行状态和日志，缺少统一的信息契约支撑这些判断。

支持长任务失败后的恢复：处理失败原因并确认接续前提后，Agent 能复用已完成结果，从受支持的恢复点继续，减少不必要的重复计算。

工具和任务适配器提供共享、可选的结构化恢复信息，作为上述能力的支撑。LLM 根据这些证据决定下一步；框架负责随现有执行记录持久化和提供查询，复用已有执行工具与权限检查。

## 期望功能

- 标识原执行；任务适配器能够确定时，返回已完成阶段或工作单元、失败阶段及失败原因。
- 通过受支持的稳定产物／文件／版本标识，引用可复用结果和任务检查点，区分已验证的完整结果与未完成文件。
- 明确返回可续跑、不支持续跑或能力未知；支持时给出可用续跑入口及所需输入。
- 描述接续前需要检查的条件，例如原执行已经结束、输入和配置变化、环境可用性及结果有效性。
- 刷新或重连后仍能通过现有执行查询和 Agent 工具结果获取这些信息；兼容不提供恢复信息的已有工具。
- Agent 根据证据选择修复、接续或重新执行，沿用现有执行工具及权限检查；返回恢复信息本身不自动启动替代任务。

具体字段设计应复用现有执行记录和工具结果架构。框架保持通用，由任务适配器提供具体业务阶段及恢复信息。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 提供有文档说明、可选的统一恢复信息契约，供长任务工具／适配器使用。
- [ ] 至少一个受支持的长任务适配器或有代表性的测试夹具，能够展示已完成工作、失败工作、可复用结果／检查点引用及接续前提。
- [ ] 重连后 Agent 能读取持久化信息，识别受支持的接续点，无须仅依赖自由文本日志推断。
- [ ] 不支持或能力未知时明确返回；框架不虚构检查点，也不把文件存在直接当作步骤已完成。
- [ ] 原执行仍在运行或结果未知时，不会因为返回恢复信息而自动重复提交。
- [ ] 测试覆盖支持／不支持／未知续跑能力、部分或无效结果、前提条件变化及持久化读取。

## 范围与关联

- #398 负责找回原 NPU 任务、恢复状态和结果、避免重复提交；本需求为确认失败后的 Agent 接续决策提供结构化证据。
- #278 负责对话内配置和任务接续。
- 首版不包含任意历史 Agent 状态回滚、进程／NPU 内存恢复，也不代替具体模型实现计算检查点。实际计算续跑依赖任务程序支持。
- 目标版本：**2026 年 10 月 30 日 v0.3.0**，在 #249 跟踪。

items.body:
## Problem

In the artifact / dataset table preview, header cells are left-aligned while body cells use the global `td { text-align: right }` rule. On a wider artifact viewer this mismatch is more visible (noticed while reviewing #428; predates that PR).

## Expected

Column headers and cell values share a consistent alignment (or headers match the numeric/text alignment of their column), so a wide table does not look mis-registered.

## Verification cases

1. **Wide table in artifact viewer**
   - **Preconditions:** A session with an Artifact that renders a multi-column dataset / Markdown table in the artifact viewer; window ≥1280px wide.
   - **Steps:** Open the Artifact; look at any numeric column header vs its cells.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Header alignment matches the column’s cell alignment (no left header over right-aligned numbers for the same column).

2. **Negative — non-table previews unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same session; open a Markdown prose Artifact and a source Artifact.
   - **Steps:** Open each preview.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Prose / source layout is unchanged by any table-alignment fix.

## Context

Refs #428 (noted by author as pre-existing; not in that PR’s scope). Also visible after #309 / large-viewer work.
